transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning, ma'am, and welcome to 'Australia's Moving Experience'! How can I help you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：早上好，女士，欢迎来到“澳大利亚搬家体验”公司！我能为您做些什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I hope you can help me, I'm so up in the air right now... I, I...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：嗯，希望您能帮我，我现在真是心乱如麻……我……我……

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Just calm down, now. Let me guess: you're moving and it has you a little confused.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：请先冷静一下。让我猜猜：您要搬家了，这让您有点不知所措。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's it exactly. You see, I'm relocating to the United States next month and I'm having a hard time getting organized.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：正是这样。您看，我下个月要搬到美国去，但实在不知道怎么整理东西。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Here, fill out your name and address, and let me ask you a few questions. Oh, what should I call you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：来，请填写您的姓名和地址，我再问您几个问题。哦，我怎么称呼您？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: My name is Jane, Jane Bond.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：我叫简，简·邦德。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, Jane, first of all, what's your work phone? In case I have any questions about things.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：好的，简，首先，您的办公电话是多少？万一我有什么问题需要联系您。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: My work phone is 94635550. But please try not to call me too often there. My boss hates personal calls.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：办公电话是94635550。但请尽量别打太多次。我老板不喜欢私人电话。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: So does mine, ma'am, so does mine. And what address should we ship your things to?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：我老板也一样，女士，完全一样。那么，我们把您的东西寄到哪个地址？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: My new company is letting me stay temporarily at 509 Clark House, that's C-L-A-R-K, 1137 University Drive in Seattle.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：我的新公司让我暂时住在509号克拉克公寓，拼写是C-L-A-R-K，地址是西雅图大学路1137号。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Seattle? Beautiful city, I hear. Mountains right beside the ocean, almost. Cooler than Australia too. OK, and when should we come pack your things?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：西雅图？听说是个美丽的城市。山就在海边附近，几乎挨着。也比澳大利亚凉爽。好的，那我们什么时候来打包您的东西？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: I guess that would be on Monday, March 11th.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：我想应该是3月11日，星期一。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Do you want any help with an after-packing clean-up? We do that for a small additional charge.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：打包之后需要帮忙打扫吗？我们可以额外收费提供这项服务。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, that would be helpful. I promised the landlord I'd give her the keys back by 5:00 p.m. on Thursday, the 14th.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：好的，那会有帮助。我答应房东在14号星期四下午5点前把钥匙还给她。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great, we'll just schedule the clean-up for that day. That way, the place will smell clean and there'll be no dust.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：太好了，我们就把清洁安排在当天。这样房子会闻起来干净，也没有灰尘。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, you do think of everything! Oh, how much is this going to cost?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：嗯，您考虑得真周到！哦，这要花多少钱？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Here is a list of our basic prices.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：这是我们的基本价格清单。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh dear, this seems rather expensive!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：哎呀，看起来相当贵啊！

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes ma'am, but you're paying for the best. We're careful and we're fast. Like we say, the only thing we break are speed records getting you moved.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：是的，女士，但您付的是最好的服务。我们细心又快速。就像我们说的，我们唯一打破的就是帮您搬家时的速度纪录。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well...maybe that's so...Oh, I nearly forgot to tell you. I don't want my furniture shipped with me. I won't be looking for an apartment till after I arrive in America. Would it be possible to put my furniture in storage here for a month, then have it sent along later?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：好吧……也许是这样……哦，我差点忘了告诉您。我不想把我的家具和我一起运走。我要到了美国之后才找公寓。能不能把我的家具在这里存放一个月，然后再寄过去？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course, we do that all the time. A couple of other things. Here at "A Moving Experience', we try to pack your things logically. We don't just throw stuff in boxes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：当然可以，我们经常这样做。还有几件事。在“搬家体验”公司，我们会尽量合乎逻辑地打包您的物品，而不是随便把东西塞进箱子里。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Do you have any special requests? You know, things you want packed in some special place, so you know where to find them?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：您有什么特别要求吗？比如，您希望某些东西放在特别的位置，以便您知道去哪里找？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Like what?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：比如什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, I don't know...Things like dishes maybe. Not to be rude, but you look like a lady who likes to eat.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：哦，我也不太确定……比如餐具吧。无意冒犯，但您看起来像一位喜欢美食的女士。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Ahhh! Yes, I need my dishes and things where I can find them quickly.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：啊！是的，我需要我的餐具之类的东西能很快找到。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great. We'll put those dishes and cutlery in what we call the emergency pack. Can you think of anything else?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：好的。我们会把这些餐具和刀叉放在我们称之为“应急包”的箱子里。您还能想到别的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Ummm, I do have an antique tea kettle my great-grandmother gave my mother. I wouldn't want to lose that. So I guess you'd better put that in storage with the furniture.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：嗯，我有一个古董茶壶，是我曾祖母给我母亲的。我不想弄丢它。所以我想最好把它和家具一起存放。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Grandma's tea kettle with the furniture, got it! Say, how about things like your alarm clock? You don't want to miss your plane on the big day, right?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：祖母的茶壶和家具一起放，记下了！那您的闹钟之类的呢？您可不想在出发那天错过飞机，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, you certainly think of everything! Yes, that's right. I'll also need my alarm clock where I can find it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：嗯，您想得真是周到！是的，没错。我还需要闹钟，要放在我能找到的地方。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Fine, we'll put that in your personal package. And of course, we'll give you a list of where we pack everything. So, all you'll have to do on Thursday the 14th. is grab your luggage on your way out the door. Um, I couldn't help noticing the new CD player you're carrying. Is that a Samsung?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：好的，我们会把它放在您的个人物品包里。当然，我们会给您一份清单，标明每样东西打包在哪里。这样，您在14号星期四那天要做的只是出门时带上您的行李。嗯，我忍不住注意到您拿着的新CD播放机。是三星的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Why yes, it is. One of their best. Cost me nearly a hundred dollars, it did!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：是的，确实是。是他们最好的型号之一。花了我将近一百美元呢！

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Do you want to take special care of it? I mean it's brand new.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：您想特别小心保管它吗？毕竟它是全新的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Take care of it, but nothing special. You can just put it in storage with the furniture.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：小心保管就行，但不必特别处理。把它和家具一起存放就好。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CLERK
transcriptSentences.englishText: That looks like everything we need here. I guess you're all set.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 职员：看来我们需要的信息都齐了。我想您都准备好了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: That was certainly quick. Thank you, young man. This has been a most moving experience!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：这确实很快。谢谢您，年轻人。这真是一次“搬家的体验”！

transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning everyone and welcome to the 2nd. Annual Wullaballoo Conference on Mastering Computer Languages. I hope you all had a good trip. Before we get underway with today's programme, let me fill you in as to what's on tap for tomorrow, Sunday, February 19th.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 大家早上好，欢迎参加第二届年度“掌握计算机语言”Wullaballoo大会。希望各位旅途顺利。在我们开始今天的日程之前，我来跟大家说明一下明天（2月19日，星期日）的安排。

transcriptSentences.speaker: At 9
transcriptSentences.englishText: 00 a.m. right here in the Main Hall we'll be hearing a lecture from Dr. John Smith about "Computer as Teacher." Professor Smith, from the University of Melbourne, is a world-class expert in the field of computer-assisted education, and his talk promises to be both stimulating and informative.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 上午9点整，就在这个主厅，我们将聆听约翰·史密斯博士关于“计算机作为教师”的讲座。史密斯教授来自墨尔本大学，是计算机辅助教育领域的世界级专家，他的演讲预计将既发人深省又内容丰富。

transcriptSentences.englishText: Immediately afterwards, at 10:30, there will be a presentation of papers by various delegates. That, however, will take place in the Garden Room on the ground floor. If you don't yet know, the Garden Room is also called the Ballroom, and we'll be gathering at the west end, the slightly raised area called Level 2. Just look for the crowd. If you get lost, there are signs in the foyer.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 紧接着，在10点半，将由各位代表进行论文展示。不过，那将在底层的花园厅举行。如果你们还不知道，花园厅也叫舞厅，我们将在西端稍微高起的那块区域（称为2层）集合。跟着人群走就行。如果迷路了，门厅里有指示牌。

transcriptSentences.englishText: After all that thinking, talking, and listening, I expect everyone will be a bit weary. So at 11:15, there will be a break for coffee, cookies, and other light refreshments. These will be available at the aptly named Refreshment Stand, placed by the door back here in the Main Hall. Also, if you choose to skip the formal lunch, you can buy a packed lunch at the stand for a reasonable price.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 在这么多思考、讨论和聆听之后，我想大家都会有点疲惫。所以在11点15分，会有一次茶歇，供应咖啡、饼干和其他点心。这些将在门口那间名副其实的“茶点台”提供，就在主厅的门口。另外，如果您选择不参加正式午餐，也可以在茶点台购买盒装午餐，价格合理。

transcriptSentences.englishText: I strongly urge you, however, to join us at the formal lunch. That won't be till one o'clock sharp, so you have time to stroll about town a bit. We'll be eating at the Sea View Restaurant. The restaurant is located right here in the hotel, on the top floor. It's a good dozen flights of stairs, so I suggest you take the lift on the ground floor, eh? If you're not fond of fish, there is an all-you-can-eat barbecue available as well. They even offer wallaby meat!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 不过，我强烈建议您参加正式午餐。那要到下午1点整才开始，所以您有时间在镇上逛逛。我们将在一家名为“海景”的餐厅用餐。餐厅就在这家酒店的顶层。有十几层楼梯，所以我建议您坐一楼的电梯，怎么样？如果您不喜欢鱼，还有不限量的烧烤可供选择。他们甚至提供袋鼠肉！

transcriptSentences.englishText: After lunch, we'll troop back downstairs to Level 2 in the Ballroom for the presentation of further papers, which will begin at 2:00 p.m. Please try to be on time. I know you'll be a bit tired after lunch, but the Ballroom echoes so with people coming in late. Thank you in advance.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 午餐后，我们将回到舞厅2层，继续听取更多论文展示，将于下午2点开始。请尽量准时。我知道午餐后大家会有点困，但舞厅回音很大，所以迟到的人进来会打扰到大家。提前感谢配合。

transcriptSentences.englishText: Once we've heard the papers, we'll break for afternoon tea at 3:10 p.m. No need to walk. The manager of the refreshment stand has graciously agreed to have tea served in the Ballroom. He's even promised us some special scones, baked from a recipe of his dear old Scottish grandmother.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 听完论文展示后，我们在下午3点10分休息，享用下午茶。不用走路，茶点台的经理已经慷慨地同意在舞厅内提供茶点。他甚至答应给我们做一些特别的烤饼，用的是他亲爱的苏格兰老奶奶的食谱。

transcriptSentences.englishText: Then, tea being drunk and scones munched, we'll retire here to the Main Hall for some closing remarks and questions. So, by 5:00 we should have the conference wrapped up. But the fun isn't over! This is Australia mates! We'll be flocking to the hotel's own Palm Lounge on the east side of the foyer for an informal reception. You can relax, mingle with the other delegates, and let your hair down a bit. This will run from 5:10 to 6:10, though you're free to stay as long as you like. The lounge manager has informed me that, for the duration of the actual reception, you can have all-you-can-drink beer for $20.00 with purchase of an advance ticket.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 喝完茶，吃完烤饼，我们将回到主厅进行闭幕致辞和提问。这样，到5点会议应该就能结束了。但欢乐还没结束！这里是澳大利亚，伙计们！我们将涌向酒店门厅东侧的棕榈酒廊，参加一个非正式招待会。您可以放松身心，与其他代表交流，尽情放松一下。招待会从5点10分到6点10分，不过您想待多久都行。酒廊经理告诉我，在招待会期间，凭预售票只需20美元就可以无限畅饮啤酒。

transcriptSentences.englishText: And, yes, tickets can be purchased from any conference organizer or at the front desk anytime between now and the start of the reception. I suggest you come by tomorrow evening to pick up the tickets since the conference hall only holds 800 people. That way you can also get your journey planned ahead of time and be sure not to miss this truly memorable conference. If you want cocktails, however, I'm sorry. You'll have to pay for those at the regular price.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 是的，门票可以向任何会议组织者购买，或者在招待会开始前在接待处购买。我建议您明天晚上来取票，因为会议厅只能容纳800人。这样您也可以提前规划好行程，确保不会错过这次真正难忘的会议。不过，如果您想喝鸡尾酒，很抱歉，您需要按正常价格购买。

transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh my goodness! Speaking of paying, I see I forgot to tell you a couple of things. The first is about lunch. The charge for the lunch will be $15.00 for all you delegates. If you have guests with you, the cost is $25 for the general public, and $6.50 for children under the age of 10. That's fifteen dollars each, not total for everyone! Another item is about the lunch menu. I very much urge you to try the fish. I mean, look at the restaurant's name: Sea View. As the name suggests, it is a famous seafood restaurant. The chef is a Basque from Spain and he really gets quite put out when people ignore his fish specialties for burgers or barbecue. If fish isn't your thing though, try the steak - he makes an exquisite Filet mignon topped with bleu cheese and mushrooms.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 天哪！说到付款，我发现自己忘了告诉你们几件事。首先是午餐。各位代表的午餐费用是15美元。如果您带客人来，普通公众是25美元，10岁以下儿童是6.5美元。这是每人15美元，不是所有人的总和！另一件事是午餐菜单。我非常推荐您尝试鱼类菜肴。我的意思是，看看餐厅的名字：海景。顾名思义，这是一家著名的海鲜餐厅。厨师是来自西班牙的巴斯克人，如果人们不点他的鱼类特色菜而点汉堡或烧烤，他会很不高兴。如果您不喜欢鱼，那就试试牛排——他做的菲力牛排配蓝纹奶酪和蘑菇非常精致。

transcriptSentences.englishText: Finally, if you'd like to buy a ticket, you can have both lunch and the unlimited beer for $35.00. I should have mentioned that earlier, but I am a bit forgetful. Maybe I should avoid the beer after the conference, eh?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 最后，如果您想买票，可以花35美元同时享受午餐和无限畅饮啤酒。我本来应该早点说的，但我有点健忘。也许会后我应该避免喝啤酒，嗯？

transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I've said my bit. Are there any questions?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 好了，我要说的就这些。有什么问题吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello...are you Professor Van Diezen?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 您好……您是范·迪森教授吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, I am. And who might you be?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 是的，我就是。你是哪位？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh! Sorry, my name is Tina. I'm a freshman here. They told me I should ask you for advice in choosing courses.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 哦！抱歉，我叫蒂娜。我是这里的大一新生。他们告诉我应该向您请教选课的事。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, that's part of what I'm here for. Please come in and sit down. Now, what are your questions?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 嗯，这就是我工作的一部分。请进来坐下。那么，你有什么问题？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: I, I almost don't know! Everything is so confusing! Like what is a 'specialized course'?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 我……我几乎不知道从何问起！一切都太乱了！比如什么是“专业课程”？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, easy. A specialized course is one that is compulsory, meaning it's a requirement for your major and regular so you can't place out by taking a proficiency exam.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 哦，这个简单。专业课程就是必修课，意思是它是你专业的必需课程，而且是常规课程，你不能通过参加水平考试来免修。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds pretty strict. Then what are all these general courses? I seem to have to take so many.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 听起来很严格。那这些通识课程又是什么？我好像要修很多门。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Nothing to be alarmed over. These are courses open to all students and not directly related to your major. The university offers these general courses to choose so that you can become more well-rounded individuals. For example, I see you're a Microbiology major. So it might be a good idea to take some literature or history courses so that you can know something besides all science.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 不用大惊小怪。这些课程面向所有学生，与你的专业没有直接关系。大学提供这些通识课程供你选择，是为了让你成为更全面发展的人。比如说，我看到你的专业是微生物学。那么选修一些文学或历史课程可能会是个好主意，这样你除了科学之外还能了解些别的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: You mean these courses are, like, for fun?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 您的意思是，这些课程就像……为了好玩？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: That might be one way to look at it, but don't tell the literature professor such a thing. Think of a general course as the opposite of a specified course. A specified course is one that pertains directly to your major.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 你可以这么理解，但可别跟文学教授这么说。你把通识课程看作专业指定课程的反面就行了。指定课程就是直接与你的专业相关的课程。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: So can I take any Microbiology course I want?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 那么我可以选任何我想要的微生物学课程吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Let's see. Oh, those courses used to be open to Microbiology students only. The good thing is, now it's open to students on a flexible schedule, so it's not only for full-time students. So the answer is yes, if you have the instructor's permission. May I ask you why you chose Microbiology?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 让我看看。哦，那些课程以前只对微生物学专业的学生开放。好消息是，现在也对非全日制学习的学生开放了，所以不限于全日制学生。所以答案是肯定的，只要你有任课老师的许可。我能问一下你为什么选择微生物学吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I also like plain old Biology too. You know, full-sized animals. I might even become a veterinarian. Could I take some Biology classes?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 嗯，我也喜欢普通的生物学。就是那种大型动物。我甚至可能成为一名兽医。我能选一些生物学的课吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, they are open to full-time students only, which I believe is what you are. I don't know how a freshman would get along with Microbiology, though. I mean, most of the students presently looking into it are from off-campus.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 嗯，这些课程只对全日制学生开放，我相信你属于这类。不过，我不知道一个大一新生学微生物学会怎么样。我的意思是，目前选修这门课的大部分学生都是校外人员。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Off campus?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 校外人员？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, you know, people who use it in their work at hospitals, laboratories, even a police detective. Why did you choose Microbiology, if I may ask? I don't think you quite answered that.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 是的，就是在医院、实验室工作的人，甚至还有警探。恕我冒昧，你为什么选择微生物学？我觉得你还没完全回答这个问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well eventually I want to be a doctor. At least my dad tells me so.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 嗯，最终我想当医生。至少我爸爸是这么跟我说的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: If I may say so, young lady, you seem a little uncertain. Still, I think that might be a good idea for a career. Of course, if you're thinking about being either a doctor or a vet, you should take some Medical Science classes before you even think of applying to med school.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 恕我直言，小姑娘，你似乎有点不太确定。不过，我仍然认为这或许是个不错的职业选择。当然，如果你想当医生或兽医，在考虑申请医学院之前，你应该先修一些医学科学的课程。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great! What should I take?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 太好了！我该选什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: There is one small problem. The new Medical Sciences building is under construction, so there are no experimental facilities available until next year. I'm afraid you'll have to wait. But don't forget to take those courses at the first opportunity!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 有一个小问题。新的医学科学大楼正在建设中，所以明年之前都没有实验设施可用。恐怕你得等一等了。但别忘了，一旦有机会就立刻去选那些课程！

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, bummer. Is there any other course you'd recommend for someone like me?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 哦，真扫兴。您还有什么其他课程推荐给我这样的人吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, since you seem to like animals, have you ever thought about looking into Environmental Science?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 嗯，既然你似乎喜欢动物，你有没有考虑过了解一下环境科学？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: No, I never really thought about it before. Is it worthwhile?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 没有，我以前从没真正想过。这门课值得学吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Quite! In fact it's the fastest growing subject on this campus.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 非常值得！事实上，它是这个校园里发展最快的学科。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm sorry, I couldn't help noticing the long list of classes you've written out there. May I have a look?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 抱歉，我忍不住注意到你写的那一长串课程。我能看看吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, sure.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 哦，当然可以。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Medical Science, Statistics, Laboratory Techniques, Medicine, Mathematics, Computing. My, my, a bit of everything here.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 医学科学、统计学、实验室技术、医学、数学、计算机。哎呀呀，真是应有尽有。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Is it too much?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 是不是太多了？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: For your first semester, yes. What I suggest is starting out by taking the compulsory courses. Like we said before, the Medical Science can wait. Consider taking that in your sophomore year. I think I'd put off Computing too. I recommend to all freshmen that I talk to to get the compulsory Mathematics out of the way as early as possible, so take that one. It'll be one less difficult course you have to focus on when the science lab opens next year and you have to catch upon classes like Laboratory Techniques. Your major also requires Statistics so you have to balance two math classes, and no doubt you should take that. Otherwise, get your required Medicine course out of the way by taking something theory based. Oh, of course and your Environmental Science class if you're interested. The others can wait, though I think Computing is definitely a good idea, even though it's not required. I see too, on your paper there, you seem to have had high marks on the entrance exam.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 对于你的第一学期来说，是的。我的建议是从必修课开始。就像我们之前说的，医学科学可以等等。考虑在大二再选。我想我也会推迟计算机。我向我交谈过的所有新生建议，尽早把必修的数学修完，所以选数学吧。这样明年科学实验室开放、你需要补上实验室技术等课程时，就能少一门需要集中精力的难课。你的专业也要求统计学，所以你得平衡两门数学课，这门无疑应该选。另外，通过选一些理论基础的课程来把必需的医学课先修完。哦，当然，如果你感兴趣，还有环境科学课。其他的可以等等，不过我认为计算机绝对是个好主意，即使它不是必修的。我也看到，在你的纸上，你似乎在入学考试中得了高分。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Uhhh, yeah. I guess so.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 呃……是的，我想是吧。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Don't be shy! Have you thought about applying for a scholarship?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 别害羞！你有没有考虑过申请奖学金？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Do they have any? I mean, my dad is always complaining about how much money it costs him.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 有奖学金吗？我是说，我爸爸总是抱怨他花了多少钱。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: In your department there are actually three full scholarships available. They cover tuition and provide $1,500 cash.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 在你们系里，实际上有三个全额奖学金名额。它们涵盖学费，并提供1500美元现金。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: $1,500 cash?! PARTY!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 1500美元现金？！开派对啦！

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Please, Miss. The money is intended more as a textbook allowance, not party money. If you promise to behave, I'll show you how to apply.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **教授:** 拜托了，小姐。这笔钱更多是作为课本津贴，不是派对资金。如果你保证会规矩点，我就教你怎么申请。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great, and thanks!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: **学生:** 太好了，谢谢您！

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: We've been talking about choosing building materials in the last week. Now, a great many factors influence the choice of building materials. You can't make a house of cards, right? And "people who live in glass houses..." and all that...anyhow, today I'd like to say a few words about flooring.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：上周我们一直在讨论选择建筑材料。现在，有非常多的因素影响建筑材料的选择。你不能用扑克牌搭房子，对吧？还有“住在玻璃房子里的人……”等等……总之，今天我想谈谈地板。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Some artificial materials can be used, like plastic for instance, which offer mixed blessings when used as a flooring surface. On the one hand, plastic is cheaper than nearly any other alternative, short of bare ground. Plastic also does not warp like wood. On the other hand, the best that can be said about plastic is that it "looks like" wood or stone. However, it cannot replace the real materials. As I have mentioned, I'm fixing up a new house. The decorator my wife hired told me, "Plastic does a great job of looking exactly like plastic." Besides, it scratches easily, fades or discolors, and starts cracking within a year or two. So, if you're fitting out a sleazy hotel or plan to live in a trailer park, go with the plastic. Really, though, for all intents and purposes, this leaves us with wood or stone as choices for flooring.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：可以使用一些人造材料，比如塑料，用作地板材料有利有弊。一方面，塑料比几乎任何其他选择都便宜，除了裸露的土地。塑料也不会像木头那样翘曲。另一方面，关于塑料最好的评价也就是它“看起来像”木头或石头。然而，它无法替代真正的材料。正如我提到的，我正在装修新房子。我妻子雇的装饰设计师告诉我：“塑料最好的地方就是看起来完全像塑料。”此外，它容易刮花、褪色或变色，并在一两年内开始开裂。所以，如果你要装修一家廉价旅馆或打算住在拖车公园，那就用塑料吧。不过，实际上，权衡下来，我们只能选择木材或石材作为地板材料。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Stone and wood are alike in at least one respect: both go through processing before they can be put to use. Since few of us cut our own lumber or quarry our own stone, this is not perhaps a pressing concern. Still, do-it-yourselfers would do well to remember to buy only properly seasoned wood. Unseasoned wood warps and a warped floor quickly becomes firewood (and its owner quickly becomes poorer). Likewise, except for dull-hued materials like slate or sandstone, most stone floors are polished before installation. The choice goes well beyond just wood or stone - each type requires many further considerations. A few special remarks are called for when considering woods, for example. As always, aesthetics, personal taste, and layout all play roles as well as the type of house or room. Oh, and certainly don't forget the cost. When it comes to cost, a rule of thumb is that the softer and less exotic the wood, the lower the cost. In the U.S., for instance, pine is both ubiquitous and cheap. Mahogany is imported and exorbitantly expensive. If you're on any kind of budget when remodeling, it's really helpful to remember to go for the softer woods.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：石材和木材至少在一个方面是相似的：两者都需要经过加工才能使用。因为我们中很少有人自己砍伐木材或开采石材，所以这也许不是一个紧迫的问题。不过，自己动手装修的人最好记住，只购买经过适当干燥处理的木材。未经干燥的木材会翘曲，而翘曲的地板很快就会变成柴火（它的主人也会很快变穷）。同样，除了板岩或砂岩等颜色暗淡的材料外，大多数石材地板在安装前都要经过抛光。选择远不止木材或石材——每种类型都需要许多进一步的考量。例如，在考虑木材时，需要特别提及几点。一如既往，美学、个人品味和布局，以及房屋或房间的类型，都起作用。哦，当然别忘了成本。说到成本，一个经验法则是，木材越软、越不稀有，成本就越低。例如，在美国，松木既普遍又便宜。桃花心木是进口的，价格极其昂贵。如果你在翻新时有预算限制，记住选择较软的木材会很有帮助。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Aside from cost, there are still lots of different factors that are important in choosing the best flooring for the job. Continuing with the example of wood, one must consider the effects of each type of wood on the mood of the room. When selecting the best wood to use, particular attention needs to be paid to its grain patterns, texture, and color. In rooms where relaxation or deep thought is the aim--say bedrooms or the study--dark, strong grained woods are the rule. Here the grain ought to match the furniture for a feeling of homogeneity. In rooms where activity and motion are typical--the dining room or living room--lighter, finer-grained lumber is more suitable. In such a setting, the wood grain might be useful in offering a contrast to the furniture. This leads to a feel of subconscious excitement, in keeping with the room's function.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：除了成本之外，在选择最适合的地板时还有许多不同的因素。继续以木材为例，必须考虑每种木材对房间氛围的影响。当选择最佳木材时，要特别注意其纹理图案、质地和颜色。在以放松或沉思为目的的房间——比如卧室或书房——深色、纹理强烈的木材是常规选择。这里的纹理应该与家具相匹配，以营造统一感。在以活动和动感为典型的房间——餐厅或客厅——较浅色、纹理更细腻的木材更合适。在这样的环境中，木纹可以用来与家具形成对比。这会产生一种潜意识的兴奋感，与房间的功能相契合。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: In either case, though, consult a decorator. It is a decorator's job to know what materials to use to fit the function of the room. Though some things about putting together a room are subjective and based on one's individual taste, materials appropriate to a room's function are much more straightforward. A decorator takes the needs of the customer and uses a mathematical formula, rather than subjective words. Since feelings vary from person to person, verbal descriptions of wood types tend to be ambiguous. You may want the wood you select, but not something approximate! And if you do decide to do it yourself, remember that all woods must be treated with preservatives to enhance their appearance and preserve their natural beauty.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：不过，无论哪种情况，都要咨询装饰设计师。装饰设计师的工作就是知道用什么材料来适应房间的功能。虽然布置房间的某些方面是主观的，基于个人品味，但适合房间功能的材料则更加明确。装饰设计师会根据客户的需求，使用数学公式，而不是主观的词语。因为感受因人而异，关于木材类型的口头描述往往含糊不清。你可能想要你选择的木材，而不是某种近似品！如果你决定自己动手，记住所有木材都必须用防腐剂处理，以增强其外观并保持其自然美感。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: In the case of stone, or "quarry tile" as flat-cut flooring stone is properly called, a new set of considerations must be weighed. Simple color aside, the degree of reflection must be kept in mind. This is called the "reflectance rate", which is expressed in a number between 0.0 and 1.0, depending on the amount of light it reflects.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：对于石材，或者更准确地称为“采石场瓷砖”（指平切地板石材），需要权衡一系列新的考虑因素。除了简单的颜色之外，还必须记住反射程度。这被称为“反射率”，用0.0到1.0之间的数字表示，具体取决于其反射的光量。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: At one end of the scale is polished silver. At a rating of 1.0, this shiny surface reflects nearly all of the light directed at it. Numbers closer to zero describe materials that absorb more light. Moving down the scale a bit, we see that plastic that has been painted white has a rate of 0.8, which makes sense. We know that the color white reflects all other color while black absorbs all color, and plastic itself is a relatively reflective material.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：刻度的一端是抛光银。在1.0的评级下，这种闪亮的表面几乎反射所有照射到它的光线。接近零的数字表示吸收更多光的材料。稍微往下移，我们看到涂成白色的塑料的反射率是0.8，这很合理。我们知道白色反射所有其他颜色，而黑色吸收所有颜色，塑料本身是一种相对反射的材料。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Materials that are denser and darker have reflectance rates much closer to zero. The quarry tile I mentioned a while ago has a rate of 0.1. As you may know, quarry tile is generally dark brown and made from clay so it is quite dense. Of course, there is considerable variation among types of quarry tile because of the hue or treatment of the clay during its creation.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：更密实、更暗的材料反射率更接近零。我刚才提到的采石场瓷砖的反射率是0.1。你可能知道，采石场瓷砖通常是深棕色的，由粘土制成，所以非常密实。当然，由于制造过程中粘土的色调或处理方式不同，采石场瓷砖的类型之间存在相当大的差异。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Does anyone have guesses as to what materials may have a rate of almost 0.0? We can guess most of these materials are black in color, but plastic, wood, and even stone reflect some light. One material with a rate of almost 0.0 is black velvet. The texture produces almost no shine at all.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：有人能猜一下什么材料的反射率可能接近0.0吗？我们可以猜测这些材料大多是黑色的，但塑料、木材甚至石材都会反射一些光。一种反射率几乎为0.0的材料是黑色天鹅绒。其质地几乎不产生任何光泽。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Carrera marble, despite its white hue, is actually lower in reflectivity than black onyx! In any case, the fact that tiles vary somewhat should not be forgotten. A highly reflective floor would not be suitable in a library; it would be indispensible in a ballroom (should your home be large enough to feature one). Again, a rule of thumb is that "light means lively." Since form (and material) follows function, one should only use the more reflective materials in rooms where the cultivation and expression of energy is important. Bear in mind too that most types of stone cost more than all but the rarest of woods.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：卡拉拉大理石，尽管是白色调，实际上反射率比黑色缟玛瑙还要低！无论如何，不应忘记瓷砖有差异。高反射率的地板不适合图书馆；但在舞厅里却是不可或缺的（如果你的家足够大，能有一个舞厅的话）。再次强调，一条经验法则是“明亮意味着活泼”。既然形式（和材料）服从功能，那么只有在培养和表达活力重要的房间里，才应该使用反射性更强的材料。还要记住，大多数石材的价格比除最稀有木材之外的所有木材都贵。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course, there is no reason why some rooms of a house should not feature wood floors or other stone tiles. You can even mix the two. A room with wood panels on the walls can have a beautiful stone floor. My bedroom has white birch walls and a light blue slate floor. The place looks like a Russian hunting lodge. Remember, though, go with what feels right to you. Good taste and the "laws" of interior design are the home-owner's servants, not his master. It's only beautiful when you decide it is. I mean, you're the one who lives there, not the decorator, right? OK, are there any questions?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：当然，房子里有些房间用木地板或其他石材地砖，没有任何不妥。你甚至可以混合使用两者。墙上有木板的房间可以配漂亮的石地板。我的卧室有白桦木墙壁和浅蓝色板岩地板。那个地方看起来像俄罗斯的狩猎小屋。不过，记住，要选择你觉得合适的。良好的品味和室内设计的“法则”是房主的仆人，而不是主人。只有当你认为它美的时候，它才美。我的意思是，住在那里的是你，而不是装饰设计师，对吧？好的，有问题吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning. I've been looking at your holidays to Australia in your brochure. I'm thinking about going during the second half of next month.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：早上好。我一直在看你们宣传册里关于澳大利亚度假的内容。我在考虑下个月后半段去。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning. As you can see from our brochure, we offer a wide variety of packages to various destinations in Australia. Is there anything in particular that interests you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：早上好。正如您从宣传册中看到的，我们提供前往澳大利亚不同目的地的多种套餐。您有什么特别感兴趣的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, my husband and I are very interested in the holidays in the Outback.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：是的，我丈夫和我对内陆地区的度假非常感兴趣。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: These holidays are becoming increasingly popular. Would you like to arrange flights and accommodation with us, or just accommodation?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：这些度假方式正变得越来越受欢迎。您想在我们这里安排航班和住宿，还是只安排住宿？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Can you arrange flights from Sydney?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：你们能安排从悉尼出发的航班吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Certainly.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：当然可以。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, flights and accommodation then.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：好的，那就航班和住宿都安排。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right. You said that you wanted to travel next month. Which date would you prefer? I should point out that there are no flights available every day, so if you have a flexible itinerary, that's better.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：好的。您说您想下个月出行。您更倾向哪个日期？我应该指出，不是每天都有航班，所以如果您的行程灵活，那会更好。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, we arrive in Sydney on 15th April and we were thinking of travelling to the Outback on 18th August, er... I mean April.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：嗯，我们4月15日到达悉尼，我们原计划8月18日去内陆，呃……我是说4月。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK. There's only one flight from Sydney to Alice Springs on 18th, so I'll book you on that. It leaves at 10 in the morning, which is quite convenient. Shall I book two seats for you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：好的。18日只有一班从悉尼到爱丽丝泉的航班，所以我为您预订那一班。它早上10点起飞，相当方便。我为您预订两个座位吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, please.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：好的，请预订。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: As for your stay in the Outback, you can see from the brochure that we offer three packages - budget, standard and luxury. The budget package is about 500 Australian dollars. The standard package is about 700 and the luxury one is approximately 1,000, though it does depend on exactly what you would like regarding extras. Which one would you prefer?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：关于您在内陆的住宿，您可以从宣传册中看到，我们提供三种套餐——经济型、标准型和豪华型。经济型套餐大约500澳元。标准型大约700澳元，豪华型大约1000澳元，不过具体取决于您对附加项目的需求。您更喜欢哪一种？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, we can't decide between the budget and standard options.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：嗯，我们在经济型和标准型之间拿不定主意。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Ah, well, actually, just looking at my computer here, on the date that you want to fly into Alice Springs, there is no standard accommodation available. It's fully booked, I'm afraid.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：啊，实际上，我刚看了电脑，在您想飞往爱丽丝泉的那个日期，没有标准型住宿可用。恐怕已经订满了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's OK. We think that the cheapest one should be fine for us. We don't mind roughing it for a few days and we don't expect to be spending much time at the accommodation. We prefer the outdoors.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：没关系。我们认为最便宜的应该适合我们。我们不介意凑合几天，而且我们也不打算在住宿上花太多时间。我们更喜欢户外。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right. Let's look at the room options.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：好的。我们来看看房间选项。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: First of all, would you prefer a non-smoking room?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：首先，您更喜欢无烟房吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes. Neither of us smokes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：是的。我们俩都不抽烟。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：好的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, before I forget, could you book everything in my husband's name, please?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：哦，趁我还没忘，您能用我丈夫的名字预订所有东西吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, of course. Are you paying by credit card?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：好的，当然。您用信用卡支付吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：是的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: In that case, I'll need your husband's name exactly as it appears on the card.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：那样的话，我需要您丈夫的姓名，要跟信用卡上显示的一模一样。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course. It's John A. Smyth. That's Smyth with a 'Y'.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：当然。是John A. Smyth。Smyth带一个‘Y’。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: John... middle initial 'A'... surname Smyth - S-M-Y-T-H. Is that correct?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：John……中间名首字母‘A’……姓Smyth——S-M-Y-T-H。对吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Correct.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：对。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Thank you. I'll just check the price. The room will cost 100 dollars a night plus 10 dollars tax, so 110 dollars per night in total. Is that OK?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：谢谢。我查一下价格。房间每晚100美元加10美元税，所以总共每晚110美元。可以吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, that's fine. Book us for three nights, please.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：可以，没问题。请为我们预订三晚。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Most of the guests like to participate in some special activities and trips while they are staying in the Outback. Is there anything that interests you and your husband?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：大多数客人在内陆逗留期间喜欢参加一些特别的活动和旅行。您和您先生有什么感兴趣的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, there are several things we'd like to see and do. We'd definitely like to visit the Cultural Centre.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：有的，有好几件事我们想看想做。我们肯定想去参观文化中心。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, that's very popular. It's within walking distance of the accommodation and it's free. It's also a great place to pick up souvenirs of your trip.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：是的，那里非常受欢迎。从住宿处步行即可到达，而且是免费的。也是购买旅行纪念品的好地方。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: We were thinking about visiting one of the nearby farms.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：我们考虑去参观附近的一个农场。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: There are two farms nearby - a sheep farm and a kangaroo farm. There is also an opportunity to ride camels in the desert. Have you ridden a camel before?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：附近有两个农场——一个绵羊农场和一个袋鼠农场。还有机会在沙漠里骑骆驼。您以前骑过骆驼吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: No, but it sounds like fun. Could you give me some more details about the kangaroo farm and the camel ride?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：没有，但听起来很有趣。您能给我更多关于袋鼠农场和骑骆驼的细节吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Certainly. The kangaroo farm includes information on how the animals are raised whilst the camel ride provides information on desert flora and fauna. Which would you prefer? You can arrange to see the kangaroos in the wild if you like, rather than on a farm.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：当然。袋鼠农场包括关于动物如何饲养的信息，而骑骆驼则提供关于沙漠动植物的信息。您更喜欢哪个？如果您愿意，可以安排在野外看袋鼠，而不是在农场。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds perfect. OK, we'll go on the camel ride and see the kangaroos in their natural habitat.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：听起来很完美。好的，我们参加骑骆驼，然后在自然栖息地看袋鼠。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK. I'll arrange that for you. I forgot to mention that the journey also includes a stop at a place of aboriginal artwork. It's a place well-known for its stone carvings of animals and mythical creatures.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：好的。我为您安排。我忘了说，旅程还包括在土著艺术品的地方停留。那是一个以动物和神话生物石雕而闻名的地方。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds great! Are the carvings in the desert?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：听起来太棒了！那些石雕在沙漠里吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：是的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wonderful!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：太棒了！

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, that's perfect then. I'm sure you'll have a lovely trip, but remember that you need take care in the sun.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：那就完美了。我相信您会有一个愉快的旅行，但记住要注意防晒。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes. We're really looking forward to our trip. We really want to try to experience the dreamtime under the stars.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：是的。我们真的很期待这次旅行。我们真的很想尝试体验星空下的梦幻时光。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course. That's what a trip to the Outback is really all about.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：当然。这才是内陆旅行的真正意义所在。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes. Now, how about the cost...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 顾客：是的。那么，费用方面……

transcriptSentences.speaker: ANNOUNCER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Continuing our broadcast of public service announcements, Worldwide Helpers announces upcoming vacancies for a number of volunteer worker positions. All applicants must meet the following requirements.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 播音员：继续我们的公共服务公告，Worldwide Helpers 宣布即将有一些志愿者职位空缺。所有申请者必须满足以下要求。

transcriptSentences.speaker: ANNOUNCER
transcriptSentences.englishText: First of all, applicants must be over 18 years of age. The company apologizes, but there can be no exceptions to this rule. Second, persons interested in these positions may not have police records. Minor traffic offenses like a parking ticket are, of course, no problem. But, and I quote, "past and present drug users and sex offenders" need not apply. The employer will, of course, check with the police to verify your clean record.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 播音员：首先，申请者必须年满18岁。公司表示歉意，但这条规则没有例外。第二，对这些职位感兴趣的人不能有犯罪记录。轻微的交通违规，比如停车罚单，当然没问题。但是，我引用原话，“过去和现在的吸毒者和性犯罪者”无需申请。雇主当然会向警方核实你的清白记录。

transcriptSentences.speaker: ANNOUNCER
transcriptSentences.englishText: In addition, applicants must supply references from past or present employers or teachers along with their recent CV. These references must testify as to the applicant's work habits and/or character. Remember, these are references from employers or teachers. A note from your dear old Mum won't do. Worldwide Helpers assures me that they will contact these references to confirm they are genuine.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 播音员：此外，申请者必须提供过去或现在的雇主或老师的推荐信，连同近期的简历。这些推荐信必须证明申请人的工作习惯和/或性格。记住，这些是雇主或老师的推荐信。你亲爱的老妈写的便条可不行。Worldwide Helpers 向我保证，他们会联系这些推荐人以确认其真实性。

transcriptSentences.speaker: ANNOUNCER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Although all positions are volunteer, the employer will reimburse some of your expenses. For example, they will pay for transportation to and from the job site. Aside from that the cost of phone calls is covered.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 播音员：虽然所有职位都是志愿者，但雇主会报销你的一些费用。例如，他们会支付往返工作地点的交通费。除此之外，电话费也包含在内。

transcriptSentences.speaker: ANNOUNCER
transcriptSentences.englishText: As for the positions themselves, there are three types. The first involves assisting persons confined to wheelchairs. For this position, volunteers must be physically fit and in excellent health. They must be able to lift at least one-hundred and fifty pounds. They should also have a current First Aid certificate from the Red Cross. But the most important requirement is that the volunteer must have his own car. On Tuesday afternoons, the volunteers take their clients to various scenic spots around the city to experience and enjoy nature.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 播音员：至于职位本身，有三种类型。第一种是帮助被限制在轮椅上的人。对于这个职位，志愿者必须身体健康，状况良好。他们必须能举起至少150磅的重量。他们还应该持有红十字会颁发的有效急救证书。但最重要的要求是志愿者必须有自己的汽车。每周二下午，志愿者们带他们的客户去城市周围的各个景点体验和享受大自然。

transcriptSentences.speaker: ANNOUNCER
transcriptSentences.englishText: If you don't drive, but you'd still like to get involved, the center has a number of openings for people to read to the blind. Readers must, of course, read English clearly. Persons with no foreign accent are preferred. For these positions, you must be available on Monday mornings. Oh, wait, I see a note here. There is one opening for someone who can read Urdu. Apparently, there is a Pakistani blind person who'd like to hear his or her native language. But the other positions are all in English.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 播音员：如果你不开车，但仍然想参与，中心有为盲人朗读的多个职位空缺。朗读者当然必须清晰地朗读英语。没有外国口音的人优先。这些职位要求你周一上午有空。哦，等等，我看到这里有个备注。有一个职位需要能读乌尔都语的人。显然，有一位巴基斯坦盲人想听自己母语的朗读。但其他职位都是英语。

transcriptSentences.speaker: ANNOUNCER
transcriptSentences.englishText: And finally, there are a limited number of volunteers needed to care for disabled children. I'm sorry, but the information I've been given does not say how many children or what disabilities they have. In any case, you are needed to care for the children for one week in August. Apparently this will be at the close of the summer holiday. I would guess this involves helping them with the routine chores of daily life. Again, volunteers for this position must know basic First Aid, be in good health, and be able to lift up to 75 pounds.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 播音员：最后，还需要有限数量的志愿者来照顾残疾儿童。很抱歉，我得到的信息没有说明有多少儿童或他们有什么残疾。无论如何，你需要在8月份照顾这些孩子一周。显然这将在暑假结束时进行。我猜这包括帮助她们处理日常生活中的常规杂务。同样，这个职位的志愿者必须了解基本的急救知识，身体健康，并能举起75磅的重量。

transcriptSentences.speaker: ANNOUNCER
transcriptSentences.englishText: All applications for this position have to be submitted no later than Monday, August 8. Applications may be made either by regular postal service-- the "snail mail"--or by email. The mailing address is Worldwide Helpers, Post Office Box 651, East Surrey BY8 99C. Please write "ATTENTION: Mary Smith" on the envelope. Or you can send e-mail to acrawfor@worldwidehelpers.org. That's A-C-R-A-W-F-O-R at W-O-R-L-D-W-I-D-E-H-E-L-P-E-R-S dot org. So get out there and do something good!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 播音员：所有这些职位的申请必须在8月8日星期一之前提交。申请可以通过普通邮政服务——“蜗牛邮件”——或电子邮件提交。邮寄地址是Worldwide Helpers, Post Office Box 651, East Surrey BY8 99C。请在信封上写“ATTENTION: Mary Smith”。或者您可以发送电子邮件至 acrawfor@worldwidehelpers.org。那是 A-C-R-A-W-F-O-R 在 W-O-R-L-D-W-I-D-E-H-E-L-P-E-R-S dot org。所以，走出去做点好事吧！

transcriptSentences.speaker: ANNOUNCER
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, our next announcement is looking for someone to "facilitate" tiger breeding at the London Zoo. And, get this, it's a "strictly volunteer" position. That means you don't get paid! Oh my God...I'm sorry ladies and gentlemen, but I just have to laugh...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 播音员：好的，我们的下一个公告是在为伦敦动物园寻找一位“促进”老虎繁殖的人。而且，听好了，这是一个“严格自愿”的职位。这意味着你没有报酬！哦，天哪……女士们先生们，很抱歉，但我实在忍不住要笑……

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Are you just leaving the library now? I saw you get there at 8:00 a.m.!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：你现在才离开图书馆？我看见你早上8点就到了！

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, I've been there all day.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：是的，我在那儿待了一整天。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: What for? They hire a cute new librarian or something?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：为了什么？他们雇了一个漂亮的新图书管理员还是什么的？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: I wish. No, it's the presentation that I will give in Environmental Science the day after tomorrow.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：我倒是希望。不，是因为后天我要在环境科学课上做展示。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: What's it about? I heard you were really excited about the class. And Dr. Schnee always calls you for the "arcane" questions, as he calls them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：关于什么的？我听说你对那门课非常感兴趣。施尼博士总是找你回答他所谓的“深奥”问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: It's about environmental damage in the Yucatan.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：是关于尤卡坦半岛的环境破坏。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Excuse me, what? Or is that where?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：你说什么？那是个地方吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yucatan. It's a state in Southeast Mexico.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：尤卡坦。是墨西哥东南部的一个州。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: So what's happening there?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：那里发生了什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Agriculture is having a really adverse impact on the environment. There are too many farmers doing too much farming. It's really destroying the forests and ruining the soil. Deforestation is a major problem there now.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：农业对环境产生了非常不利的影响。农民太多，耕作过度。这正在破坏森林，毁坏土壤。森林砍伐现在是那里的主要问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: How did you learn about this? I don't recall Dr. Schnee saying anything about it in lecture.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：你是怎么知道的？我不记得施尼博士在课上提到过这个。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, but my brother went there last month. You know, to look at the old cities the Maya Indians built. That's what first got me interested.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：是的，但我哥哥上个月去了那里。你知道，去看玛雅印第安人建造的古城。那是让我开始感兴趣的原因。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Your brother Tom?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：你哥哥汤姆？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: No, Dick, Harry's twin. Anyway, he told me how few trees there were now and how much empty ground that grows almost nothing. He said the place looked more like desert than jungle in some parts. It brought environmental damage. So I started looking for materials in the library. Here, look at this magazine.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：不，是迪克，哈利的双胞胎兄弟。总之，他告诉我现在树很少，大片空地几乎什么都不长。他说有些地方看起来更像沙漠而不是丛林。这让我想到了环境破坏。所以我就开始在图书馆找资料。喏，看看这本杂志。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: What's in it?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：里面有什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: It's an old issue of "National Geographic." It includes interviews with tourists who've been there in the past few years. It's pretty bad. See the photos?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：是一本旧《国家地理》杂志。里面有过去几年去过那里的游客的采访。情况很糟糕。看到这些照片了吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: I see the photos, but one or two photos don't prove anything.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：我看到照片了，但一两张照片不能证明什么。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Then read what the article says. Right there. The first thing it points out is how soil samples show it is hard for anything to grow there. It says how an area of 21,000 square kilometers has lost most of its forest in the past ten years. See, there are graphs. As the number of farmers increases, the acres of forest have decreased. It's an inverse relation.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：那就读读文章上写的。就在那里。它首先指出的是土壤样本显示那里很难生长任何东西。它说21,000平方公里的区域在过去十年里失去了大部分森林。看，有图表。随着农民数量的增加，森林英亩数减少了。这是一个反比关系。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: So how big is that state? I'm sorry, but I've never really learned the metric system.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：那个州有多大？抱歉，我从来没真正学过公制单位。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: It's bigger than the state of Massachusetts!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：比马萨诸塞州还大！

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's shocking! Anything else?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：太令人震惊了！还有别的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: There's lots of else. Scientists say there's a "growing area" of about 10.5 square kilometers where nothing can grow at all. It's like the beginning of a desert.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：还有很多。科学家说有一个大约10.5平方公里的“生长区域”，那里什么都长不了。就像沙漠的开端。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh yes. What Dr. Schnee called "desertification." But, why can't anything grow there? I've never really studied soil chemistry.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：哦对。就是施尼博士所说的“沙漠化”。但是，为什么那里什么都长不了？我从没真正研究过土壤化学。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm just starting to look into that subject, but my sister Marie is a geologist and she says the problem is that the soil has too much saline, with no plants helping to adjust the chemistry. Apparently, that's a common problem with soil types throughout areas with rain forest. Once you lose the plant cover, it's difficult to bring it back. Reforestation is almost impossible, even if the land is not being used for other purposes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：我才刚开始研究这个问题，但我姐姐玛丽是地质学家，她说问题在于土壤含盐量太高，没有植物帮助调节化学平衡。显然，这是雨林地区土壤类型普遍存在的问题。一旦失去植被覆盖，就很难恢复。再造林几乎不可能，即使土地没有用于其他用途。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wait a minute, what is 'saline?'
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：等等，什么是“含盐量”？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Saline is salt dissolved in water. Scientists who've gone there have taken measurements. They do this by gathering a sample of the soil and running a simple test that shows the ionization of the solution. The Geology Department in our own university has reviewed the soil at the site too. They're right. It looks pretty bad. The level of salinity is going up. But the plants that would solve that problem can't be planted in soil like that. There is a narrow spectrum of salinity in which the plants will grow.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：Saline 就是溶解在水里的盐。去过那里的科学家进行了测量。他们通过采集土壤样本并进行简单测试来显示溶液的离子化。我们大学的地质系也检测了那里的土壤。他们说得对。情况看起来很糟。盐度水平在上升。但能解决这个问题的植物在这样的土壤里种不了。植物能生长的盐度范围很窄。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: And once you pass the threshold, there is no way to put the problem right?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：一旦超过了阈值，就没有办法纠正了吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Exactly. It's possible that no one can do anything to stop the trend now. And all because of human greed! I...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：正是如此。也许现在没人能阻止这个趋势了。而这一切都是因为人类的贪婪！我……

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wait a second. How do you know these 'scientists' can be trusted? What kind of reputation do they have? Are they reliable?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：等一下。你怎么知道这些“科学家”可信？他们有什么样的声誉？他们可靠吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh they're definitely reliable. They include four members of the faculty from the Geology Department right here at MIT. Here, study these photographs and check the damage yourself. That's what Dr. Horst who wrote this book here did. He's newly appointed, but Dr. Schnee says he's brilliant.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：哦，他们绝对可靠。其中包括麻省理工学院地质系的四位教员。喏，研究这些照片，你自己看看破坏情况。这就是写了这本书的霍斯特博士所做的。他是新上任的，但施尼博士说他非常有才华。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, where are you going now?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：那你现在去哪儿？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm headed over to the Geography Department to borrow a map for my presentation. You know, this whole problem could have been avoided! The farmers there in the Yucutan--
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：我要去地理系借一张地图用于我的展示。你知道，整个问题本来是可以避免的！尤卡坦的农民们——

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Uh, Pete??
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：呃，皮特？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PETE
transcriptSentences.englishText: What?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 皮特：什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: DAVE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Go take a break! Leave some studying for the rest of us.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 戴夫：去休息一下吧！给我们其他人留点学习的机会。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good afternoon, and welcome to Insect Biology 101. I'd like to begin this course with a few remarks about good insects and bad ones. Bugs are all around us and that's both a benefit and an annoyance--sometimes maybe even serious harm. First let's talk about the good things that insects do for us.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：下午好，欢迎来到昆虫生物学101。我想用一些关于益虫和害虫的评论来开始这门课。虫子无处不在，这既是好处也是烦恼——有时甚至可能造成严重伤害。首先，让我们谈谈昆虫为我们所做的好事。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Probably the most important insect for humans, and maybe for all other life, is the bee. Bees help plants in the process of pollination, and thus are necessary to most flowers and fruit-producing trees. That is, they carry pollen from "male" flowers to "female." If it weren't for bees, we'd have very few food plants and no fruit either. In fact, there would be no "we." No less a thinker than Albert Einstein pointed out that, without bees, humanity would be dead within a year or less. We'd starve. It's that simple. That should maybe make us just a little humble.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：对人类，也许对所有其他生命来说，最重要的昆虫可能是蜜蜂。蜜蜂在植物授粉过程中帮助植物，因此对大多数花卉和果树是必需的。也就是说，它们把花粉从“雄性”花带到“雌性”花。如果没有蜜蜂，我们的粮食作物会很少，也不会有水果。事实上，也不会有“我们”。就连爱因斯坦这样伟大的思想家也指出，没有蜜蜂，人类会在一年或更短时间内灭亡。我们会饿死。就这么简单。这也许应该让我们稍微谦卑一点。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: A little less dramatic is the fact that bees also make the honey we eat. Moreover, they produce beewax, which is useful in candles and it's also used as a first-rate furniture polish. Sure, these may not be vital to our lives, but they can serve as reminders of how important bees are. That's a point I keep coming back to in this course. Though, in all fairness, I should point out that butterflies aid in pollination as well as bees.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：不那么戏剧性的是，蜜蜂也制造我们吃的蜂蜜。此外，它们产生蜂蜡，可用于制作蜡烛，也可以用作一流的家具抛光剂。当然，这些可能对我们的生命不是至关重要的，但它们可以作为蜜蜂重要性的提醒。这是我在本课程中反复强调的一个观点。不过，公平地说，我应该指出蝴蝶也和蜜蜂一样帮助授粉。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, here in Michigan, what's the worst part of summer? Yep, that's right--- mosquitoes. But I'm talking about helpful insects, right? So let's look at the dragonfly first. If there were no dragonflies, there would be even more mosquitoes! Dragonflies mainly eat mosquitoes and also a few other insects. Yes, that's right. They don't just fly around, they also help to eliminate harmful insects. So, the next time you see a dragonfly, don't you dare kill it!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：现在，在密歇根这里，夏天最糟糕的是什么？是的，就是蚊子。但我在说有益昆虫，对吧？所以让我们先看看蜻蜓。如果没有蜻蜓，蚊子会更多！蜻蜓主要吃蚊子，也吃其他一些昆虫。是的，没错。它们不只是飞来飞去，它们还有助于消灭有害昆虫。所以，下次你看到蜻蜓时，你敢杀它试试！

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now let's talk a little about those harmful insects. Take the mosquitoes I just mentioned as an example. Not so many years ago, mosquitoes here in America weren't just annoying. Some were even deadly. They carried malaria and yellow fever. My own ancestor, the Confederate General John Bell Hood lived through the worst battles of Civil War, only to die at age thirty-eight from yellow fever. A pest, not a bullet!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：现在我们来谈谈那些有害昆虫。以我刚刚提到的蚊子为例。就在几年前，美国的蚊子不仅令人烦恼。有些甚至是致命的。它们携带疟疾和黄热病。我自己的祖先，南方联邦将军约翰·贝尔·胡德经历了内战中最惨烈的战斗，却在38岁时死于黄热病。是害虫杀了他，而不是子弹！

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: But there's worse. In the first British colony, Virginia, 70% of the people coming to America died within the first seven years! Things were so bad that the English had to start bringing in slaves from Africa. In general the Africans were immune to malaria and lived longer. And the effects of slavery are still with us. American slavery: that's an awfully big evil due to one little insect!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：还有更糟的。在第一个英国殖民地弗吉尼亚，来到美国的70%的人在头七年内死亡！情况如此糟糕，以至于英国人不得不开始从非洲引进奴隶。一般来说，非洲人对疟疾免疫，活得更久。奴隶制的影响至今仍在。美国奴隶制：那是由于一种小昆虫而造成的一个巨大的邪恶！

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Other insects, of course, destroy food crops. In China, for instance, locusts continue to be a danger to the harvest in some areas. Less important, but still annoying, moths eat people's clothes and dust mites slowly destroy carpets. Worse, but still in the home, termites or "white ants" eat wood: the wood of your house. If they are not stopped, they can eventually destroy the whole building. Usually they seriously damage a building before anyone even notices them. So, as we all know, insects can be a real trouble.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：当然，其他昆虫会破坏粮食作物。例如，在中国，蝗虫在一些地区仍然对收成构成威胁。不那么严重但仍然恼人的是，蛾子吃衣服，尘螨慢慢破坏地毯。更糟的，但仍在家里，白蚁吃木头：你房子的木头。如果不阻止它们，它们最终可能摧毁整栋建筑。通常在任何人注意到它们之前，它们就已经严重损坏了建筑。所以，我们都知道，昆虫确实是个大麻烦。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, what to do? You can go ahead and start killing harmful insects. In the early decades after the Communist Revolution in China, Chairman Mao encouraged the people to swat every fly they could see. Slogans on the walls of buildings called them "little capitalists." But flies reproduce too quickly for this to be a long-term solution.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：那么，该怎么办？你可以直接开始杀死有害昆虫。在中国共产党革命后的头几十年里，毛主席鼓励人们拍死他们能看到的每一只苍蝇。建筑墙上的标语称它们为“小资本家”。但苍蝇繁殖太快，这并非长久之计。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: For some decades in the West, to kill insects with chemicals seemed a good remedy. Unfortunately, chemicals can only be used in a limited area for a limited time. It's a small scale solution. The insects come back. Worse still, some of the poisons used like DDT were found harmful to the environment. Many kinds of wildlife, like hawks, were harmed. And people in chemical-using rural areas have one of the highest rates of liver cancer in the world. It's no secret that the chemicals remain harmful to humans.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：在西方，有几十年时间，用化学药品杀虫似乎是个好办法。不幸的是，化学品只能在有限的区域和有限的时间内使用。这是一种小规模的解决方案。昆虫会卷土重来。更糟的是，一些使用的毒药如DDT被发现对环境有害。许多野生动物，如鹰，受到伤害。在大量使用化学品的农村地区，肝癌发病率居世界前列。化学品对人体有害早已不是秘密。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Like all species, insects adapt to their changing environments at an amazing rate. When a new chemical is introduced to their habitat, the insects that survive are generally the ones with some way of resisting the harmful effects. They then breed with the other survivors, and just like that insects become resistant to most poison in a few generations. An insect generation, remember, is a couple of months at most!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：像所有物种一样，昆虫以惊人的速度适应变化的环境。当一种新化学物质被引入它们的栖息地时，存活下来的昆虫通常是有某种抵抗有害效应能力的。它们然后与其他幸存者繁殖，就这样，昆虫在几代之内就对大多数毒药产生了抗性。记住，昆虫的一代最多只有几个月！

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, again we have to ask: what to do? Well, there are biological solutions. Some of these are pretty simple. One is destroying the insects' habitat. You take away their home or food. Cleaning your kitchen is the best way to prevent roaches. No garbage: no food. Getting rid of marshes and swamps eliminates mosquitoes. Other solutions might include bringing in dragonflies or bats in areas where mosquitoes are many. This is a cheaper alternative to chemicals. Biological methods like this also bring no extra pollution to the environment. But you have to be careful. If you change the environment too much, you might be hurting other forms of life accidentally.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：所以，我们再次要问：怎么办？有生物解决方法。有些非常简单。一种是破坏昆虫的栖息地。你拿走它们的家或食物。打扫厨房是防止蟑螂的最好方法。没有垃圾就没有食物。清除沼泽地可以消灭蚊子。其他解决方案可能包括在蚊子多的地方引入蜻蜓或蝙蝠。这是比化学品更便宜的替代方案。这样的生物方法也不会对环境造成额外污染。但你必须小心。如果你改变环境太多，可能会意外伤害其他生命形式。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: One recent method of controlling insect populations involves interrupting their breeding cycle. What does that mean? It means "birth control for bugs." Insects are provided with food that makes them unable to reproduce. Since they can't have babies, the population disappears, or nearly so. And since no young are born, resistance is not a problem with no young insects developing increased resistance. Interrupt the life-cycle, eliminate the bug! It's clear that we must have an understanding of the life cycle of the insect. At least that's the plan. We'll go into more details as this course goes along. Now I will stop here to see whether you have any questions or not.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：最近一种控制昆虫数量的方法涉及中断它们的繁殖周期。这是什么意思？意思是“虫子的计划生育”。给昆虫提供使它们不能繁殖的食物。因为它们不能繁殖，种群就会消失或几乎消失。而且因为没有幼体出生，抗性就不成问题，没有幼体会发展出增加的抗性。打断生命周期，消灭虫子！很明显我们必须了解昆虫的生命周期。至少这是计划。随着课程的深入，我们会进一步探讨细节。现在我停下来，看看你们是否有问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SERVICE REP
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello, and welcome to "Under Pressure Enterprises," Customer Service Department. This is Kelly. How may I help you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服代表：您好，欢迎致电 Under Pressure Enterprises 客户服务部。我是凯利。我能为您做些什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: MR. HEWITT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, I'm calling about one of your rice cookers I just purchased.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 休伊特先生：是的，我打电话来是关于我刚买的一个你们品牌的电饭煲。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CR
transcriptSentences.englishText: What seems to be the problem, sir?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服：先生，出了什么问题？

transcriptSentences.speaker: H
transcriptSentences.englishText: Seems? There's no seeming about it! The blasted thing shoots hot steam all over the place, that's what! It nearly scalded my hand when I went to open it. Why it could have killed the cat or something. It could have exploded and killed my wife and me!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 休伊特：似乎？这没什么似乎的！这该死的东西到处喷热蒸汽，就是这样！我去打开的时候差点烫伤我的手。它甚至可能把猫或别的什么弄死。它可能爆炸，把我和我妻子炸死！

transcriptSentences.speaker: CR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sir, sir, please calm down. As long as the steam escapes the cooker, it won't explode.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服：先生，先生，请冷静。只要蒸汽从电饭煲里排出来，它就不会爆炸。

transcriptSentences.speaker: H
transcriptSentences.englishText: So you're telling me there's no problem! Are you calling me a liar?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 休伊特：所以你是在告诉我没问题！你在说我是骗子吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sir, no one is calling you a liar.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服：先生，没人说您是骗子。

transcriptSentences.speaker: H
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes! So I demand a full refund!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 休伊特：是的！所以我要求全额退款！

transcriptSentences.speaker: CR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Under Pressure will be happy to refund your money, sir. Now I just need some basic information.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服：Under Pressure 很乐意给您退款，先生。现在我需要一些基本信息。

transcriptSentences.speaker: H
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, OK. Sorry. I do tend to get a little hot under the collar. My wife tells me to slow down...So, what do you need to know?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 休伊特：好的，好的。对不起。我确实有时容易发火。我妻子叫我放慢节奏……那么，你需要了解什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sir, don't worry. I just need to ask you the model number of the cooker.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服：先生，别担心。我只需要问您电饭煲的型号。

transcriptSentences.speaker: H
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hmmm... where are my glasses? Ah, here! Let's see...ah. It's R242.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 休伊特：嗯……我的眼镜在哪？啊，找到了！让我看看……啊。是R242。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CR
transcriptSentences.englishText: R242. OK, and how much did you pay for the product?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服：R242。好的，您为这个产品付了多少钱？

transcriptSentences.speaker: H
transcriptSentences.englishText: 89.99 pounds. It was on sale, I guess I should tell you.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 休伊特：89.99英镑。是在打折时买的，我想我应该告诉您。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Thank you, that's honest of you. Now, where did you buy the cooker? Which store and which branch?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服：谢谢您，您很诚实。那么，您在哪里买的电饭煲？哪家商店，哪个分店？

transcriptSentences.speaker: H
transcriptSentences.englishText: At that big Electric Life appliance store downtown.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 休伊特：在市中心的那个大型 Electric Life 电器商店。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CR
transcriptSentences.englishText: The City Centre Branch? That's the one.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服：市中心分店？就是那家。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CR
transcriptSentences.englishText: And you say the problem is that the steam escapes?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服：您说问题是蒸汽泄漏？

transcriptSentences.speaker: H
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, it does!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 休伊特：是的，确实！

transcriptSentences.speaker: CR
transcriptSentences.englishText: No problem, sir. If there's steam escaping, clearly the cooker is broken or defective. So we have a R242 cooker with an escaping steam problem. It was bought from Electric Life's City Centre Branch for 89.99. Is that correct?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服：没问题，先生。如果有蒸汽泄漏，显然电饭煲是坏了或有缺陷。那么，是一台有蒸汽泄漏问题的R242电饭煲，从 Electric Life 市中心分店以89.99英镑购买。对吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: H
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, that is correct.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 休伊特：是的，正确。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, I nearly forget. When did you buy the cooker?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客服：哦，我差点忘了。您什么时候买的电饭煲？

transcriptSentences.speaker: H
transcriptSentences.englishText: Just as soon as my wife got the crazy idea she'll live longer if she stops eating good English food: roast beef and mash. No, all she says she wants is rice and vegetables and sauces you'd not soak your feet in!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 休伊特：就在我妻子刚有了那个疯狂念头的时候——她说如果她不吃好的英式食物：烤牛肉和土豆泥，就能活得更长。不，她说她只想要米饭和蔬菜，还有你都不想泡脚的酱汁！
