transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello everyone, and welcome to the University of New South Wales. The first thing I'd like to do at today's Orientation Session is get you all oriented! That means tell you the location of some useful facilities and services. So, first of all, take out the maps we gave you all as you came in the door. The map is the big yellow sheet of paper.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家好，欢迎来到新南威尔士大学。在今天的新生入学指导会上，我想做的第一件事就是让大家熟悉环境！也就是告诉你们一些有用的设施和服务的位置。首先，拿出你们进门时我们发给每个人的地图。地图就是那张大黄纸。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: As you can see on the map, North is at the top, South at the bottom, etcetera. Which way is North? Well, look through that window on my left, your right. See the rising sun? That would have to be East. So North must be directly behind me.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：正如你们在地图上看到的，北在上方，南方在下方，等等。哪边是北？看看我左边、你们右边的窗户。看到升起的太阳了吗？那一定是东方。所以北方一定在我的正后方。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, We are at the campus's Main Gate. The Recreational facilities are on my right-hand and its opposite is the Student Center. No questions? Good. Pretty easy, right?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：现在，我们位于校园的正门。娱乐设施在我的右手边，它的对面是学生中心。没有问题？好的。很简单，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, did everyone eat breakfast at the Student Food Service this morning? Was the food good? Yes, yes. I am joking. I've eaten there, too. So after a meal like that, you must be eager to go to a doctor. Right? Well I have good news for you: the Student Health Center is located about half a kilometer straight north of here. Look on your maps. You see the street on the east side of this building? Ned Kelly Avenue? Just follow that about 500 meters, and the Health Center will be on your left at the third cross-street.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：好的，大家今天早上都在学生餐饮服务中心吃早饭了吗？食物好吃吗？是的，是的。我在开玩笑。我也在那里吃过。所以吃过那样的饭之后，你们一定急着想去看医生吧？对吧？好消息是：学生健康中心就在从这里正北大约半公里的地方。看你们的地图。你们看到这栋建筑东边的那条街了吗？内德·凯利大道？沿着它走大约500米，健康中心就在你们左手边第三条横街上。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, I know you all just got here. So you must be wondering how to tell your folks you've arrived safely, how much you miss the dog, and how you already need more money. If you don't have an Iphone, you probably are wondering where to find a computer. Well, I have good news. If you go straight out of its door and walk down the Garden Street, you'll see the Internet Unit on your left-side, just next to the Gym. The hours are posted on the door, and the computers are free, but you must bring your student I.D. card with you. Like I tell everyone, if you need help with anything, you can probably find it right here in the Student Center.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我知道你们都是刚到这里。所以你们一定在想怎么告诉家人你们安全到达了，你们有多想念你们的狗，还有你们已经需要更多钱了。如果你没有苹果手机，你可能想知道在哪里能找到电脑。好消息是：如果你从正门出去，沿着花园街走，你会看到互联网中心在你的左手边，就在健身房旁边。开放时间贴在门上，电脑是免费的，但你必须带上你的学生证。就像我跟每个人说的，如果你需要任何帮助，你可能在学生中心就能找到。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Do you see the four buildings there between the Student Center and the Library? Those are the dormitories. The men's dorms are the two on the south; the women's the two on the north.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：你们看到学生中心和图书馆之间的那四栋建筑了吗？那些是宿舍。南边的两栋是男生宿舍；北边的两栋是女生宿舍。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, I'm sorry to have to tell you. But, the university has been doing a lot of repairs and remodeling, and it's not all done yet. So there may be some small problems with your dorm rooms. Maybe the window doesn't open. Maybe an air-conditioner is missing or does not work. If there are any problems, you can go to the Complaint Office, which is right beside the teaching building between the Parker Street and the Crammer Street. Just tell them your problem and they should have it fixed by the time you graduate in four years. I'm joking, but please be patient. There are a lot of little things they need to take care of.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：好的，很抱歉要告诉你们。但是，学校一直在进行大量的维修和改造，还没有全部完成。所以你们的宿舍房间可能会有一些小问题。也许窗户打不开。也许没有空调或者空调坏了。如果有什么问题，你可以去投诉办公室，就在帕克街和克拉默街之间的教学楼旁边。只要告诉他们你的问题，他们应该会在四年后你毕业之前修好。我在开玩笑，但请耐心一点。有很多小事需要他们处理。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Tired of the school food? No? Give it a week. Or maybe you just need a place to get coffee in the wee hours of the night during one of those marathon study sessions. Either way, you definitely have to check out the little Cafe just past the women's dormitories. They've got free Wi-Fi, so a lot of students saddle up with coffee and a bagel for hours on end to get work done.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：厌倦了学校的食物？没有？等一个星期试试。或者你只是需要在一个通宵学习的时候，在深夜找个地方喝杯咖啡。不管怎样，你一定要去看看女生宿舍旁边的那个小咖啡馆。那里有免费无线网络，所以很多学生会带着咖啡和百吉饼一坐就是几个小时来赶功课。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: As for the dorm rooms, I have some bad news and some good news. The bad news is the rooms are small and you'll probably be sharing space with at least three other students. The good news is that each room has its own bathroom. What's good about sharing a bathroom with three strangers? Hmmm....good question. OK, call it bad news and worse news.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：至于宿舍房间，我有坏消息也有好消息。坏消息是房间很小，而且你可能会和至少三个其他学生共用空间。好消息是每个房间都有自己的浴室。和三个陌生人共用浴室有什么好的？嗯……问得好。好吧，就当是坏消息和更坏的消息吧。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hey, maybe try this for good news: each dorm has a kitchen. If you want to make snacks or meals, you can do it there. You can buy food containers at any campus convenience store, so you can store your food in the kitchen.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：嘿，也许这个算是好消息：每栋宿舍都有一个厨房。如果你想做零食或饭菜，可以在那里做。你可以在任何校园便利店买食品容器，这样你就可以把食物存放在厨房里。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: But a word of warning: you should definitely write your name on your food containers. Sad to say, there are food thieves among your fellow students. Speaking of thieves, a word about security. I mean this is Australia and we do get drunken bush-rangers wandering onto campus. Each of you will be given a key for your dorm room. Don't lose it. You have to pay for any replacement and fill out a bunch of papers too. Red tape, huh? Your key does not work for the front door of your dorm, however. To the right of each door, there is a keypad with numbers. When you move in, they will tell you the code you use to enter the door. Please do NOT tell the code to people who do not live in the dorm.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：但是要提醒一句：你一定要在食品容器上写上你的名字。很遗憾地说，同学中有偷食物的贼。说到贼，说一句关于安全的话。我的意思是这里是澳大利亚，确实会有喝醉的丛林游荡者漫步到校园里。你们每个人都会得到一把宿舍房间的钥匙。别弄丢了。补办要花钱，还要填一堆表格。官僚主义，对吧？不过你的钥匙不能开宿舍大门。每扇门的右边都有一个数字键盘。当你入住时，他们会告诉你进入大门的密码。请不要把密码告诉不住在宿舍的人。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Let's see. Have I forgotten anything? Oh, yes. Most of you are not rich, correct? So when your clothes get dirty, you can't just throw them away and buy new ones. That means you have to learn to do laundry. Or, men, that means you have to hurry up and get married. If you decide to wash those clothes and not get married, there are laundries in each dorm. Where? Oh, I almost forgot to tell you. The laundry for each dorm is in the basement.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：让我想想。我有没有忘了什么？哦，是的。你们大多数人都不富裕，对吧？所以当你们的衣服脏了，你们不能直接把它们扔掉买新的。这意味着你们得学会洗衣服。或者，男生们，这意味着你们得赶紧结婚。如果你们决定洗那些衣服而不是结婚，每栋宿舍都有洗衣房。在哪里？哦，我差点忘了告诉你们。每栋宿舍的洗衣房都在地下室。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Some real good news this time: if you are a student, it is free. You do have to buy your own soap, however. The laundry closes, by the by, at 11:30.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：这次有一些真正的好消息：如果你是学生，免费。不过你得自己买肥皂。顺便说一下，洗衣房晚上11点半关门。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: And, now that I've mentioned 11:30, please remember the dorm doors are locked at 11:30 p.m. Your code will not work. If you want to get in, you'll have to call the night watchman. Don't worry, you can get that number at the Dorm Office. Yes, the Dorm Office and the Complaint Office are the same office. All right, then. Before we continue are there any questions?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：现在既然我提到了11点半，请记住宿舍大门在晚上11点半上锁。你的密码没用了。如果你想进去，就得打电话叫守夜人。别担心，你可以在宿舍办公室拿到那个号码。是的，宿舍办公室和投诉办公室是同一个办公室。好了，在我们继续之前，有问题吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SHEILA
transcriptSentences.englishText: Professor Dundee? We're ready to make our presentation.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 希拉：邓迪教授？我们准备好做展示报告了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, yes. I did say one o'clock, didn't I? Please, sit down. So, who goes first? Bruce? Or you, Sheila?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：哦，是的。我说了一点钟，对吧？请坐。那么，谁先来？布鲁斯？还是你，希拉？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SHEILA
transcriptSentences.englishText: I guess I could. Bruce is always a little shy.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 希拉：我想我可以先来。布鲁斯总是有点害羞。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Not after he's had a lager for lunch, eh Bruce?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：他午饭喝了啤酒就不害羞了，对吧布鲁斯？

transcriptSentences.speaker: BRUCE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Heh, heh. No, Sheila really should go first.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布鲁斯：嘿，嘿。不，还是希拉先来吧。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SHEILA
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK. Well, I'm reporting on the effects of different marketing strategies on the cheese and oil markets in New Zealand. Different strategies obviously affect the sales volume differently. I looked at the sales in two cities, Christchurch and Wellington.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 希拉：好的。嗯，我报告的是不同营销策略对新西兰奶酪和油类市场的影响。不同的策略显然对销售量有不同的影响。我研究了两个城市的销售情况，基督城和惠灵顿。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: And what did you find, pray tell?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：那么你发现了什么，请问？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SHEILA
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, in Wellington the sales of both oil and cheese have risen pretty steadily. In fact the sales have risen quicker than the population. On the other hand, in Christchurch, the volume of sales for both products has been about even.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 希拉：嗯，在惠灵顿，油和奶酪的销售都相当稳定地增长。事实上，销售增长比人口增长还要快。另一方面，在基督城，两种产品的销售量大致持平。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wait, so you said sales in Wellington have been going up?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：等等，所以你说惠灵顿的销售一直在上升？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SHEILA
transcriptSentences.englishText: Correct. The big ad agencies are trying out a new series of ads that shift the focus from health to great taste. They think that will get sales moving up in Christchurch, where the population is less affluent and as a result generally less health-conscious.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 希拉：对。大型广告公司正在尝试一系列新广告，把焦点从健康转移到美味上。他们认为这会让基督城的销售上升，那里的人口不太富裕，因此普遍不太注重健康。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Brilliant. Thank you. And Bruce?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：精彩。谢谢。布鲁斯呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: BRUCE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Uhhh...yeah. My report is about chocolate sales in Italy and Germany. The two countries' marketers have found out that you have to market chocolate differently in each country.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布鲁斯：呃……是的。我的报告是关于意大利和德国的巧克力销售。这两个国家的营销人员发现，你在每个国家销售巧克力的方式必须不同。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: For example?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：举个例子？

transcriptSentences.speaker: BRUCE
transcriptSentences.englishText: In Italy, if you locate your sales outlets near a children's school, sales do great. They say it doesn't matter much what brand of chocolate you're selling. As for Germany--
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布鲁斯：在意大利，如果你把销售点设在儿童学校附近，销售会很好。他们说卖什么牌子的巧克力关系不大。至于德国——

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: "Das Land der Schokolade".
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：“Das Land der Schokolade”。

transcriptSentences.speaker: BRUCE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Huh?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布鲁斯：啊？

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's German. It means "The Land of Chocolate." Germans love the stuff, so people make a joke and call Germany that.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：那是德语。意思是“巧克力之乡”。德国人喜欢巧克力，所以人们开玩笑把德国叫做这个。

transcriptSentences.speaker: BRUCE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh...uh, right...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布鲁斯：哦……呃，对……

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, you were saying?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：那么，你继续说？

transcriptSentences.speaker: BRUCE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, like you pointed out, Germans love chocolate. But they're thrifty. For a long time, the biggest selling brand was "Schmutzig", mostly because it was the second cheapest, but didn't taste too bad.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布鲁斯：嗯，正如你指出的，德国人喜欢巧克力。但他们很节俭。很长一段时间，最畅销的品牌是“Schmutzig”，主要是因为它是第二便宜的，但味道不差。

transcriptSentences.speaker: BRUCE
transcriptSentences.englishText: But lately, "Kostig", the most expensive brand, has been selling a lot.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布鲁斯：但最近，“Kostig”，最贵的品牌，卖了很多。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Really? And how did this begin to occur?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：真的吗？这是怎么发生的？

transcriptSentences.speaker: BRUCE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Kostig pays shop owners to put the candy just about knee-high for an adult.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布鲁斯：Kostig付钱给店主，把糖果放在大约成人膝盖高的位置。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: I don't see--
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：我不明白——

transcriptSentences.speaker: BRUCE
transcriptSentences.englishText: For little kids, that's about eye-level! That bright red candy is the first one they see, so they buy it! Even better, they start telling their moms to buy it too!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布鲁斯：对于小孩子来说，那大概就是视线高度！那种亮红色的糖果是他们第一个看到的，所以他们就会买！更好的是，他们开始叫他们的妈妈也买！

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Again brilliant! A pretty good job, both of you. Tell me, what do you plan to investigate for next week?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：又是精彩！你们两个都做得很好。告诉我，下周你们打算调查什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SHEILA
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'll be looking at ads for cleansing products in the local market. I'm especially interested in the effects of color on sales in advertising. You know, like the distinct orange color of Neutrogena face cleansing products.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 希拉：我会关注当地市场清洁产品的广告。我对颜色在广告中对销售的影响尤其感兴趣。你知道，比如露得清洁面产品那种独特的橙色。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: And you, Bruce?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：你呢，布鲁斯？

transcriptSentences.speaker: BRUCE
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm interested in the impact of container types on sales of cookies. I'm looking into packaging for cookies and how much the material used affects the image, and in turn sales. You know, most containers are paper, but some expensive cookies come in metal boxes. The shiny metal boxes catch people's attention and the image remains in the memory longer.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布鲁斯：我对容器类型对饼干销售的影响感兴趣。我在研究饼干的包装，以及所用材料对形象的影响，进而影响销售。你知道，大多数容器是纸的，但一些昂贵的饼干是金属盒装的。闪亮的金属盒吸引人们的注意力，形象在记忆中停留更长时间。

transcriptSentences.speaker: PROFESSOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, it sounds like you two are all set. But as always in this course, I urge you to keep paying attention to the extension of advertising. That's often the key. Alright, any questions for me before you go?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 教授：嗯，听起来你们两个都准备好了。但和这门课一贯的要求一样，我敦促你们继续关注广告的延伸。那往往是关键。好了，你们走之前还有什么问题问我吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SHEILA
transcriptSentences.englishText: No, I think I'm all set. Thanks!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 希拉：没有，我想我都准备好了。谢谢！

transcriptSentences.speaker: BRUCE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Me too. Thanks, Professor Dundee. See ya later.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布鲁斯：我也是。谢谢邓迪教授。再见。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. I'd like to take this opportunity to welcome you to our exhibition, "Two Centuries of the Bike." Let's stroll around the exhibition, shall we?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：女士们先生们，下午好。我想借此机会欢迎大家来到我们的展览“自行车两个世纪”。让我们一起逛逛展览吧，好吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Although there were a few early efforts back in the 1700s, you didn't really see many bikes till, say, the 1830s in England. Bikes were a response to the rapid growth of cities early in the 19th Century. Cities like London were getting too big to walk across! The early bike let people travel with less effort than walking. Plus a bike was a lot cheaper than a horse!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：虽然在18世纪有一些早期的尝试，但直到19世纪30年代左右在英国，你才真正看到很多自行车。自行车是对19世纪早期城市快速增长的回应。像伦敦这样的城市变得太大了，走路都走不过来！早期的自行车让人们比走路省力。而且自行车比马便宜多了！

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Think of it. No one invented a bike for, what, five thousand years of human history? Why did people do it then? Probably because this was the start of the Machine Age: people wanted machines to do all the work.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：想想看。在人类历史上大概五千年里，没有人发明自行车？为什么人们在那时发明了它？可能是因为那是机器时代的开始：人们想让机器做所有的工作。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: There were some drawbacks however. For one thing, there were no pedals. You simply pushed yourself along using your feet. Kind of like today's skateboard. That meant you went fairly slowly. And uphill, you actually worked harder, pushing that two-wheeler. Plus, the wheels were made of wood covered with metal, as you can see from this model. So the downside was that the ride was quite uncomfortable on most roads. Only a few gadget lovers had or used them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：然而也有一些缺点。其一，没有踏板。你只是用脚蹬着地面向前走。有点像今天的滑板。那意味着你走得相当慢。上坡时，推着两轮车实际上更费劲。另外，轮子是木头做的，外面包着金属，正如你们从这个模型看到的。所以缺点是在大多数路上骑起来很不舒服。只有少数小玩意爱好者拥有或使用它们。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: By the 1860s, though, improvements were being made. As you can see from this specimen, metal frames had become the rule. They're more durable than wood, and they don't warp in the rain. The biggest improvement however was the development of the chain and sprocket system. - They are connected. This meant you did not push the bike. You used pedals just like today. You had to try harder to balance, so it took some practice to figure out how to use the pedals. But it made the ride so much easier. As a result, the good thing was that you could ride a lot more smoothly and with very little effort.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：到了19世纪60年代，改进开始了。正如你们从这件展品看到的，金属车架成为了标准。它们比木头更耐用，而且不会在雨中翘曲。然而最大的改进是链条和链轮系统的开发——它们是连接在一起的。这意味着你不必推车了。你使用像今天一样的踏板。你需要更努力地保持平衡，所以需要一些练习来掌握如何使用踏板。但这让骑行轻松多了。结果是，好处是你骑起来更平稳、更省力。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: By the 1880s, another big change was the use of rubber wheels. These became pretty common at that time. Though the first ones were solid rubber, the ride was a good deal more comfortable than the old iron and wood - system. This is a big consideration because the faster you go, the more you feel every bump. Air-filled tyres--"pneumatic tyres"--didn't really come here. That made the ride even more comfortable.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：到了19世纪80年代，另一个重大变化是橡胶轮子的使用。那时这些变得相当普遍。虽然最早的实心橡胶轮胎，但骑行比旧的铁木系统舒服得多。这是一个重要的考量，因为骑得越快，你感受到的每个颠簸就越明显。充气轮胎——“气动轮胎”——并没有真正出现。那让骑行更加舒适。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, by 1890 or so, people were going a lot faster and a lot more smoothly. There was one problem when you were going quickly and comfortably: OH NO HOW DO I STOP?! Yes, we all laugh now. But for a long time, the only way to stop was to drag your feet. That didn't work very well and it would be dangerous if you were going fast. In the crowded cities of those years--New York, Chicago, and so on--you would get killed if you couldn't stop for, say, a streetcar.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：所以，到1890年左右，人们骑得又快又平稳。当你快速舒适地骑行时有一个问题：哦不，我怎么停下来？！是的，我们现在都会笑。但很长一段时间，唯一停下来的办法就是拖脚。那效果不太好，如果你骑得快就会很危险。在那些年拥挤的城市里——纽约、芝加哥等等——如果你不能为比如电车停下来，你会被撞死的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Plus look at this bike. The front wheel is nearly a meter and two-thirds tall! They made them that way so you could see over people and wagons. But, you couldn't drag your feet. This model is called a "velocipede"--a "speed pedal." Another characteristic of the bike in this period is that it has two equal-sized wheels, which signaled a big change in bikes...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：再看看这辆自行车。前轮几乎有1.66米高！他们那样做是为了让你能越过人群和马车。但是，你不能拖脚。这种型号被称为“velocipede”——“速度踏板”。这一时期自行车的另一个特点是它有两个大小相等的轮子，这标志着自行车的一个重大变化……

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: For with the velocipede, brakes appeared. If you wanted to stop, you just pushed the pedal backwards. Doing that stopped the back wheel of the bike. This technique worked a lot better than dragging your feet, or jumping off the high seat there! This meant that bikes became a great deal safer. It would have been safer if people wore helmets, but the first bicycle helmet wasn't invented until years later, and even then it was little more than a leather ballcap. It really wasn't until the 1970s that the bike helmet was modified to provide some real protection.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：因为有了 velocipede，刹车出现了。如果你想停下来，只需向后踩踏板。这样做就会刹住自行车的后轮。这种技术比拖脚或从高高的座位上跳下来好多了！这意味着自行车变得更安全。如果人们戴头盔会更安全，但第一个自行车头盔直到很多年后才被发明，即使那时也不过是一顶皮帽。直到20世纪70年代，自行车头盔才被改进以提供一些真正的保护。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Before continuing on to look at developments since the 1890s, let's say a word more about safety. Everyone knows if you're going downhill, you can get going dangerously fast. To go more than a hundred kilometers an hour isn't all that difficult! But even on level ground it's easy to go too quickly. On a city street, today's bicycles can be ridden at a speed of over forty miles an hour, over a short distance. That's about sixty-four kilometers an hour. Remember you're on a bike, not in a car. There's nothing to protect you. People are killed in single-bicycle accidents every day, just from hitting the road.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在继续探讨19世纪90年代以来的发展之前，让我们再多说几句关于安全的话。大家都知道，如果你下坡，你可能会骑得飞快，非常危险。时速超过一百公里并不是那么难！但即使在平地上也容易骑得太快。在城市街道上，今天的自行车可以在短距离内以超过每小时40英里的速度骑行。那大约是每小时64公里。记住你是在自行车上，不是在汽车里。没有任何东西保护你。每天都有人在单自行车事故中死亡，仅仅是因为撞到路面。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: A good rule to remember is, if you're going faster than the cars: slow down. And please wear a helmet. Nearly one-quarter of the epilepsy cases come from head injuries in accidents on bikes and motorcycles. I didn't mean to scare you, but safety is everyone's business.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：一个好的经验法则是，如果你骑得比汽车还快：减速。请戴上头盔。近四分之一的癫痫病例来自自行车和摩托车事故中的头部受伤。我不是想吓唬你们，但安全是每个人的事情。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: What? Now that's a good question. Why are today's bikes so much faster? Well it's not just that today's athletes are faster. The answer is partly mechanical. If you look closely here, at the back wheel you'll see a number of gears. Changing gears is what makes those fast speeds possible. You can shift gears depending on the terrain and how hard you wish to pedal. So you can put it on a higher gear for downhill, and a lower gear for uphill travel to make it easier to climb that slope. You'll notice this gear-shifting mechanism is attached at the back wheel, and when the rider shifts on the handlebar gear-shifter, the chain moves to the appropriate sprocket. And, speaking of changing gears, let's look over here at our "Tour de France" exhibit...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：什么？这是个好问题。为什么今天的自行车快得多？这不只是因为今天的运动员更快。答案部分是机械方面的。如果你在这里仔细看，在后轮上你会看到许多齿轮。变速让那些高速成为可能。你可以根据地势和你希望踩踏的力度来换挡。所以下坡可以用高挡位，上坡用低挡位，让爬坡更容易。你会注意到这个变速装置连接在后轮上，当骑手在手把变速器上换挡时，链条会移动到相应的链轮上。说到换挡，让我们看看这边的“环法自行车赛”展品……

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello, how may I help you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：你好，我能帮你什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I've been seeing these yellow boxes in front of a lot of houses in my neighborhood. I just wondered what they were for. I noticed your phone number on all of them, so I called. Could you tell me about your business?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：嗯，我看到我家附近很多房子前面都有这些黄色箱子。我只是想知道它们是干什么的。我注意到上面都有你的电话号码，所以就打了。你能告诉我你的业务是什么吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: We do do recycling, but we're not a business. Gaea's Guardians is a non-profit group. We encourage recycling as a way of protecting the environment.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：我们是做回收的，但我们不是企业。盖亚守护者是一个非营利组织。我们鼓励回收，把它作为保护环境的一种方式。

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: I don't know. I mean it is a good idea. But I really don't read the newspaper every day or anything.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：我不太确定。我的意思是这个想法不错。但我真的不是每天都看报纸什么的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: And we don't come collect newspaper every day! In fact, we only do pickups every other week.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：我们也不是每天都来收集报纸！实际上，我们只隔周收一次。

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, well then maybe I could help. I mean in my neighborhood there's too much rubbish lying around everywhere. I'd like to help out, I guess.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：哦，那也许我能帮忙。我的意思是，我家附近到处都是垃圾。我想我愿意帮忙。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's great, sir. You're doing the right thing. OK, I need to get your contact information. What is your name please?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：太好了，先生。你做得对。好的，我需要你的联系方式。请问你叫什么名字？

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Peter Wisrough.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：彼得·维斯罗。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Peter...how do you spell your last name? 'W-I-S-R-O-W'?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：彼得……你的姓怎么拼？‘W-I-S-R-O-W’？

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: No, actually it's 'W-I-S-R-O-U-G-H.'
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：不，实际上是‘W-I-S-R-O-U-G-H’。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, I'm sorry. I'm a terrible speller.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：哦，对不起。我拼写很糟糕。

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: You're a good speller. It's just that my family are terrible pronouncers!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：你拼得很好。只是我家人的发音太糟糕了！

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: You're quite a card, Peter! OK, now what's your address?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：你真是个有趣的人，彼得！好的，你的地址是什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: No. 168, Bridge Road. That's here in London. How about if I have any questions?

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm sending you a copy of our booklet, too. The booklet has our phone number and our e-mail address, helpline@blackcat. com, that's H-E-L-P-L-I-N-E at B-L-A-C-K-C-A-T dot com But, I nearly forgot to ask what's your post code.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：我也会给你寄一份我们的小册子。小册子上有我们的电话号码和电子邮箱地址，helpline@blackcat.com，那是 H-E-L-P-L-I-N-E 在 B-L-A-C-K-C-A-T dot com。但是，我差点忘了问你的邮编是什么。

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: BS97PU. - WOMAN: PS97BU?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：BS97PU。——女士：PS97BU？

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: No. That's 'B' as in 'boy' S 9 7 'P' as in 'Peter' U.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：不。那是‘B’（如boy）S 9 7 ‘P’（如Peter）U。

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, I'm guessing those yellow boxes I saw are for recycled newspapers?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：那么，我猜我看到的那些黄色箱子是用来回收报纸的？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, that is correct, and it's free of charge.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：是的，没错，而且是免费的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wow, that's good news! Do you recycle anything besides newspaper?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：哇，真是好消息！除了报纸，你们还回收其他东西吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh yes, we recycle most everything. Glass, plastic, paper...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：哦是的，我们几乎回收所有东西。玻璃、塑料、纸张……

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, so I can put like glass and plastic bottles in the box?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：哦，那么我可以把玻璃瓶和塑料瓶放进箱子里吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sorry again. Things like that you have to bring to our collection center.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：又得抱歉了。像那样的东西你得送到我们的回收中心。

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: And where is that?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：那在哪里？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Our main center isn't that far from you. It's actually right on the East Side of Central Park.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：我们的总中心离你不远。实际上就在中央公园东侧。

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: That new blue building?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：那栋新的蓝色建筑？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's the one!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：就是那个！

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Cool. Hey, what's with all those different colored boxes outside that place?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：酷。嘿，那个地方外面那些不同颜色的箱子是怎么回事？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, that's for the different materials we recycle. The blue is for metal, the green is for glass and plastics, and the yellow of course is for paper.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：哦，那是为了分装我们回收的不同材料。蓝色是金属，绿色是玻璃和塑料，黄色当然是纸张。

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hm, Okay. I'll try and manage to keep all that straight.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：嗯，好的。我尽力把这些搞清楚。

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh no need, they're each labeled.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：哦不用，每个都贴了标签。

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great. So which one would I put magazines in?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：太好了。那么杂志我应该放哪个里面？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Actually, they don't go in any of the bins. Unfortunately, magazines can't be recycled because of the material they're made of. It's such a waste. So would you be interested in volunteering?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：实际上，它们不属于任何一个桶。不幸的是，杂志不能回收，因为它们所用的材料。真是一种浪费。那么你对做志愿者感兴趣吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Um, I'll think about it. Could you send me some more info?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：嗯，我考虑一下。你能再给我寄些资料吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely. Along with the newspaper box, I'll be sending you our booklet, "Savvy", that is "S-A-double V-Y". It tells you about what you can do to protect the environment in your daily life. Plus it lists things you can do as a volunteer with our group.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：当然。除了报纸箱，我还会给你寄我们的小册子“Savvy”，就是“S-A-double V-Y”。它告诉你日常中能为保护环境做什么。此外，它还列出了你作为我们组织志愿者可以做的事情。

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hey, that's cool, thanks!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：嘿，太酷了，谢谢！

transcriptSentences.speaker: WOMAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: My pleasure. Do you have any other questions or concerns?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：不客气。你还有别的问题或顾虑吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: MAN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Nope, that's it!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：没有了，就这些！

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Welcome everyone to today's seminar on "CV and Interview Skills."
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：欢迎大家参加今天的“简历与面试技巧”研讨会。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Remember: your CV is probably the most important document you will ever write. It opens the door to your career! And that job interview is probably the most important meeting you will ever attend. It's like stepping through that open door. So let's roll up our sleeves and get down to work, shall we?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：记住：你的简历可能是你写过的最重要的文件。它为你打开了职业生涯的大门！而工作面试可能是你参加过的最重要的会议。就像跨过那扇敞开的门。所以让我们卷起袖子开始干吧，好吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: First of all, I cannot possibly tell you everything you need to know about writing a resume in the time we have. But let me tell you that there are dozens of great websites on the Internet. These will give you all the suggestions you need. If you look at the paper I gave you, you will see a list of the dozen most popular sites.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：首先，在我们有限的时间里，我不可能告诉你所有关于写简历你需要知道的东西。但我告诉你，互联网上有几十个很好的网站。这些网站会给你所有你需要的建议。如果你看我给你的那张纸，你会看到十几个最受欢迎网站的列表。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: I can mention a couple of important points, however. One is that your CV or resume should not be too long. A page is about right. Why? HR departments do not have the time to read long documents. Too many people are sending too many CV's! After all, the economic crisis of 2008 is still very much alive. Everyone needs a job now.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：不过我可以提几个要点。一点是，你的简历不应该太长。一页左右比较合适。为什么？人力资源部门没有时间读长篇文件。太多人在寄太多简历了！毕竟，2008年的经济危机依然影响深远。现在每个人都想找到工作。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: No matter how short you make that resume, though, you do not want to forget to tell HR how to contact your references. References are people who will give you a recommendation for a job. That's usually an ex-boss or a professor who knows you well. Do not use relatives! I don't care how much your mum loves you.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：无论你把简历写得多短，你都不想忘了告诉人力资源部如何联系你的推荐人。推荐人是会为你提供工作推荐的人。通常是前任老板或很了解你的教授。不要用亲戚！不管你妈妈多爱你，都不行。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Also, when you send that CV, be sure to include a typed cover letter. A cover letter is a letter where you, basically, are asking for a job. It's like introducing yourself. Make it brief. The real information about you is on that CV of yours. And, please, make sure the letter is typed! It doesn't matter if your handwriting is beautiful or not. Companies only read typed letters. Another point about CV's is you should try to have an attractive layout. Maybe use different type-fonts or colors to highlight information. Some people include a photo. You can find dozens of examples on the Internet. Whatever layout you decide to use, however, avoid all spelling and grammar errors. I used to be an HR manager. If I saw a mistake, that CV went into the garbage.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：另外，当你寄出简历时，一定要附上一封打印的求职信。求职信基本上就是你求职的信。就像是自我介绍。要简短。关于你的真实信息都在简历上。还有，请确保信是打印的！你的字写得好不好看没关系。公司只读打印的信。关于简历的另一点是，你应该尝试有一个吸引人的版面设计。也许用不同的字体或颜色来突出信息。有些人会附上照片。你可以在网上找到很多例子。但无论你决定使用什么版面设计，都要避免拼写和语法错误。我以前是人力资源经理。如果我看到一个错误，那份简历就会进垃圾桶。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Something you write in a CV is a description of your skills and experiences in an interesting way. Mention training, too. I mean these are what get you hired! Do not just say, "I have lots of experience." Or, "I have many skills." Tell that boss what you did, for what company, and when. Better, tell him how well you did it! Don't just say, "I sold houses." Say, "I sold two million pounds worth of houses in my first year." That is, say something to make the person reading excited and curious.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：你在简历中要写的是以有趣的方式描述你的技能和经验。也要提到培训。我的意思是，这些是让你被录用的关键！不要只说“我有丰富经验”或“我有许多技能”。告诉老板你做了什么，为哪家公司，什么时候。更好的是，告诉他你做得有多好！不要只说“我卖房子”。要说“我在第一年卖了价值两百万英镑的房子”。也就是说，说一些让读者感到兴奋和好奇的话。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Finally, speaking of CV's, it's sad. But some people actually forget to provide a contact number. That's pretty silly. You wrote a great CV, you have HR dying to meet you...and they don't know how. You forgot your phone number! Oh sure, if you apply online, they have your e-mail address. But you just showed them you're forgetful. Why are they going to want to talk to you after that?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：最后，说到简历，很遗憾。但有些人确实忘了提供联系电话。那很愚蠢。你写了一封很棒的简历，你让HR迫不及待想见你……但他们不知道方式。你忘了你的电话号码！哦当然，如果你在线申请，他们有你的电子邮箱。但你刚刚向他们展示了你的健忘。那之后他们为什么还想和你谈？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Alright, moving on to the actual interview, I'll go over what you need to know by the end of it, and what you can discuss and negotiate on later once it looks like you'll be offered the job. First there's working hours. It's not that necessary to hammer out the hours off the bat, especially since it's easy to come off as lazy when the first thing you bring up is how much you're going to have to work. You can also find out more about possible promotions later on. It is important, however, to get a feel for how much you'll be paid. You should make sure the salary range is commensurate with what you're worth, and if you're not you can move on to better opportunities. Being sure you're going to make what you want to live on is much more important than issues like your pension - you're all so young pension is not going to matter for quite a long time.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：好的，接下来进入面试本身。我会过一遍面试结束前你需要知道的内容，以及一旦看起来你会被录用之后你可以讨论和协商的事项。首先是工作时间。没必要一开始就敲定工作时间，尤其是如果你最先提到的是你得工作多长时间，容易给人懒惰的印象。你也可以晚些再了解可能的晋升机会。然而，重要的是要了解你的薪酬水平。你应该确保薪资范围与你的价值相匹配，如果不匹配，你可以转向更好的机会。确保你能赚到维持生活所需比养老金之类的问题重要得多——你们都还年轻，养老金在很长一段时间内都不重要。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: You should find out about what skills you must know for the job, and what they'll teach you. In addition, if the company will provide training, you should find out how long the training period is and whether it is paid. Beware of any jobs that want you to train for a long time without appropriate compensation.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：你应该了解这份工作你必须具备哪些技能，以及他们会教你什么。此外，如果公司提供培训，你应该了解培训期有多长以及是否带薪。警惕那些让你长时间培训却没有适当报酬的工作。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Speaking of compensation, find out about holidays as well. Do you get paid vacation time? Are you allowed to take personal days? Do you have to work on national holidays?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：说到报酬，也要了解假期。有带薪假期吗？允许请事假吗？法定假日需要工作吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Once you work out these main issues you can move on later to details like the location and expected attire and whatnot.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：一旦你解决了这些主要问题，你可以稍后再处理细节，比如工作地点、着装要求等等。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wow, that's a lot of information! Let's take a break so you can think everything over and ask any questions you may have. Don't hesitate to come see me if you need any clarification on all this stuff!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：哇，信息量真大！我们休息一下，这样你们可以好好想想，并提出你们可能有的问题。如果你们对这一切需要任何澄清，尽管来找我！

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello, are you Dr. Lindsey? The Returning Students Advisor?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：你好，你是林赛博士吗？返校生顾问？

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, that's right. Are you Frank? Your appointment wasn't till 2:00, but that's OK. Please come in and have a seat.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：是的，没错。你是弗兰克？你的预约是两点，但没关系。请进来坐。

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Thanks, I like to arrive early whenever I have anything to do.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：谢谢，我无论做什么事都喜欢早到。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's certainly a praiseworthy habit. Let me see, it looks like you've taken a long break from school, and I understand you wanted to have a chat about what you should study if and when you return for further classes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：这当然是个值得称赞的习惯。让我看看，看来你休学了很久，我了解到你想聊聊如果你回来继续上课，应该学什么。

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: It's such a big challenge. I don't know if I'm crazy for doing this or not!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：这是个巨大的挑战。我不知道我这么做是不是疯了！

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: Believe it or not, I know exactly what you mean. Before I began working here at the university, I taught primary school for nearly ten years. It takes a lot of courage to go back to school!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：信不信由你，我完全明白你的意思。在来这里工作之前，我在小学教了将近十年书。重返校园需要很大的勇气！

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: I feel more shy and scared than the primary students I teach! In the schools I taught, I found today's youngsters are very sure of themselves. In terms of intelligence, I have a lot to teach them. And the maturity level of much of my class leaves something to be desired. But in terms of confidence, wow! A lot more confident than I am now, that's for sure!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：我比我教的小学生还要害羞和害怕！在我教过的学校里，我发现现在的年轻人非常自信。在智力方面，我有很多东西可以教他们。而且我班上大多数学生的成熟度还有待提高。但在自信方面，哇！肯定比我现在自信多了！

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: Stop fretting. "A brave man is a coward who refuses to run." Let's talk about your strong points. You seem an intelligent man. What is it you would you like to study?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：别担心了。“勇敢的人是不愿逃跑的懦夫。”我们来谈谈你的长处。你看起来很聪明。你想学什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: You see, I've been teaching children for a few years, but I think I'd be happier teaching adults.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：你看，我教了几年孩子，但我觉得教成人会更快乐。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: I think teaching students in middle school is much more satisfying because they end up being much more grateful for your work. If I may ask, what got you interested in teaching adults?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：我认为教中学生更有成就感，因为他们最终会对你的工作更加感激。我可以问一下，是什么让你对教成人产生兴趣？

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: A lot of things, I guess. I met my future wife back in my first year of college. She always complains that I was more interesting then. She says that now I talk like I'm seven years old! That's probably from being with children all day.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：我想有很多原因。我大学第一年就认识了我未来的妻子。她总是抱怨那时的我更有趣。她说现在我说起话来像个七岁小孩！那大概是因为整天和孩子待在一起。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: Ha, ha, ha! Again I know just what you mean. My husband used to say the same thing about me when I taught kindergarten. Anything else?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：哈哈哈！我又完全明白你的意思了。我教幼儿园的时候，我丈夫也这么说我。还有别的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, yes. Fairly often now I run into former students and we talk. Some of them are getting close to being grown up. I guess I think more and more about how people develop over time. So, I'm interested in the results of education, you know. The final stages.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：嗯，有的。现在我经常遇到以前的学生，我们会聊天。他们有些人快成年了。我想我越来越关注人是如何随着时间发展的。所以我对教育的结果感兴趣，你知道，就是最后阶段。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: I see. Well, coming back to the university can be both difficult and very rewarding. There are some problems unique to returning students, you know, older students like yourself. What do you think is your greatest weakness?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：我明白了。重返大学既困难又很有收获。返校生有一些独有的问题，你知道，像你这样年龄较大的学生。你认为你最大的弱点是什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I actually think my confidence is getting better. I'm definitely overcoming my introversion and starting to be much more comfortable in front of a class. To say the truth, I'm afraid I'm rather behind the times about many things. It's more difficult for me to chase after the popular things youngsters are fond of - such as Iphone, Twitter, if you name it!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：嗯，实际上我认为我的自信心在提高。我肯定在克服内向，开始在课堂上感到自在多了。说实话，恐怕我在很多事情上落伍了。我比较难去追赶年轻人喜欢的东西——比如苹果手机、推特之类的！

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: I think I understand.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：我想我理解。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: How old are you, 35? People at your age still go back to school for further education. I was a bit the same way. I mean I didn't study at the university till after I had a family: a husband and one child. My point of view was a lot different from your average eighteen year old girl's, I can tell you!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：你多大了，35岁？你这个年纪的人还是有人重返校园进修的。我也有点像这样。我是说，我直到有了家庭——丈夫和一个孩子——才上大学。我的观点和普通18岁女孩很不一样，我可以告诉你！

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Gee, that sounds pretty rough. A family and college? Clearly you weren't unsuccessful though!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：哎呀，听起来很不容易。家庭和大学？不过你显然没有不成功！

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: It was, Frank. It truly was. My first term at school was extremely stressful. But excuse me! You're not here to listen to my life story. We're talking about your plans. Is there anything unique I should know about you or your past experience or plans?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：确实不容易，弗兰克。真的。我第一个学期压力非常大。但不好意思！你不是来听我讲人生故事的。我们在谈你的计划。有什么特别的关于你或你的过去经历或计划是我需要知道的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm afraid not. There is nothing interesting about my career or plans. It's really not too impressive.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：恐怕没有。我的职业或计划没什么有趣的。真的不太出彩。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, I forbid you to talk like that. This is your one life and if you're not interested, why bother living it? Don't be so humble, Frank.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：好了，我不许你这么说。这是你仅有的一次生命，如果你都不感兴趣，那活着还有什么意思？别这么谦虚，弗兰克。

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, OK. My wife says I'm a wimp.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：好吧，好吧。我妻子说我是一个懦夫。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: Let's talk about your dreams a bit. You want to teach adults, you said. What would you like to teach them?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：我们来谈谈你的梦想吧。你说你想教成人。你想教他们什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, when I first came to college I really liked Languages and Literature. A lot of people have told me that for practical reasons it would be more rewarding to choose Business Management as my major, but I made up my mind to study Liberal Arts once I got the idea of going back to school.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：嗯，我第一次上大学时真的很喜欢语言和文学。很多人告诉我，出于实际原因，选择工商管理作为我的专业会更有回报，但我一旦有了回学校的想法，就下定决心学文科。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: I must say it's refreshing to meet someone who knows there's more to an education than computers and finance. Let's have a look at the university course catalogue--
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：我必须说，遇到一个懂得教育不只是计算机和金融的人，真是令人耳目一新。我们来看看大学课程目录——

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Excuse me, Dr. Lindsey. Before we do that, could I maybe ask you some questions about changes in university life? I think I need to discuss that so I know what to expect.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：打断一下，林赛博士。在我们看之前，我能不能先问你一些关于大学生活变化的问题？我想我需要讨论一下，这样我才知道该期待什么。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR. LINDSEY
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course. I'm here to help you. The biggest thing to get used to is the change in technology. Professors present things on huge screens, many of which are interactive computerized whiteboards. You can write on them still, and use them like a touch screen. They're really handy! No more sloppy scribbled notes on the projector. Let's see, I doubt you'll be living in student housing, so I won't go into all the improvements there. Another major change that you'll enjoy is the plethora of resources available for students. As a student you have 24-hour access to the gym, and library privileges that include the use of school computers to scan, copy, and print, and of course the Media Library, which contains movies from all genres, and most of the movies listed on AFI's Top 100 Movies of All Time. The dining facilities are also not what they used to be. They offer choices for all diets and you can expect a hot meal any time of day.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 林赛博士：当然。我是来帮你的。最需要适应的是技术的变化。教授们在巨大的屏幕上展示内容，其中许多是交互式电脑白板。你仍然可以在上面写字，像触摸屏一样使用。非常方便！不再有投影仪上潦草的笔记了。让我想想，我猜你不会住在学生宿舍，所以我不多讲那里的改进了。另一个你会喜欢的主要变化是学生可利用的资源非常丰富。作为学生，你可以24小时使用健身房，还有图书馆特权，包括使用学校电脑扫描、复印和打印，当然还有媒体图书馆，里面有各种类型的电影，以及AFI评选的史上百部经典电影中的大部分。餐饮设施也今非昔比了。他们提供适合各种饮食的选择，你一天中的任何时候都能吃到热饭。

transcriptSentences.speaker: FRANK
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wow, things really have changed! I'll be sure to utilize all those great facilities in my time here. Thanks for all your help, Dr. Lindsey. I think that's all the questions I have for now.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 弗兰克：哇，真的变了！我一定会在我的时间里好好利用所有这些好设施。谢谢你的帮助，林赛博士。我想我现在的问题就这些了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK and welcome back. During the short break we just took, several of you approached me with questions. So, before going on with the orientation talk, I'd like to address those queries. As I've found, if one person asks a question, probably a dozen others are wondering about the same thing!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：好的，欢迎回来。在我们刚刚短暂的休息时间，你们当中有几个人带着问题来找我。所以，在继续迎新讲座之前，我想回答这些问题。根据我的经验，如果有一个人问问题，很可能还有十几个人也在想同样的事情！

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The first question is whether Wassamatta U. employs modules technology as an instruction method. The answer is yes, we do. At least that's what the university catalogue says. If some of you don't understand what "modules" means, you probably won't be surprised to learn that not many people seem to know, including myself. I looked it up. Apparently, though, it's a method of broadband, wireless access. At least that's what an American company's website told me. But again, don't worry. If you need to know something more, your professor can tell you.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：第一个问题是沃萨马塔大学是否采用模块技术作为教学方法。答案是是的。至少大学目录上是这么说的。如果你们中有些人不懂“模块”是什么意思，你们可能不会惊讶于包括我自己在内，没有多少人似乎知道。我查了一下。不过显然，这是一种宽带无线接入方式。至少我是从一家美国公司的网站上看到的。不过再说一次，别担心。如果你需要了解更多，你的教授会告诉你的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Another question someone asked me was what tomorrow's workshop on "Research Methods and Skills" was about. Well, research skills include any method you can imagine for finding and presenting any information you need. That's not just schoolwork either. Writing English--the native language for most of you--and finding a job are also research skills. And, yes, those will be addressed in tomorrow's workshop.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：另一个人问我的是明天的“研究方法与技巧”研讨班是关于什么的。嗯，研究技能包括你能想到的任何查找和展示你需要的信息的方法。那不仅仅是作业。写英语——你们大多数人的母语——和找工作也是研究技能。是的，这些都会在明天的研讨班上讲到。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: As you know, Wassamatta U. is one of this country's premiere universities for the study of "the dismal science", economics. Some of you, it seems, want to get a jump on their classmates. During the break, half a dozen of you came up and asked me where to find economics tomes. I know it's odd, but this school's library holdings are divided up between two libraries. Economics books are in the old library. If you look out of the window behind me, you can see it. It's the red brick building.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：如你所知，沃萨马塔大学是这个国家研究“阴郁科学”——经济学的顶尖大学之一。有些人似乎想领先于他们的同学。休息期间，有六个人过来问我经济学大部头在哪里能找到。我知道这很奇怪，但学校的藏书分布在两个图书馆之间。经济学书籍在旧图书馆。如果你看我身后的窗外，你可以看到它。就是那栋红砖建筑。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, before I forget, you economics types also need a lot of math, am I right? Well, those math books are neither in the old library nor in the new one. They can be found in the Math Department Building. Why am I telling you this? Doesn't "the Invisible Hand" guide economists? Maybe it's good you asked: in 2008, that Hand shoved most of the world economy off a cliff, didn't it?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：哦，趁我还没忘，你们这些学经济的也需要大量数学，对吧？那些数学书既不在旧图书馆也不在新图书馆。它们在数学系大楼。我为什么要告诉你这个？“看不见的手”难道不引导经济学家吗？也许你问得好：2008年，那只手把世界经济的大部分推下了悬崖，不是吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now I realize that most of you couldn't bring a computer printer or a photocopier from home. So I'm sure you're already wondering where you can copy things like term papers, Internet articles, and things like that. I have some good news and some bad news. The good news is that there are a number of places you can make copies. These include both libraries and the Student Union Building.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：现在我意识到你们大多数人不能从家里带电脑打印机或复印机。所以我肯定你们已经在想哪里可以复印期末论文、网络文章之类的东西。我有好消息也有坏消息。好消息是有很多地方可以复印。包括图书馆和学生活动中心。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now the bad news: I am sorry to say, most classroom buildings and academic departments do not have copiers students can use. So most of the large buildings you see around campus do NOT have copiers for students. The copiers there are reserved for professors and office staff. Oh, yes! I nearly forget to tell you. If you need to have printing done, all the copiers available to students are laser printers. Plus, for your convenience, you can pay using prepaid cards. You can get those in the Student Union Building.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：坏消息是：很遗憾，大多数教学楼和院系没有学生可以使用的复印机。所以你在校园里看到的大部分大型建筑都没有学生复印机。那里的复印机是给教授和办公室员工用的。哦对了！我差点忘了告诉你。如果需要打印，所有学生可用的复印机都是激光打印机。另外，为了方便你们，可以使用预付费卡支付。可以在学生活动中心买到。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: That just covers the questions put to me. If you have more, please see me during the next break at 2:15. Right now, though, I'd like to start to give you a run down on the various facilities here on campus. That way you won't get lost so easily in the weeks to come.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：这些只是回答了大家提出的问题。如果还有问题，请在下午2：15的下一次休息时间找我。但现在，我想开始给你们介绍一下校园里的各种设施。这样在接下来的几周里你们就不会那么容易迷路了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: I have been told that this year's incoming class features a large number of married students and parents. So you must be wondering where to put the baby while you're in class. OK, right now, we are in the Student Union Building, right? Remember the big doors in front where you all came in? If you go out of the building, you can see the Nursery is just on the other side of this building. It's only about twenty meters away! Convenient, eh?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我被告知今年入学的新生中有很多已婚学生和家长。所以你们一定在想上课时把孩子放在哪里。好的，现在我们在学生活动中心，对吧？还记得你们进来的那扇大门吗？如果你出去，可以看到托儿所就在这栋楼对面。只有大约二十米远！很方便吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Next, we're all from different places around the country. Some of you are from other countries. That means we're pretty likely to get sick during the first months of school as we expose each other to many new viruses. So, where's the doctor? Of course, you need to find the Medical Services Center which is on the right as you leave the building. Remember, that's the second building on the right.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：接下来，我们都来自全国各地。有些来自其他国家。这意味着在开学的头几个月里，我们很可能生病，因为我们彼此接触许多新病毒。那么，医生在哪里？当然，你需要找到医疗服务中心，就在你出这栋楼时右边。记住，那是右边第二栋楼。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: And if you look out of that window, you can see a lot of antennae and satellite dishes on the roof. So that's what we call the Media Center. Yeah, I know, I think it's confusing too. The Media Center is next to the Medical Center. The chairwoman of the Journalism School on the first floor doesn't like it when people who wander in there mistake her for a nurse!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：如果你看那扇窗户，可以看到屋顶上有许多天线和卫星锅。那就是我们说的媒体中心。是的，我知道，我也觉得容易混淆。媒体中心在医疗中心旁边。一楼新闻学院的院长不喜欢有人逛进去把她错当成护士！

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Chances are you'll have at least one math class while you're here. That red building there just outside to the left is the Math Department Building. I know, it looks about as old as the subject as math, but I assure you that the inside is equipped with state-of-the-art classroom equipment including interactive chalkboards and surround sound in every room.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：你们在这里期间很可能至少会修一门数学课。左边那栋红色建筑就是数学系大楼。我知道，它看起来和数学这门学科一样古老，但我向你保证，里面配备了最先进的教室设备，包括交互式黑板和每间教室的环绕音响。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, can you see the back building there? Yes, behind the Media Center. Quite new, isn't it? That's the new library, just decorated. They're back-to-back, you might say. If you look just to the left of it at the lower, older looking building you'll find the old library. It's nice and quiet - perfect for those marathon study sessions during exam week. Since the weather is so nice, why don't we stop looking at our maps but go for a walk around the campus?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：哦，你能看到后面的建筑吗？是的，在媒体中心后面。很新，对吧？那是新图书馆，刚装修好。你可以说它们是背靠背的。如果看它左边那栋较矮、看起来老一些的建筑，你会发现旧图书馆。那里又舒适又安静——考试周那些长时间学习的最佳场所。既然天气这么好，我们不如放下地图，一起去校园里走走？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good Afternoon and welcome to Habitat Hunters. You must be Joseph.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：下午好，欢迎来到 Habitat Hunters。您一定是约瑟夫。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, that's right. You said on the phone that I could come by at 2:00. Sorry, I'm a little early.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：是的，没错。您在电话里说我可以在两点钟过来。抱歉，我早到了一点点。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: No problem at all: In Calgary's market, you have to move fast if you want a good apartment!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：完全没问题：在卡尔加里的房产市场上，要想租到好公寓，就得动作快！

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Actually, I'd settle for almost anything. I've been here ten days and the hotel is ruining me. My father has me on a strict budget.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：实际上，我几乎什么都凑合。我在这里已经十天了，酒店开销快把我掏空了。我父亲给我定了严格的开支预算。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sit right down here now, sir. Let's talk a little about the places before we go have a look. Now, we have four apartments available.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：先生，您先请坐。在去看房之前，我们先聊聊这几处房子。我们现在有四套公寓可供出租。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, could you tell me more about these four apartments?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：好的，您能详细介绍一下这四套公寓吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure. The first one is on Beatle Road, just a block off campus. It's a 3-bedroom with a bathroom and a living room and a great Italian restaurant right next to it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：当然。第一套在披头士路，离校园就一个街区。是三居室，带一个卫生间和一个客厅，旁边还有一家很棒的意大利餐厅。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: How much?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：多少钱？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, it's $435 a month including Internet and utilities.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：每月435美元，包括网费和杂费。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Okay, that sounds reasonable. Any drawbacks to the house?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：好的，听起来挺合理。这套房子有什么缺点吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: There's a really big garden, but it hasn't been taken care of over the years and is just too big to clean up nicely.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：有一个非常大的花园，但多年来没好好打理，太大了，没办法好好清理出来。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hmm. That sounds Okay; tell me about the next option.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：嗯。听起来还行；说说下一个选项吧。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: The other 3-bedroom apartment is on Oakington Avenue on campus. It is right near the building where you have classes, and the kitchen and living room are newly furnished.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：另一套三居室公寓在校内的奥金顿大道上，紧挨着你上课的教学楼，厨房和客厅是新装修配了家具的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wow, that sounds like a pretty good option.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：哇，听起来是个很不错的选择。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well it is a cool apartment, but since it's a dormitory, the living room, bathroom, kitchen, and washing machine are all shared. It would be nice not to have to buy living room furniture, though.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：嗯，公寓是不错，但因为是宿舍，客厅、卫生间、厨房和洗衣机都是共用的。不过，不用自己买客厅家具倒是挺好的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: And how much is this one?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：那这套多少钱？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: $400 per month for a bedroom with an air conditioner. For a bedroom without an air conditioner, you would pay less, $340, for it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：带空调的卧室每月400美元。不带空调的卧室就便宜一些，340美元。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yikes, even with the air conditioner it sounds really inconvenient to have to share facilities. I'll never cook if I have to walk down the hall to use the kitchen.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：哎呀，就算有空调，要共用设施听起来也太不方便了。如果要走过走廊才能用厨房，那我肯定不会做饭。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, that's true.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：是啊，说的也是。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Anyway, the next place is a 2-bedroom on Mead Street.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：不管怎样，下一套是米德街上的两居室。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, I like Mead Street - that's off campus, right?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：哦，我喜欢米德街——那是在校外，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yep. It's pretty cool, but it has only 2 bedrooms, plus a living room and a study.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：是的。很不错，但只有两间卧室，外加一个客厅和一个书房。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: But I want to live together with my two friends.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：但我想和我的两个朋友住在一起。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: So you could make the study into a small bedroom if you end up living with them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：所以如果你们三个人合租的话，你可以把书房改成一间小卧室。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Also, we guys will want a TV and DVD player since we're all so much into movies.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：还有，我们男生肯定会想要电视和DVD播放机，因为我们都很爱看电影。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, this place has a great TV and VCR, but no DVD player.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：嗯，这套房子有一台很好的电视和录像机，但没有DVD播放机。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: No DVD? That's so weird. Are any other facilities provided?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：没有DVD？太奇怪了。还提供其他设施吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: As you said, weird enough, it also comes with a washbasin.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：正如你所说，确实够奇怪的，它还有一个洗脸盆。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Is there a washing machine? I think we need that more than just a washbasin.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：有洗衣机吗？我觉得我们更需要洗衣机，而不是洗脸盆。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm afraid there's no washing machine in the apartment.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：恐怕公寓里没有洗衣机。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wow, that's so old-fashioned! Maybe it's not the best choice for three college guys. How much is it?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：哇，这也太老派了！可能对三个大学生来说不是最佳选择。多少钱？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well it's $600 per month, but of course it would be cheaper if you made it into 3 bedrooms instead of 2.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：每月600美元，不过当然，如果你把它改成三间卧室而不是两间，就会便宜一些。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Where is this apartment located?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：这套公寓位置在哪里？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: It's 2500 Mead Street, where there are a lot of bars.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：米德街2500号，那里有很多酒吧。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: It would be affordable, but it would get pretty noisy. And that sounds really expensive for an old place in a noisy area. How about the last place?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：价格还能接受，但肯定会很吵。而且在这么吵的地方，老房子还这么贵。最后一个地方呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: This one's on-campus in the Devon Close complex. It's a one-bedroom, so it will be a little quieter than the Mead Street place.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：这个在校内的德文小区，是一居室，所以会比米德街那套安静一些。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: One bedroom, huh? That could be good for focusing on my studies. What else does it have?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：一居室，嗯？那可能有助于我专心学习。还有什么设施？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: It comes with a living room and a study, and includes a really nice lamp in the study that has a bunch of different settings. You know what else is cool? There's a dining hall downstairs so all evening meals are free. You can purchase breakfast and lunch, but meals after 6 p.m. are free.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：配有一个客厅和一个书房，书房里有一盏非常漂亮的灯，有各种不同的亮度设置。你知道还有什么很酷的吗？楼下有个食堂，所以所有晚餐都是免费的。你可以自己买早餐和午餐，但下午6点以后的餐食免费。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wow, this place sounds too good to be true. Is it really expensive?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：哇，这个地方听起来好得令人难以置信。真的很贵吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: It's alright - $500 per month, but there's no bathroom.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：还好——每月500美元，但没有卫生间。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: WHAT? No bathroom?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：什么？没有卫生间？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, there's no bathroom in the apartment but there's one at the end of the hall.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：嗯，公寓里没有卫生间，但走廊尽头有一个。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hmm. Thanks, I think now I just have to decide whether I want to live alone or not.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：嗯。谢谢，我想现在我得决定要不要一个人住了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, which one do you prefer?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：嗯，你更喜欢哪个？

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: I think I'd choose either this apartment or the one on Beatle Road.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：我想我会选择这套或者披头士路那套。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK. You'd better think about it, and then you can contact me ASAP.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：好的。你最好考虑一下，然后尽快联系我。

transcriptSentences.speaker: RENTER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Fine, thanks for your help!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 租客：好的，谢谢你的帮助！

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: You're welcome...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：不客气……

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hi folks, my name is Loretta Johnston, and I'm here from the Baltimore Department of Public Waste. Thank you for coming out to our community meeting tonight. I've got a few words to say about the waste collection here in Baltimore.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家好，我叫洛蕾塔·约翰斯顿，来自巴尔的摩公共废弃物部门。感谢大家今晚来参加我们的社区会议。我想就巴尔的摩的垃圾收集工作说几句话。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: First there's the sorted collection bins themselves. They're made of sturdy, solid material so none of your trash can seep out, or puncture the bin. Also, since these things sit out on the curb overnight rain or shine, they have to be waterproof. We can't have water getting up in it and filling up the bin. Remember to pay attention to which bin is which, and sort your waste accordingly. You should have a blue or green bin for recyclable garbage, a yellow bin for unrecyclable garbage, and a red bin for toxic waste.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：首先是分类收集桶本身。它们用坚固耐用的材料制成，不会让垃圾渗漏出来，也不会被戳破。此外，由于这些桶要放在路边过夜，无论刮风下雨，所以必须防水。不能让水进到桶里灌满。记住要分清哪个桶是装什么的，相应地对垃圾进行分类。你们应该有蓝色或绿色的桶装可回收垃圾，黄色的桶装不可回收垃圾，红色的桶装有毒废弃物。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Our city-wide waste management is divided into two services. The first is commercial waste collection, or trash collection from buildings. The majority of building waste is paper, which goes in the blue or green bins. You'll notice in your office buildings there are signs that warn you not to overfill these bins. All that paper adds up, and an overflowing bin is infinitely harder for collectors to carry to the truck and empty.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我们全市的废弃物管理分为两种服务。第一种是商业垃圾收集，也就是从建筑物收集垃圾。大部分建筑垃圾是纸张，放在蓝色或绿色桶里。你们会注意到办公楼里有标志提醒不要装得太满。纸张累积起来量很大，满溢出来的桶对收集人员来说，搬运到卡车上倒掉要难得多。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Aside from paper, another large source of building waste is metals. Metals such as tin and aluminum can be put in the yellow recycle bins, but metals like lead and copper should be disposed of in the red bins. These heavy metals are harmful to the environment and exacerbate our city's existing pollution problem.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：除了纸张，建筑垃圾的另一大来源是金属。锡和铝之类的金属可以放进黄色回收桶，但铅和铜之类的金属应该放进红色桶。这些重金属对环境有害，还会加剧我们城市已有的污染问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's about all the information you need for building waste. Moving on to the second service, household waste collection is probably what you primarily think of when you think of what we do here... Many of the same guidelines apply - the sorting is the same, etcetera. Please remember to keep garbage like kitchen waste in a plastic bag. It makes collection easier and lessens the abominable rotten-trash smell.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：关于建筑垃圾，这些就是你需要知道的了。转到第二种服务，家庭垃圾收集可能才是你们主要想到的我们所做的工作……很多同样的规则适用——分类是一样的，等等。请记住，像厨房垃圾这样的垃圾要用塑料袋装好。这样收集起来更方便，也能减轻那种难闻的腐烂垃圾气味。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: So after we take your trash away, what happens to it? We take all the garbage to one of a number of garbage disposal plants, each of which is located in the middle of an open space of some sort. No one wants to have their home or office right next door to a waste disposal plant, right? Waste is collected and then disposed of once every four weeks. A lot of trash can build up in that time, so we're in the process of developing a plan to fund collection more frequently. Ideally it would be collected weekly, but we will likely have to settle for biweekly. The garbage trucks make their rounds to clear the bins at night in order to avoid traffic.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：那么我们把垃圾收走之后，会发生什么？我们把所有垃圾送到多个垃圾处理厂之一，每个厂都位于某种空旷区域的中心。没人希望自己的家或办公室紧挨着垃圾处理厂，对吧？垃圾每四周收集并处理一次。这段时间内会积攒大量垃圾，所以我们正在制定一个计划，筹集资金来更频繁地收集。理想情况是每周收集一次，但可能不得不满足于两周一次。垃圾车在夜间进行清运，以避开交通拥堵。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm sure you've seen how much waste your own household produces in a given week. Now imagine all the trash produced by all the households in Baltimore. It's a lot, right? It may surprise you that this amount is only marginal compared to commercial waste. Yep, the main waste producers are actually businesses, industrial facilities, retail, and offices. Hard to believe humans produce that much waste, right? No wonder we have pollution problems!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我相信你们都见过自己家一周会产生多少垃圾。现在想象一下巴尔的摩所有家庭产生的所有垃圾。很多，对吧？但可能让你惊讶的是，这个量与商业垃圾相比只是很小的一部分。是的，主要的垃圾生产者其实是企业、工业设施、零售店和办公室。很难相信人类会产生那么多垃圾，对吧？难怪我们有污染问题！

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Anyway, after all incoming waste is sorted, recyclables are sent to a recycling plant while garbage and toxic waste are transported to their respective areas of the plant for treatment. Items such as stones, which should not be disposed of in our bins, are separated out and discarded.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：总之，所有运来的垃圾经过分类后，可回收物被送到回收厂，而垃圾和有毒废弃物被送到厂内各自的区域进行处理。像石头这类不应该扔进我们桶里的物品，会被分离出来丢弃。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Once the trash has undergone the treatment process, it is compacted and disposed of with all the other trash and finally, when the landfill space is full, it is buried deep underground and in time something new is built on the land.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：垃圾经过处理流程后，会被压缩，和其他垃圾一起进行处置。最后，当填埋场空间填满时，就会被深埋在地下，过一段时间后，土地上会建起新的东西。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's everything about waste collection, thank you for listening. Are there any questions?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：关于垃圾收集就是这些了，谢谢大家的聆听。有问题吗？
