transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Tonight I'm going to present an overview of the research on amber. Okay, I'll start by giving a brief introduction about amber, then talk about the formation of amber, and then describe amber's applications in different fields.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：今晚我将概述关于琥珀的研究。好的，我先简单介绍一下琥珀，然后谈谈琥珀的形成，接着描述琥珀在不同领域的应用。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: First of all, what is amber? Amber is not a stone, but is ancient, fossilised tree resin, which is the semi-solid amorphous organic substance secreted in pockets and canals through epithelial cells of the plant. And why is resin produced? Although there are contrasting views as to why resin is produced, it is a plant's protection mechanism. The resin may be produced to protect the tree from disease and injury inflicted by insects and fungi.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：首先，什么是琥珀？琥珀不是石头，而是古老的、石化的树脂，是一种半固体的无定形有机物质，通过植物的上皮细胞分泌在囊状体和管道中。那么树脂为什么会产生？虽然关于树脂产生的原因有不同观点，但它是植物的保护机制。树脂产生可能是为了保护树木免受昆虫和真菌造成的疾病和伤害。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Amber occurs in a range of different colors. Besides the usual yellow, orange, and brown, other uncommon colors are also associated with it. Interestingly, blue amber, the rarest Dominican amber, is highly sought after. It is only found in Santiago, Dominican Republic. There are several theories about what causes the blue color in amber. The most common one links it to the occurrence of volcanic dust that was present when the resin was first pressed out from hymenaca protera millions of years ago.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：琥珀有多种不同的颜色。除了常见的黄色、橙色和棕色，还有其他不常见的颜色。有趣的是，最罕见的多米尼加蓝琥珀非常受欢迎。它只在多米尼加共和国的圣地亚哥被发现。关于琥珀为什么会呈现蓝色有多种理论。最常见的一种认为这与数百万年前树脂首次从古植物中挤出时存在的火山灰有关。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: At this point, you might be curious about how amber is formed. Molecular polymerisation, resulting from high pressures and temperatures produced by overlying sediment, transforms the resin first into copal. Sustained heat and pressure drives off terpenes and results in the formation of amber. Copal that I've just mentioned is also a tree resin but it hasn't fully fossilised to amber. More generally, the term copal describes resinous substances in an intermediate stage of polymerisation and hardening between "gummier" resins and amber.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：这时候，你们可能对琥珀是如何形成的好奇。分子聚合——由上覆沉积物产生的高压高温导致——首先将树脂转化为柯巴脂。持续的热量和压力驱除萜烯，最终形成琥珀。我刚才提到的柯巴脂也是一种树脂，但它尚未完全石化为琥珀。更普遍地说，柯巴脂这个术语描述的是处于“更粘稠”树脂和琥珀之间的聚合与硬化中间阶段的树脂物质。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: So where can we find amber? It can be found on sea shores. The main producer worldwide is Russia. In fact about 90% of the world's available amber is located in the Kaliningrad region of Russia, which is located on the Baltic. Here, the resin is washed up on the coast after being dislodged from the ocean floor by years of water and ocean currents. However, exposure to sunlight, rain, and temperate extremes tends to disintegrate resin. This also indicates that amber is not really an ideal fossil preservative for most uses.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：那么我们在哪里能找到琥珀？它可以在海滩上找到。全球主要产地是俄罗斯。事实上，世界上约90%的可开采琥珀位于俄罗斯的加里宁格勒地区，该地区地处波罗的海沿岸。在那里，树脂经过多年水流和洋流作用从海底被冲上海岸。然而，暴露在阳光、雨水和极端温度下往往会使树脂分解。这也说明琥珀并非大多数用途的理想化石保存剂。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: We've already learned that amber is made of tree resin. It often includes insects that were trapped within the tree many millions of years ago. A piece with a visible and well-arranged insect is generally valued much higher than simple, solid amber. One Dominican amber source reported finding a butterfly with a five-inch wing spread; this is both a large and unusual find; most butterfly specimens have no more than a two-inch wingspan. Inclusions in Dominican amber are numerous - 1 inclusion to every 100 pieces; Baltic amber contains approximately 1 inclusion to every 1,000 pieces.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我们已经知道琥珀由树脂制成。它常常包含数百万年前被困在树中的昆虫。一块含有可见且排列良好的昆虫的琥珀通常比普通实心琥珀价值高得多。一个多米尼加琥珀来源曾报告发现一只翅展5英寸的蝴蝶；这是一个既大又不寻常的发现；大多数蝴蝶标本翅展不超过2英寸。多米尼加琥珀中的内含物很多——每100块有1块含内含物；波罗的海琥珀每1000块大约有1块含内含物。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now that you have a basic knowledge of amber, I'd like to talk a bit about amber's applications in different fields. First, amber is appreciated for its color and beauty. Good quality amber is used to manufacture ornamental objects and jewelry, for instance using a variety of exclusive first class quality natural Baltic amber with silver to make natural amber jewelry. But due to the biodegradation of Amber fossils, people with amber jewelry have to take special care of it, to ensure that the amber is not damaged.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：现在你们对琥珀有了基本了解，我想谈谈琥珀在不同领域的应用。首先，琥珀因其颜色和美丽而受到欣赏。高品质琥珀用于制造装饰品和首饰，例如使用各种一流的天然波罗的海琥珀与银结合制作天然琥珀首饰。但由于琥珀化石的生物降解特性，佩戴琥珀首饰的人必须特别小心，确保琥珀不受损。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: It was previously believed that amber worn on the neck served to protect one from diseases of the throat and preserved the sound mind. Kalistrate, a famous doctor in the Roman Empire wrote that amber powder mixed with honey cures throat, eye and ear diseases, and if it is taken with water, eases stomachache. While the mystery around that use of amber has not been cleared, one thing is sure: it will help effectively to defeat small malaises. Amber has even been used as a building material. Amber created the altar in St. Brygida Church in Gdansk, Poland. In St. Petersburg, Russia, the walls of the famous Amber Room were lined with intricate carvings and inlaid designs. This palace room is being reconstructed from photographs, and can be visited at the Catherine Palace, located in the town of Tsarskoye Selo.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：以前人们认为脖子上佩戴琥珀可以预防咽喉疾病并保持心智健全。罗马帝国的著名医生卡利斯特写道，琥珀粉与蜂蜜混合可以治疗咽喉、眼睛和耳朵疾病，如果用水服用可以缓解胃痛。虽然琥珀这种用途的神秘性尚未完全解开，但有一件事是确定的：它能有效帮助消除小病痛。琥珀甚至被用作建筑材料。琥珀制造了波兰格但斯克圣布里吉达教堂的祭坛。在俄罗斯圣彼得堡，著名的琥珀宫的墙壁镶嵌着复杂的雕刻和镶嵌图案。这座宫殿房间正在根据照片重建，可以在位于沙皇村叶卡捷琳娜宫参观。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: And finally, the fourth use of amber is that...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：最后，琥珀的第四种用途是……

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello, Elite Travel, this is Emily speaking, how may I assist you today?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：您好，精英旅行社，我是艾米丽，今天能为您效劳吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hi, I have a group visit to plan, and I wonder whether you could help me decide on which hotel to book. I have narrowed it down to either the Winchester, the Royal Hotel, or the Star Hotel. I am wondering if you have a recommendation.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客户：你好，我要计划一次团体旅行，你能帮我决定订哪家酒店吗？我已经缩小到三家：温切斯特、皇家酒店和明星酒店。我想知道你有什么推荐。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: I would be happy to help! Those three are excellent choices. If everyone is booking hotel rooms independently, an easy way to do it is online booking. The Star Hotel offers online bookings at no additional charge.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：很乐意帮忙！这三家都是很好的选择。如果每个人自己订房，一个简单的方式就是在线预订。明星酒店提供在线预订，不收取额外费用。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: It sounds fine!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客户：听起来不错！

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, and you can even book the gorgeous sea view rooms if you act quickly.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：是的，如果你动作快的话，甚至能订到漂亮的海景房。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hm, I will consider that. It would be great since we are mostly first-time visitors to the area to get a nice view of the water. Now, are there handicap accessible rooms?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客户：嗯，我考虑一下。我们大多数人都是第一次来这个地区，能看水景会很棒。另外，有残疾人无障碍房间吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, all three options have access for the physically disabled.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：有的，三个选项都为身体残疾人士提供无障碍设施。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great. I should also mention that we will be on a tight schedule, so we won't have much time to go out for meals. Which of these hotels serve food?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客户：太好了。我提一下，我们的行程很紧，所以没有太多时间外出吃饭。这些酒店哪家供餐？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: There is a limited continental breakfast menu at the Star and at the Winchester. For a full restaurant and room service, the Royal Hotel is your best bet.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：明星酒店和温切斯特酒店提供有限的欧陆式早餐。如果要用正餐厅和客房服务，皇家酒店是您的最佳选择。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh wonderful! Could you tell me more about the restaurant?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客户：哦太好了！你能多介绍一下餐厅吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely. In the morning there is a gourmet buffet or a la carte item, and after 11 a.m. lunch is served in the dining room. Dinners are in a nice, low-key but high quality setting in the hotel's Private dining room and Fridays feature the house jazz band.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：当然。早上有美食自助餐或单点菜品，上午11点后午餐在餐厅供应。晚餐在酒店私人餐厅里优雅、低调但高品质的环境中享用，周五有酒店的爵士乐队表演。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: How lovely! Is there a group discount?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客户：太棒了！有团体折扣吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: No, sorry. Not at the Royal hotel. Let me check on the others, though. Could I place you on hold for just a second?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：抱歉，没有。皇家酒店没有。不过让我查查其他两家。您能稍等片刻吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure, thanks.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客户：好的，谢谢。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: It looks like there is one at the Winchester - 15% off when you book 8 or more rooms.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：看起来温切斯特酒店有优惠——预订8间或以上房间打85折。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Really? Sold! We'll book at the Winchester. Wait - is it suitable for children though? We'll have a few little ones in our group, and it would be great to have a way to keep them occupied.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客户：真的吗？成交！我们订温切斯特。等等——不过那里适合儿童吗？我们团里会有几个小孩，有办法让他们有事做就好了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes. In fact, it has a play place that kids just love, with slides, and swings and everything. Definitely a good hotel to bring the kids.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 代理人：有的。事实上，它有一个孩子们很喜欢的游乐区，有滑梯、秋千等等。绝对是带孩子入住的理想酒店。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Okay, great.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客户：好的，太好了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CUSTOMER
transcriptSentences.englishText: So now I know where we'll be staying, what next? Should I go ahead and book transportation and assign rooms and everything?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 客户：那现在我知道我们要住哪了，接下来呢？我应该去订交通、分配房间之类的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: AGENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, for now, there are only a few things for you to take care of. We will hold a block of rooms for you as soon as you send a deposit. I recommend booking as soon as possible, so you probably want to send the invitations as soon as you know how many rooms to hold.

You don't have to be a motor head to appreciate the finest cars both new and old in existence today, but it helps! Be one of the 70,000 people to see everything from big rig monster trucks to good old fashion classic hot rods.

transcriptSentences.englishText: Get your tickets now! Admission is £10 for adults and £5 for children during off-peak times, and £20 for adults and £10 for children and senior citizens on weekends and for full-day passes.

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hi, Professor Jamison, I was hoping we could talk this week about choosing courses for next semester.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：嗨，贾米森教授，我想我们这周能不能谈谈下学期的选课。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds great! Any idea yet what you would like to take?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：太好了！有什么想法你想选什么吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I was hoping you could kind of tell me. There are so many to choose from. I don't even know where to start!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：嗯，我希望你能告诉我。有太多课要选了。我甚至不知道从哪里开始！

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure. Well, first thing's first. Do you know what you will major in? It is important to take courses that are relevant to your career path.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：好的。首先，你知道你打算主修什么吗？选与职业道路相关的课程很重要。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I think I want to major in Biology. I want to go to medical school, so it seems like it would make sense.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：嗯，我想主修生物。我想上医学院，所以这似乎说得通。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: I agree - if you like Biology, it is definitely a good idea to focus on that since so many of the requirements overlap.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：我同意——如果你喜欢生物，专注于此肯定是个好主意，因为很多要求有重叠。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Okay, so I should take a few Biology classes then?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：好的，所以我应该选几门生物课？

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes. Let's start there. You should pick one or two Biology classes. Not just any Biology classes, though! If possible, read online or talk to senior fellows and find out about the structure of the courses. You don't want to end up signing up for two classes that require labs in the same semester - you'll spend so much time in the Biology Department that you won't see the light of day.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：是的。我们先从这里开始。你应该选一两门生物课。不过不是随便什么生物课！如果可能的话，上网阅读或和高年级学长交流，了解课程的结构。你不会想同一学期选两门都需要实验的课——你会花太多时间在生物系，连白天都见不到。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh right, good idea. I heard labs can be as long as 4 hours.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：哦对，好主意。我听说实验课可能长达4个小时。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: That is true. And another thing - make sure the topic is either relevant to your major, or something you are interested in learning about. It sounds obvious, but do not just take a class because you heard it was easy, or because it does not require attendance.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：确实。另一件事——确保主题要么与你的专业相关，要么是你有兴趣学的东西。听起来很明显，但不要仅仅因为你听说它容易或者不需要出勤就选一门课。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course not. Though it would be really nice to have at least one class, that's a little bit less rigorous than the ones I'm taking this semester. I barely sleep as it is with all this studying.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：当然不会。不过至少有一门课比我这学期上的课程稍微不那么严格就好了。这么多学习我已经几乎不睡觉了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: That may have more to do with your study habits, though I don't disagree that your schedule is really difficult this semester.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：这可能更多和你的学习习惯有关，不过我不否认你这学期的课表真的很难。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: So any idea which Biology classes you may decide on for next semester?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：那你有没有决定下学期选哪些生物课？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I was thinking of taking Human Physiology - it sounds relevant and interesting.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：嗯，我在想选人体生理学——听起来既相关又有趣。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: I think it is an interesting class, but I would recommend against it. You are already in Human Anatomy, which also covers Physiology so it would be repetitive, and probably not the best use of your time.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：我觉得那是一门有趣的课，但我不建议选。你已经在人体解剖学上了，那也涵盖生理学，所以会重复，可能不是最佳利用时间。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: If I already know some of the stuff, I could take it to boost my GPA a little bit.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：如果我已经知道一些内容，我可以用它来稍微提高一下我的平均绩点。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Um, you could maybe do that, except the professor that teaches it is famous for giving out the fewest A's of any professor.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：嗯，你也许可以这么做，不过教那门课的教授以给A最少而闻名。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh wow. Never mind.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：哦天哪。那算了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, changing subjects, have you decided yet on your research topic?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：现在换个话题，你决定好你的研究课题了吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I actually decided. I don't want to do a research paper. I'm going to do a dissertation instead. I think I will much more enjoy coming up with a thesis and finding all the details to support it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：嗯，我其实已经决定了。我不想写研究论文。我打算写学位论文。我觉得我会更喜欢提出论点并找到所有细节来支持它。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: I see. Didn't you already do some of the research though? What happened to that?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：我明白了。不过你不是已经做了一些研究了吗？那个怎么样了？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I started doing research. Then the more data I collected, the more complicated things got. I realised I would have to take a lot more steps to randomise the sample, and then I realised I would need to control for more factors.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：嗯，我开始做研究。然后收集的数据越多，事情就越复杂。我意识到我需要采取更多步骤来随机化样本，然后我意识到我需要控制更多变量。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: I see. What kind of data collection did you do?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：我明白了。你做了什么数据收集？

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: I interviewed employees at the water treatment facility after Professor Dickinson recommended it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：在迪金森教授推荐后，我采访了水处理设施的员工。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: I understand. Well, the research paper could be much more outside work, but it may be worth it if that is what you are interested in.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：我明白了。研究论文可能涉及更多的课外工作，但如果那是你感兴趣的，也许值得。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: No, I am a lot happier just doing the dissertation.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：不，我只写学位论文开心得多。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's fine with me. Just remember, you need to finish your first draft and send it in soon. It's already the middle of February!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：我没问题。只是记住，你需要完成初稿并尽快提交。已经是二月中旬了！

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh wow, it is, isn't it? I just have to finish it by the end of March, right?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：哦天哪，确实是，对吧？我只需要在三月底之前完成，对吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yep, but don't forget! The date will really sneak up on you.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：是的，但别忘了！这个日期真的会悄悄逼近你。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, I'll make sure to set reminders in my calendar. And who do I talk to about registering my dissertation?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：好的，我一定会在日历上设提醒。关于注册我的学位论文，我应该找谁？

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: You should go to the Department Office, and then talk to the secretary.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：你应该去系办公室，然后找秘书。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: I thought I needed to talk to the Department Head.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：我以为我需要找系主任。

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: Not for registering. If you need help developing your dissertation, that's when you should go to the Department Head.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：注册不用。如果你需要帮助完善你的学位论文，那时才应该去找系主任。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, I see. And who would I see about getting access to the database of past research on my topic?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：哦，我明白了。那关于获取我课题相关过往研究的数据库，我应该找谁？

transcriptSentences.speaker: TUTOR
transcriptSentences.englishText: That you can find in the computer lab, specifically in the office - you'll have to ask a lab technician to give you access.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：你可以在计算机实验室找到，具体来说是在办公室——你需要找实验室技术人员给你权限。

transcriptSentences.speaker: STUDENT
transcriptSentences.englishText: Okay. Well, I'll go ahead and get started on that then. Thanks!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 学生：好的。那我先去着手做那个了。谢谢！

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning, everyone. In today's lecture, I'm going to talk about the role of sleep in humans and animals. Of all the biological processes in the animal kingdom, sleep is perhaps the most important. A human can survive for almost two weeks without eating, but did you know that one week without sleep can be fatal? It's even worse for animals, especially for those who must avoid predators. Without sleep, an animal is much less capable of avoiding an attack - this is the case for all animals, whether they are reptiles, mammals or fish. Let us look now at how different animals sleep, reasons for their ways of rest, and the potential problems they might encounter.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家早上好。在今天的讲座中，我要谈谈睡眠在人类和动物中的作用。在动物界的所有生物过程中，睡眠也许是最重要的。人类不吃东西可以存活近两周，但你知道一周不睡觉可能致命吗？对动物来说更糟，尤其是那些必须躲避捕食者的动物。没有睡眠，动物躲避攻击的能力就会大大降低——这对所有动物都是如此，无论是爬行动物、哺乳动物还是鱼类。现在让我们看看不同动物如何睡觉，它们睡眠方式的原因，以及可能遇到的潜在问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: In marine life, sleep must be balanced with breathing. For example, the dolphin must float to the surface as it sleeps in order to breathe. Like other large sea mammals, they keep one eye open and one half of the brain awake at all times to maintain some amount of consciousness required to breathe and to watch out for possible threats. They sleep with only one brain hemisphere in slow-wave sleep.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在海洋生物中，睡眠必须与呼吸保持平衡。例如，海豚睡觉时必须浮到水面呼吸。像其他大型海洋哺乳动物一样，它们一直保持一只眼睛睁开，一半大脑清醒，以维持呼吸所需的意识水平并警惕可能的威胁。它们只有一侧大脑半球处于慢波睡眠状态。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Birds also have unusual sleeping patterns, mostly due to being constantly on edge in the presence of numerous predators. They usually sleep quite lightly -for example, Swainson's Thrush, also called Olive-backed Thrush, is a medium-sized thrush that takes hundreds of naps during the day, each of which lasts just a few seconds. While migrating, migratory birds tend to function well on micro-naps.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：鸟类也有不寻常的睡眠模式，主要是因为它们在众多捕食者面前一直保持警惕。它们通常睡得很浅——例如，斯文森鸫，也称为橄榄背鸫，是一种中型鸫鸟，白天会小睡数百次，每次只持续几秒钟。在迁徙期间，候鸟往往靠极短的微睡眠就能良好运作。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Horses, on the other hand, do most of their sleeping standing up. Scientists think that horses develop their habit of sleeping upright as a defense mechanism, a way of protecting themselves against predators, and a standing position keeps a horse in a constant state of readiness to race away if danger should approach. Also, horses do occasionally take short naps lying down. Horses are heavy animals with big muscles, but their bones are surprisingly delicate, so lying in one position for a long time could well injure a horse.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：另一方面，马大部分时间是站着睡觉的。科学家认为马养成站着睡觉的习惯是一种防御机制，一种保护自己免受捕食者攻击的方式，站姿让马保持随时准备在危险来临时跑走的状态。此外，马偶尔也会躺着小睡。马是体型沉重、肌肉发达的动物，但它们的骨骼出奇地脆弱，所以长时间保持一个姿势躺着很可能伤到马。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Just like humans, animals can also have sleeping problems. Dr. John Hedricks and Adrian Morrison from the School of Veterinary Medicine, University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia, determined that certain diseases were primarily associated with the sleep states in animals. In their research they emphasised that because so much in this area still remains unclear, animal models were very important for studies of sleep disorders. The physiology of sleep in animals is similar to that of humans.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：和人类一样，动物也会有睡眠问题。费城宾夕法尼亚大学兽医学院的约翰·赫德里克斯博士和阿德里安·莫里森确定，某些疾病主要与动物的睡眠状态有关。在他们的研究中，他们强调，由于这一领域仍有太多不明确之处，动物模型对睡眠障碍的研究非常重要。动物的睡眠生理学与人类相似。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: But why do we humans sleep? Researchers and scientists believe it helps us organise our memories of the day - that sleep acts as a kind of filing system for the brain. Without it, our thoughts become disorderly and confused, which leads to increased likelihood of accidents and a tendency to say and do bizarre things. Researchers also believe that sleep plays a key role in learning. We sleep so that the brain can integrate new knowledge and form new associations. Because of the similar sleeping pattern to that of humans, rats are often studied in order to increase our knowledge of human physiology. In one study, rats were kept awake for almost two weeks, and their behavior was observed. Researchers found the sleep-deprived rats could hardly remember anything of what they had been taught that day. For example, one rat had been taught to recognise pictures of various Parisian landmarks in order to receive food - pressing a button below a picture of the Louvre would result in food being released and so forth. However, when deprived of sleep, they would press buttons seemingly at random.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：但我们人类为什么要睡觉？研究人员和科学家认为，它帮助我们组织白天的记忆——睡眠充当了大脑的一种归档系统。没有它，我们的思想会变得混乱无序，导致事故可能性增加以及说奇怪话、做奇怪事的倾向。研究人员还认为睡眠在学习中起着关键作用。我们睡觉是为了让大脑整合新知识并形成新的联系。由于与人类的睡眠模式相似，大鼠常被研究以增加我们对人类生理学的了解。在一项研究中，大鼠被持续保持清醒近两周，观察它们的行为。研究人员发现，睡眠不足的大鼠几乎记不住当天教给它们的任何东西。例如，一只大鼠被教会识别巴黎各种地标的图片以获取食物——按下卢浮宫图片下方的按钮就会释放食物等等。然而，当被剥夺睡眠时，它们似乎是随机按按钮的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: In addition to rats, the fruit fly, a small insect that feeds and breeds on spoiled fruit, also has been used as a model organism and thousands of scientists around the world work on it. But why was the fruit fly chosen to be studied? It was for practical reasons. The most important one is that the relationship between fly and human genes is so close that the sequences of newly discovered human genes, including genes that show a susceptibility, can often be matched against their fly counterparts. This provides an indication of the function of the human gene and could help in the development of effective drugs to help people with sleeping disorders. Therefore, many scientists today choose to study the genetic structure of the fruit fly, which could make a particularly important contribution to the understanding of developmental processes in humans.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：除了大鼠，果蝇——一种以腐烂水果为食并在其上繁殖的小昆虫——也被用作模式生物，全世界有数千名科学家在研究它。但为什么选择果蝇来研究呢？是出于实际原因。最重要的一点是，果蝇和人类基因之间的关系非常密切，以至于新发现的人类基因序列——包括显示易感性的基因——往往可以与果蝇的对应基因进行匹配。这提供了人类基因功能的线索，并可能有助于开发治疗睡眠障碍的有效药物。因此，今天许多科学家选择研究果蝇的基因结构，这对理解人类的发育过程可能做出特别重要的贡献。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: In conclusion, sleep is a necessary part of life not just for humans, but for the entire animal kingdom. Now, I'd be happy to answer any questions you may have...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：总之，睡眠不仅是人类生活也是整个动物王国生活中必不可少的一部分。现在，我很乐意回答你们可能有的任何问题……

transcriptSentences.speaker: Events Coordinator
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning, you're through to the events coordinator at the Birmingham City Council, how may I help you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 活动协调员：早上好，这里是伯明翰市议会活动协调处，我能为您效劳吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello there, my husband and I are interested in purchasing tickets to the automobile exhibition, but I couldn't find many details about it on your website, and I was wondering whether you could provide me with some more information. Does it open in June?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：你好，我丈夫和我想买汽车展览的门票，但我在你们网站上找不到太多细节，我想知道您能否提供更多信息。是在六月开幕吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Events Coordinator
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, of course, Madam. The exhibition will take place during July, and will showcase the history of automobiles from the very first commercial car in the late 1800s all the way through to the present day.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 活动协调员：当然可以，女士。展览将在七月举行，将展示从19世纪末第一辆商用汽车一直到今天的汽车历史。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Is the exhibition open for the duration of July?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：展览在整个七月期间都开放吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Events Coordinator
transcriptSentences.englishText: No, Madam, the exhibition will last 3 days, from the 1st of July to the 3rd of July, and then the cars will be taken to another exhibition.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 活动协调员：不，女士，展览将持续3天，从7月1日到7月3日，之后汽车将被运往另一个展览。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Okay. Does the exhibition focus on a certain manufacturer?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：好的。展览聚焦于某个特定制造商吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Events Coordinator
transcriptSentences.englishText: No, it will showcase a wide range of manufacturers.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 活动协调员：不，它将展示多种制造商。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wonderful! I'm ever so fed up of going to these shows and only seeing one manufacturer. Are there any opportunities to sit in or even drive the cars?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：太好了！我实在受够了去看这些展览却只看到一家制造商。有没有机会坐进车里甚至试驾？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Events Coordinator
transcriptSentences.englishText: There will be many opportunities for you to sit in the cars; however, some of the cars will only be available to observe. We are yet to be told whether any of the antique cars will be available to drive, however there will certainly be an opportunity to test driving some of the more modern cars on a purpose-built track.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 活动协调员：有很多机会可以坐进车里；不过有些车只能观赏。我们还没有得到消息是否有古董车可以试驾，但肯定有机会在专门建造的赛道上试驾一些更现代的汽车。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds like great fun! I mustn't forget to bring my camera, or my husband will never forgive me!

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello, and welcome to the home page for the Healthy Hearing Medical Clinic and Surgery, where we'd like to share a little more information about the services we provide and more.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：您好，欢迎来到健康听力医疗诊所及外科的主页，我们想在这里分享更多关于我们提供的服务等信息。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Our hospital is one of the leading specialised hospitals in the United Kingdom, attracting the very best healthcare professionals from around the globe. Not only are we a leading medical practice, but we are also the only hospital in the United Kingdom dedicated entirely to the treatment of, and research into the curing of hearing loss. Our facilities and staff here are renowned across Europe, attracting thousands of patients a year. Our consultations can number anything up to 11,000 patients a year, however we aim to treat around 5,000 patients a year so as to maintain and ensure the quality of our services. Our patients are guaranteed the highest standard of care, as well as the use of our first class facilities. All patients requiring overnight treatment are provided with their own private room with en-suite facilities, as well as a state-of-the-art entertainment centre, which includes a flat screen LCD television and Playstation.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我们的医院是英国领先的专科医院之一，吸引了来自全球最优秀的医疗专业人员。我们不仅是一家领先的医疗机构，还是英国唯一一家完全致力于听力损失治疗和治愈研究的医院。我们的设施和员工在整个欧洲享有盛誉，每年吸引数千名患者。我们的门诊量每年可达11,000名患者，但我们每年目标治疗约5,000名患者，以保持和确保服务质量。我们的患者保证获得最高标准的护理，以及使用我们一流设施的权利。所有需要过夜治疗的患者都配有带独立卫浴设施的私人房间，以及最先进的娱乐中心，包括平板液晶电视和PlayStation。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Appointments with our healthcare professionals can be made at any time during the week, with female doctors available between 8 am and 11 am. If you need to see a doctor outside of these times, please visit the 'Out of Hours' page of our website for more information. Our doctors are all trained to an exceptionally high standard, and practice a vast array of specialties: Mr. Robert is a fully qualified ear and throat specialist, Mr. Edwards is a pediatric hearing specialist, while Mr. Green specialises in reversing hearing loss. For more details about our people, please visit the 'Staff Members' page on our website.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：与我们的医疗专业人员的预约可以在每周任何时间进行，女性医生在上午8点到11点之间出诊。如果您需要在这些时间之外看医生，请访问我们网站的“非工作时间”页面了解更多信息。我们的医生都受过极高标准的培训，执业范围涵盖广泛的专科：罗伯特先生是完全合格的耳喉专科医生，爱德华兹先生是儿科听力专家，而格林先生专攻逆转听力损失。关于我们员工的更多详情，请访问我们网站上的“员工”页面。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: During a consultation, doctors will sometimes decide medication is required, for which patients should receive a prescription. There are several pharmacies within the city; however we recommend that patients use the pharmacy housed within our health care facility. Our in-house pharmacy is well-stocked at all times, our products are competitively priced, and our pharmacists are on hand to help and advise from 8 am until 10 pm from Monday to Saturday, and from 9 am until 12 pm on Sundays. If you require any help outside of these hours, please see our 'Out of Hours' page on the website.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在就诊期间，医生有时会决定需要用药，患者应凭处方取药。市内有多家药店；但我们建议患者使用我们医疗机构内的药房。我们的内部药房时刻备货充足，产品定价有竞争力，药剂师在周一至周六上午8点至晚上10点以及周日上午9点至中午12点随时提供帮助和建议。如果您在这些时间之外需要帮助，请查看我们网站上的“非工作时间”页面。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Since the Healthy Hearing Medical Clinic and Surgery also functions as a teaching hospital, we aim to provide our students with every opportunity to expose themselves to medicine in practice. Therefore we would like to encourage our patients to give their consent for a medical student to attend their consultations. If our patients are not comfortable with this, there will be a form at reception where patients will be able to opt out.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：由于健康听力医疗诊所及外科同时也是一家教学医院，我们旨在为我们的学生提供每一个接触实践医学的机会。因此，我们希望鼓励患者同意医学生旁听他们的就诊。如果患者对此感到不适，前台会有一份表格让患者选择退出。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, please look at the map I've given you of the Healthy Hearing Medical Clinic and Surgery. For those not familiar with our practice, reception can be found through the main door at the end of the corridor. If your consultation is booked with Mr. Green, you need to go through the main door and turn right by the nurses' desk, and his office is at the end of the corridor on your left-hand side. If you need to alter any of your personal details, please visit our secretary at the Office for Medical Records, which you will find next to the therapy room. If you're awaiting surgery, please first check in with reception, before taking the first door on the right after you enter the clinic. Finally, in the event that you feel disappointed with any of the services we have provided, or have any further questions, please locate our Manager's Office, which can be found near the Office for Medical Records and between two closets.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：现在，请看我给您的健康听力医疗诊所及外科的地图。对于那些不熟悉我们诊所的人，前台可通过走廊尽头的大门进入。如果您的预约是与格林先生，您需要穿过大门，在护士台右转，他的办公室在走廊尽头的左手边。如果您需要更改任何个人信息，请到病历办公室找我们的秘书，该办公室在治疗室旁边。如果您在等待手术，请先到前台报到，然后在进入诊所后第一个门右转。最后，如果您对我们提供的任何服务感到不满意，或有任何进一步的问题，请找到我们的经理办公室，位于病历办公室附近，在两个壁柜之间。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jim
transcriptSentences.englishText: Jane, what did you think of Professor Morgan's lecture? I don't know about you, but I find it incredibly difficult to believe that light influences the environment as much as he says. I've never seen any journal articles, websites or anything that verifies his argument. It's stupid.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吉姆：简，你觉得摩根教授的讲座怎么样？我不知道你怎么想，但我觉得很难相信光对他说的那样对环境有那么大影响。我从没见过任何期刊文章、网站或其他任何东西能证实他的观点。太蠢了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jane
transcriptSentences.englishText: On the contrary, I've seen a great deal of research supporting his argument from a wide range of renowned scientists. Have you looked at the recommended textbook listed on the course outline given to us at the beginning of the semester? All the information is in there, perhaps you've just been looking in the wrong places.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 简：恰恰相反，我见过大量来自众多著名科学家的研究支持他的观点。你看过学期初发给我们的课程大纲上列出的推荐教材吗？所有信息都在那里，也许你只是找错了地方。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jim
transcriptSentences.englishText: I never look at the course outlines, I have so many loose sheets of paper I tend to lose anything I'm given by the end of the day. What's the textbook they recommend, and where can I get it from? I should probably go buy it soon; I'm already behind in the course.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吉姆：我从来不看课程大纲，我有那么多散页纸，一天结束前我往往会弄丢任何发给我的东西。他们推荐什么教材，我在哪里能买到？我可能得赶紧去买了；我已经落后于课程进度了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jane
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, you definitely should buy it, and our grades are more important this year! It's called 'The Influence of Light on the Environment'. You should be able to find it in the bookshop on campus. If not, they'll order it within two weeks. In the meantime, you should read up on Ken Simpson's work, he argues that in order to protect natural habitats, governments should endeavor to turn off lights in cities at night.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 简：是的，你绝对应该买，而且今年的成绩更重要！书名是《光对环境的影响》。你应该能在校园书店找到。如果没有，他们会在两周内订购。与此同时，你应该读读肯·辛普森的著作，他认为为了保护自然栖息地，政府应该努力在夜间关闭城市里的灯。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jim
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well that's controversial; I doubt any government would be willing to do that any time soon. I imagine roads would become quite dangerous without street lighting. For this issue, Dave Kepler suggests they could just replace the existing lights with more environmentally friendly bulbs. They could even install solar-powered lights; that way, roads will be more eco-friendly while maintaining safety. Although I guess they wouldn't be particularly effective in colder countries, especially during the winter.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吉姆：那很有争议性；我怀疑任何政府会在近期愿意这么做。我想没有路灯道路会变得相当危险。对于这个问题，戴夫·开普勒建议他们可以用更环保的灯泡替换现有的灯。他们甚至可以安装太阳能灯；这样道路既保持安全又更环保。虽然我猜在较冷的国家它们不会特别有效，尤其是在冬天。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jane
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's quite a good idea actually. The price of solar power is supposed to be on par with electricity within the next few decades, and it was on the news this morning. I've also heard that, according to Sharon Grey, in countries with more sunlight, insect-eating animals tend to be smaller in size. Since there are fewer insects, and the remaining insects produced a smaller number of eggs.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 简：那实际上是个不错的主意。太阳能的价格预计在未来几十年内将与电力持平，今天早上的新闻也提到了。我还听说，根据莎伦·格雷的说法，在阳光较多的国家，食虫动物的体型往往更小。因为昆虫较少，剩下的昆虫产卵数量也更少。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jim
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, I think I read somewhere that sunlight also has a negative effect on the quality of water, but I'm not sure I believe it. In many hot countries, particularly developing countries, there is a lot of water pollution caused by factories rather than sunlight. Nevertheless, Maria Jackson says that in direct sunlight, the surface of the water becomes more translucent, therefore it affects the amount of sunlight that aquatic insects can absorb. Not much research has been undertaken to prove Jackson's theory, but it seems to have been widely accepted anyway.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吉姆：是的，我记得我在哪儿读到过阳光对水质也有负面影响，但我不太相信。在许多炎热国家，特别是发展中国家，水污染很多是由工厂造成的，而不是阳光。不过，玛丽亚·杰克逊说，在阳光直射下，水面变得更透明，因此影响了水生昆虫能吸收的阳光量。证明杰克逊理论的研究做得不多，但不管怎样似乎已经被广泛接受了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jane
transcriptSentences.englishText: I've never heard of that. I'll have to look it up on Google. The only other theory I've studied is Barbara Swallow's study on how declined insect population adversely affects the frog population. Not that I'm complaining...I hate insects, especially spiders.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 简：我从没听说过那个。我得在谷歌上查一下。我研究过的另一个理论是芭芭拉·斯沃洛关于昆虫数量下降对青蛙种群不利影响的研究。倒不是我抱怨……我讨厌昆虫，尤其是蜘蛛。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jim
transcriptSentences.englishText: You have arachnophobia? I never would have guessed. Didn't your brother have a pet black widow spider?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吉姆：你有蜘蛛恐惧症？我从没猜到。你哥哥不是养过一只黑寡妇蜘蛛当宠物吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jane
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, he did, and I hated it. It escaped from its cage once and we never found it. I had nightmares for months.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 简：是的，他养过，我讨厌它。有一次它从笼子里逃出来，我们再也没找到它。我做了好几个月噩梦。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jane
transcriptSentences.englishText: Okay, now I'm getting goose bumps, let's change the subject. What's your stance on natural and artificial light?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 简：好了，我现在起鸡皮疙瘩了，换个话题吧。你对自然光和人工光的立场是什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jim
transcriptSentences.englishText: Honestly, I'm not sure it makes much difference which one you use; species will die out either way. I think the real argument we should consider is global warming and protection or replacement of finite fuels. Solar power provides us with an incredible opportunity to replace electricity, and governments should definitely increase spending on research in this field. The theories discussed in our lectures, like Simpson's and Grey's, are so vague and lack proof, so I don't understand why we even study them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吉姆：老实说，我不确定用哪个有多大区别；物种终究会灭绝。我认为我们真正应该考虑的论点是全球变暖和有限燃料的保护或替代。太阳能为我们提供了替代电力的绝佳机会，政府绝对应该增加在这一领域的研究支出。我们讲座中讨论的理论，比如辛普森和格雷的，太模糊了，缺乏证据，我不明白我们为什么要学它们。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jane
transcriptSentences.englishText: I see what you mean. I don't like learning unsupported theories for exams, and I'd rather spend my time learning something else. For example, I'd be much more interested in studying the animals in safari parks than researching migratory birds, particularly the effect of tourists on the quality of life of animals. As we know, every year thousands of visitors will drive in their own vehicles or ride in vehicles provided by the facility to observe freely roaming animals.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 简：我明白你的意思。我也不喜欢为了考试学那些没有根据的理论，我宁愿花时间学别的东西。比如，我对研究野生动物园的动物比研究候鸟感兴趣得多，尤其是游客对动物生活质量的影响。如我们所知，每年成千上万的游客会驾驶自己的车辆或乘坐设施提供的车辆观察自由漫步的动物。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jim
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, that would be really interesting! Especially those animals living in more tropical countries, like Borneo. Following on from that, I want to study how bringing animals over from foreign countries to put in our zoos affects their life expectancy. For example, do you remember when China sent pandas to Edinburgh Zoo? Apparently one of the pandas became depressed, but it was never explained why. To me, obviously, you can't take an animal out of its natural habitat and put it in a cage on the other side of the world. It just doesn't work... [fade out]
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吉姆：是的，那会很有趣！尤其是那些生活在更热带国家的动物，比如婆罗洲。接着这个话题，我想研究把动物从国外运来放进我们的动物园如何影响它们的寿命。比如，你还记得中国送熊猫到爱丁堡动物园吗？显然其中一只熊猫变得抑郁了，但从未解释原因。对我来说，显然你不能把动物从自然栖息地带出来，放到世界另一端的笼子里。这行不通……【淡出】

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great Britain is often hailed as the home of football, with talented players travelling from far and wide to play for teams in the English Premier League -one of the most popular football leagues on the planet. Today we are going to take a look back to the 19th century Great Britain in an attempt to trace the evolution of 'the beautiful game' as it is now known.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：英国常被誉为足球之乡，有才华的球员从世界各地前来为英超球队效力——英超是地球上最受欢迎的足球联赛之一。今天我们将回顾19世纪的英国，试图追溯现在我们所知的“美丽运动”的演变。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Prior to the 19th century, the game featured a wide variety of local and regional adaptations, which were later smartened up and made more uniform to create our modern-day sports of association football, rugby football, and Ireland's Gaelic football. Even up to the mid-19th century, Shrovetide football or 'mob football' was still widely practiced. According to the rules of mob football, there were no rules...a player could legally use any means whatsoever to obtain the ball, such as kicking, punching, biting and gouging, with the only exceptions being murder and manslaughter. These games may be regarded as the ancestors of modern codes of football, and by comparison with later models of football, they were chaotic and had few cooperation. Towards the latter end of the 19th century and moving into the early part of the 20th century, however, there appeared a new found emphasis on moral values in football. Perhaps a more modern example of this can be seen in John Terry's suspension as England captain following reports of his infidelity to his wife. Furthermore, as mob football died away, there grew a greater concern for players' health and general well-being, with many clubs affording their top players access to frequent medical check-ups and treatment. Despite the presence of Great Britain's unique state-funded National Health Service, football clubs are still seen today providing team members with state-of-the-art healthcare facilities, with the top clubs even housing their own specialist doctors and physicians.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在19世纪之前，这项运动有各种各样的地方和区域改编版本，后来被改进并变得更加统一，形成了现代的运动——英式足球、橄榄球和爱尔兰盖尔式足球。甚至直到19世纪中期，忏悔节足球或“暴民足球”仍然广泛流行。根据暴民足球的规则，没有规则……球员可以用任何合法手段获得球，如踢、打、咬和挖眼，唯一的例外是谋杀和过失杀人。这些比赛可以被视为现代足球规则的先驱，与后来的足球模式相比，它们混乱且缺乏合作。然而，到了19世纪末期和20世纪早期，出现了对足球道德价值的新重视。也许更现代的例子是约翰·特里因婚外情报道而被解除英格兰队长职务。此外，随着暴民足球的消亡，人们越来越关注球员的健康和总体福祉，许多俱乐部让顶级球员享有频繁的体检和治疗。尽管英国有独特的国家资助的国民健康服务体系，今天的足球俱乐部仍然为队员提供最先进的医疗设施，顶级俱乐部甚至拥有自己的专科医生和医师。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Today, football is a key feature of school children's day-to-day education, particularly for boys. With the help of football associations, all schools in the UK are boasting their own football teams. This mainly comes as a result of pressure put on schools and the government by concerned parents, who felt that football education taught their children valuable lessons and indeed vital life skills, such as teamwork and a drive to succeed. Nowadays, many of the UK's top football clubs provide training facilities and outreach programmes in an attempt to educate the nation's aspiring youths.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：如今，足球是学龄儿童日常教育的一个关键部分，尤其是对男孩而言。在足球协会的帮助下，英国所有学校都自豪地拥有自己的足球队。这主要是由于关心教育的家长对学校和政府施加压力，他们认为足球教育能教给孩子宝贵的课程和重要的生活技能，如团队合作和追求成功的动力。如今，许多英国顶级足球俱乐部提供训练设施和外展项目，旨在教育全国有志向的青少年。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: As I previously mentioned, it was only during the 19th century that football in its uniform concept truly began to emerge, with footballers previously playing according to their own versions of the rules. However, it was not until the early 20th century that different players actually began to play according to these standardised rules. Prior to the 19th century, football was played by all the major English public schools including the likes of Eton College, Winchester College, and Harrow. In 1848 there was a meeting at Cambridge University in an attempt to lay down the laws of football. Present at the meeting were representatives of each of these major public schools, whom each brought a copy of the rules enforced by their own individual school's rules of football. The result of the meeting was what is now known as the 'Cambridge Rules', thereby uniting the rules from across the country into one simple document. However, the Cambridge Rules were not liked by all, and a new set of rules, "Thring's Rules' compounded in the book "The Simplest Game' became common place among dissenters.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：正如我之前提到的，直到19世纪，统一概念的足球才开始真正出现，之前的足球运动员按照自己版本的规则比赛。然而，直到20世纪初，不同的球员才开始按照这些标准化规则比赛。在19世纪之前，所有主要的英国公学都踢足球，包括伊顿公学、温彻斯特公学和哈罗公学。1848年，剑桥大学召开了一次会议，试图制定足球规则。出席会议的是这些主要公学的代表，每个人带来自己学校执行的足球规则副本。会议的结果是现在所知的“剑桥规则”，从而将全国各地的规则统一成一份简单的文件。然而，剑桥规则并非得到所有人喜爱，一套新规则“思林规则”汇编在《最简单的游戏》一书中，在持异议者中变得普遍。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Across the country, improvements in infrastructure and public transport had a knock on effect of dramatically increasing attendance to football games. Football quickly became a social event where spectators would meet friends, drink tea and chat about the good old days. As football became more and more popular, it was decided that more money should be invested in maintaining the quality of pitches amongst other things, and there was even talk of installing seating for spectators. However, the question of who was to foot the bill quickly became a divisive issue, with many believing that the government should fund football's development as a national sport. But in the end, the onus fell upon Britain's local and regional football clubs for the funding and development of the football association. They became responsible for the upkeep of football grounds, began to pay their best players a small salary, and organised competitions against other local and regional teams. And there began England's Football Association, or the FA, as we know it in its current form, the governing body of football in England. As the FA continued to grow and accumulate greater wealth, it was able to attract more and more talented young men from across the country, before finally accepting professional talent in the early 20th century. Today, football is played at a professional level all over the world. Millions of people regularly go to football stadiums to follow their favourite teams, while billions more watch the game on television or on the Internet. [fade out]
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在全国范围内，基础设施和公共交通的改善产生连锁效应，大大增加了足球比赛的观众人数。足球很快成为一项社交活动，观众会与朋友见面、喝茶、聊过去的美好时光。随着足球越来越受欢迎，人们决定投入更多资金来维护球场质量等，甚至有人谈论为观众安装座位。然而，谁来买单的问题很快成为一个分裂的问题，许多人认为政府应该资助足球作为民族运动的发展。但最终，英国地方和区域足球俱乐部承担了资助和发展足球协会的责任。他们负责维护足球场地，开始向最好的球员支付小额薪水，并组织与其他地方和地区球队的比赛。英格兰足球协会由此诞生，也就是我们现在所知的形式，英格兰足球的管理机构。随着足协继续发展并积累更多财富，它能够吸引全国各地越来越多有才华的年轻人，最终在20世纪初接纳了职业人才。如今，足球在世界各地以职业水平进行。数百万人定期前往足球场追随他们最喜爱的球队，而数十亿人在电视或互联网上观看比赛。【淡出】

transcriptSentences.englishText: He sounds like a good teacher. Would you mind giving me his contact details so I can ask him for lessons?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利维亚：听起来他是个好老师。你能把他的联系方式给我吗，这样我就可以找他上课了？

transcriptSentences.speaker: ZACH
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course! My mother's friend Daniel Smith referred me to him. His name is Allen Sutcliffe.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 扎克：当然！我妈妈的朋友丹尼尔·史密斯把他推荐给我的。他叫艾伦·萨特克利夫。

transcriptSentences.speaker: OLIVIA
transcriptSentences.englishText: Could you spell the surname please?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利维亚：你能拼一下姓吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: ZACH
transcriptSentences.englishText: S-U-T-C-L-I-double-F-E.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 扎克：S-U-T-C-L-I-双写F-E。

transcriptSentences.speaker: OLIVIA
transcriptSentences.englishText: Thanks for helping me out, I'll give him a call tomorrow. I don't know if I should learn in a manual or automatic car. How do I decide?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利维亚：谢谢你的帮助，我明天给他打电话。我不知道应该学手动挡还是自动挡。怎么决定呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: ZACH
transcriptSentences.englishText: I wasn't sure which type of car to learn in either. In the end I chose to learn in a manual car because once you've learnt how to drive manually you can drive automatic as well. Most cars on the road are automatic nowadays.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 扎克：我也不确定学哪种。最后我选择了手动挡，因为一旦你学会开手动挡，自动挡也能开。现在路上大多数车都是自动挡。

transcriptSentences.speaker: OLIVIA
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, I think I'll learn with a manual car too then. Hopefully the teacher will be able to give me lessons in the evenings after school!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利维亚：好的，那我也学手动挡吧。希望老师能在放学后的晚上给我上课！

transcriptSentences.speaker: ZACH
transcriptSentences.englishText: It would be much better if you take the lessons during the day. It will be far easier for you to learn when there is enough daylight to clearly see everything going on around you. But you need to be an experienced driver to drive safely at night.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 扎克：如果你在白天上课会好得多。有足够的日光能清楚地看到周围的一切，学起来会容易得多。但你需要是有经验的司机才能安全地夜间驾驶。

transcriptSentences.speaker: OLIVIA
transcriptSentences.englishText: How frustrating! I was hoping I wouldn't have to take lessons during the weekends! You're right though, safety comes first!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利维亚：真让人沮丧！我本来希望不用在周末上课的！不过你说得对，安全第一！

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning, everybody and welcome to Mount Rushmore! To start your visit I'm just going to give you a brief account of the history of the memorial before letting you roam about on your own. I won't keep you long. OK?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家早上好，欢迎来到拉什莫尔山！在让你们自由游览之前，我先简单介绍一下这座纪念雕像的历史。我不会占用你们很长时间。好的？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Mount Rushmore is South Dakota's top tourist attraction and features the heads of four United States Presidents - George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln. Each head is 18 metres tall, which is taller than the heights of eleven people combined! The sculptor initially wanted to depict the presidents from head to waist, but due to a lack of funding the construction had to stop before this vision could be realised. In total it cost the government $1 million to sculpt the heads at Mount Rushmore.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：拉什莫尔山是南达科他州最著名的旅游景点，雕刻着四位美国总统的头像——乔治·华盛顿、托马斯·杰斐逊、西奥多·罗斯福和亚伯拉罕·林肯。每个头像高18米，比十一个人的身高加起来还要高！雕塑家最初想雕刻总统们的半身像（从头到腰），但由于资金不足，工程在这一愿景实现之前就不得不停止。政府总共花费了100万美元雕刻拉什莫尔山的头像。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Before the construction of the presidents' heads, the mountain was just bare rock and forest attracting only a few hikers a year. The new carving at Mount Rushmore has become an iconic symbol of presidential greatness and has appeared in works of fiction and other popular works. The sculpture has also worked perfectly as a way to develop tourism, which was its intended purpose, and now attracts over two million people a year.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在总统头像建造之前，这座山只是光秃秃的岩石和森林，每年只吸引少数徒步旅行者。拉什莫尔山的新雕刻已成为总统伟大的标志性象征，并出现在小说和其他流行作品中。这座雕塑也完美地发挥了发展旅游业的作用，这正是其初衷，现在每年吸引超过两百万人。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The original plan was to carve the Presidents' faces into the granite pillars known as "The Needles", however the sculptor soon realised that these rocks were too eroded and delicate to support such a large sculpture. Instead he chose to locate the carving at Mount Rushmore due to its grand appearance and brightly lit rock faces that experience maximum exposure to sunlight throughout the day as a result of the south-east orientation. Upon seeing Mount Rushmore, the sculptor declared 'America will march along that skyline.'
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：最初的计划是将总统的面孔雕刻在被称为“针峰”的花岗岩柱上，但雕塑家很快意识到这些岩石太受侵蚀、太脆弱，无法支撑如此巨大的雕塑。相反，他选择了拉什莫尔山作为雕刻地点，因为它外观宏伟，岩石表面因朝向东南而全天最大限度地暴露在阳光下。看到拉什莫尔山后，雕塑家宣称：“美国将沿着那条天际线前进。”

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The name of Mount Rushmore also has an interesting history. The location was originally known as the Six Grandfathers, however during an expedition in 1885 the mountain was renamed after Charles E. Rushmore, a prominent New York lawyer who joked that his annual treks to the mountain had earned him the right to have it named after him. Forty years after the mountain was renamed, Charles E. Rushmore donated $5,000 towards the sculpting of the president's heads - the largest single contribution. In 1927 the construction work started and seven years later was complete with no fatalities.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：拉什莫尔山的名字也有一段有趣的历史。这个地方原本被称为“六位祖父”，但在1885年的一次探险中，这座山被重新命名，以纪念查尔斯·E·拉什莫尔——一位杰出的纽约律师，他曾开玩笑说，他每年徒步到这座山，已经赢得了以自己的名字命名的权利。山被改名四十年后，查尔斯·E·拉什莫尔向总统头像的雕刻捐赠了5,000美元——是最大的一笔个人捐款。1927年工程开工，七年后完工，没有人员死亡。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: So that's the history for you. If you'd like any more information, please feel free to ask me questions, or you can soak up the information from our fantastic guide book.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：以上就是历史介绍。如果您想了解更多信息，请随时向我提问，或者您可以从我们精美的导游书中吸收信息。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now I'm going to give you a plan of the site and I'd just like to point out where everything is so that you can explore everything for yourself. We're currently standing at the entrance, which is marked with the arrow on the map. If you follow the trail up to our left, you will find the information centre. There's a great photo booth there where you can have your photograph taken with Mount Rushmore in the background for a fee of only $10 - what a great souvenir! In front of us is the refreshment centre where you can help yourselves to coffee, locally grown tea and a delicious selection of cold drinks and biscuits. Be sure to stay hydrated as it can get really hot up here! To our right not far up the trail is the gift shop. Here we sell copies of the guide book and it's also the perfect place to pick up some small souvenirs for yourself, your family and friends. Now further up the trail behind the gift shop is a big stone building with a workshop. This is where all of our souvenirs are made by hand, which you can purchase in the gift shop like I said before. Some are even carved from pieces of rock taken from Mount Rushmore itself! If you carry on walking up the trail past the workshop you'll find our state of the art visitor centre where you can find maps of the walking trails here at Mount Rushmore. Now for the real treat! After you have walked past the visitor centre, you can follow the trail up to the left, which will take you to our wooden shelter. From here you will have the best view of Mount Rushmore that there is - an experience not be forgotten!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：现在我要给你们一份遗址地图，我想指出每个地方的位置，这样你们就可以自己探索了。我们现在站在入口处，地图上用箭头标记了。如果沿着我们左边的路径走，你们会找到信息中心。那里有一个很棒的照相亭，你可以花10美元在拉什莫尔山背景下拍照——多么棒的纪念品！我们前面是餐饮中心，你们可以享用咖啡、当地种植的茶叶和各种冷饮和饼干。一定要保持水分，因为这里会很热！我们右边不远处是礼品店。我们在这里出售导游书，也是为你们自己、家人和朋友买小纪念品的完美地方。礼品店后面更远的路径上有一栋大石屋，里面有一个工坊。我们所有的纪念品都是在这里手工制作的，就像我之前说的，你们可以在礼品店购买。有些甚至是直接用拉什莫尔山上的岩石雕刻而成的！如果你继续沿着路径走过工坊，你会找到我们最先进的游客中心，在那里你可以找到拉什莫尔山徒步路径的地图。现在真正的享受来了！走过游客中心之后，你可以沿着左边的路径向上走，它会带你去我们的木制观景台。从这里你将看到拉什莫尔山最美的景色——一个难忘的体验！

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right, if anyone wants a guided tour then I'm starting at the information centre. If you'd like to follow me, this way please.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：好了，如果有人想要导游服务，我将在信息中心开始。请跟我来，这边走。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CHARLOTTE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Excuse me, Dr Twain. May I speak with you for a minute?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 夏洛特：打扰一下，吐温博士。我能和您谈一会儿吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR TWAIN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course, please come in.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吐温博士：当然，请进。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CHARLOTTE
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm Charlotte York. I'm considering taking your course in Tourism.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 夏洛特：我是夏洛特·约克。我在考虑选修您的旅游课程。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR TWAIN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right. Well, Charlotte, how can I help you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吐温博士：好的。那么，夏洛特，我能怎么帮你？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CHARLOTTE
transcriptSentences.englishText: I have been considering studying Tourism, however, it is such an important decision that I would like to seek some advice about it first. Would you mind answering some of my questions?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 夏洛特：我一直在考虑学旅游，但这是一个如此重要的决定，我想先征求一些建议。您介意回答我的一些问题吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR TWAIN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely, fire away!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吐温博士：当然，尽管问！

transcriptSentences.speaker: CHARLOTTE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well I have been discussing courses with my parents and they are concerned that I will not be able to get a well-paid job with a degree in Tourism. The reason that I want to study the course is that I have a great interest in the subject and I think I would really enjoy it. I believe the only way that I will enjoy my life is if I enjoy my career. Happiness is far more important than money, don't you think?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 夏洛特：嗯，我一直和父母讨论课程，他们担心我拿旅游学位找不到高薪工作。我想学这门课的原因是我对这个学科很感兴趣，我觉得我会很喜欢它。我相信我享受生活的唯一方式就是享受我的职业。幸福远比金钱重要，您不觉得吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR TWAIN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely. I would much rather be happy and poor rather than rich and miserable. Money cannot buy you happiness.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吐温博士：完全同意。我宁愿快乐地贫穷，也不愿富有而痛苦。金钱买不到幸福。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CHARLOTTE
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm glad you agree.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 夏洛特：很高兴您同意。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR TWAIN
transcriptSentences.englishText: You needn't worry about money, Charlotte. A large part of the Tourism course is dedicated to teaching students how to manage finances, a skill that you can apply to your everyday life as well. I would also recommend that you take a sideline course in time management, as this can be incredibly useful in efficiently planning your workload. Efficiency is the key to success!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吐温博士：你不必担心钱的问题，夏洛特。旅游课程的很大一部分专门教学生如何理财，这项技能你也可以应用到日常生活中。我还建议你选修一门时间管理的辅助课程，因为这对高效规划工作量非常有用。效率是成功的关键！

transcriptSentences.speaker: CHARLOTTE
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'll remember that.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 夏洛特：我会记住的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR TWAIN
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now I have found that some students have natural talents that really help them to succeed in the course. Communication skills, for example, can be very beneficial. Do you have any strengths?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吐温博士：我发现有些学生的天赋对他们在课程中取得成功很有帮助。例如，沟通技巧就很有用。你有什么长处吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CHARLOTTE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Maths was always my favourite subject at school so I really enjoy solving mathematical problems, however I find statistics quite difficult. I have always been very capable and self-sufficient. I have a lot of confidence in my abilities and will take the initiative in situations without needing to depend on anyone else for their help.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 夏洛特：数学一直是我在学校最喜欢的科目，所以我真的很喜欢解决数学问题，但我发现统计学很难。我一直很能干，能自给自足。我对自己的能力很有信心，会在情境中主动行动，不需要依赖别人的帮助。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR TWAIN
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's a really great quality to have and will be particularly useful if you choose to study Tourism.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吐温博士：这是一个非常好的品质，如果你选择学旅游，会特别有用。

transcriptSentences.speaker: CHARLOTTE
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's great.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 夏洛特：太好了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR TWAIN
transcriptSentences.englishText: I would recommend that you spend some of your time researching the course. A lot of people who are uneducated on the subject claim that Tourism is a shrinking industry and that it will become irrelevant in the future. If you study the published research however, you will see that the truth is quite the opposite. The industry has, in fact, grown significantly as people have developed an ever-increasing interest in culture and travel. Have you compared the university course with a polytechnic?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吐温博士：我建议你花一些时间研究这门课程。很多对此不了解的人声称旅游业是一个萎缩的行业，将来会变得无关紧要。但如果你研究已发表的研究报告，你会看到事实恰恰相反。事实上，随着人们对文化和旅行越来越感兴趣，这个行业已经显著增长。你比较过大学课程和理工学院的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: CHARLOTTE
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, I have. I was interested in studying the course in modules. However, the university doesn't offer that option. I don't have enough funds to be able to attend an expensive university, so I was relieved to see that the course is quite affordable. I also considered attending a summer school instead of university to save money and so that I could work during the rest of the year, but I really wanted the university experience.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 夏洛特：是的，比较过了。我对模块化学习感兴趣。然而，大学不提供那个选项。我没有足够的资金去读昂贵的大学，所以看到课程费用相当实惠时我松了一口气。我也考虑过上暑期学校而不是大学以省钱，这样我就可以在一年剩下的时间里工作，但我真的很想要大学体验。

transcriptSentences.speaker: DR TWAIN
transcriptSentences.englishText: I think that university would suit you well.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 吐温博士：我觉得大学会很适合你。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Welcome class to your very first lecture in this series on Business in the Modern World conducted by myself, Dr Toby Bennett. Today we will be looking into the practice of company outsourcing, using TCP Technologies as a case study. Now, for those of you who are unfamiliar with this practice, I will give you a summative definition: company outsourcing involves the contracting of various business activities by one company to another. This practice will sometimes occur from a western company to a party based in a third world country, the rationale being to make significant financial savings on lower international labour rates and to potentially increase quality.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：欢迎同学们来到我自己——托比·贝内特博士——主持的“现代世界商业”系列讲座的第一讲。今天我们将通过 TCP Technologies 这个案例来研究公司外包的做法。现在，对于不熟悉这种做法的同学，我给你们一个概括性的定义：公司外包涉及一家公司将各种商业活动承包给另一家公司。这种做法有时会发生在西方公司向第三世界国家的合作方外包，其理由是节省大量国际劳动力成本，并可能提高质量。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, our case study for today is TCP Technologies - a party located in India that receives outsourced tasks from western companies. The manager of TCP Technologies is a man called Manjeet Khanna who has personally developed a series of aims and philosophies by which the company is expected to operate. He claims that the most important of these philosophies is to create a workplace where each individual member has the opportunity to contribute their opinion to the operations of the company. That is to say that he found it important to develop a democratic environment.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我们今天的案例是 TCP Technologies——一家位于印度的公司，承接西方公司的外包任务。TCP Technologies 的经理是一位名叫曼吉特·卡纳的男士，他亲自制定了一系列指导公司运营的目标和理念。他声称这些理念中最重要的是创造一个每位成员都有机会对公司运营发表意见的工作场所。也就是说，他认为建立民主环境很重要。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: As a means of ensuring quality from every individual at TCP Technologies, a grading system has been developed that encourages an ethos of hard work and recognises accomplishment. This grading of individuals is based upon a series of factors such as turnover, hours worked and efficiency. Every month Khanna publishes the grades on an internal website where staff can access not only their own grades, but also compare it to others. A spirit of playful competitiveness has developed through this method, which has resulted in increased efficiency and turnover across the company. Khanna also saw it as essential to develop a culturally diverse group of employees as a means of presenting a multi-faceted image that would appeal to a host of potential employees from across the globe. This cultural openness has not only increased the quantity of incoming contracted opportunities by 7%, but has also benefitted the company itself significantly. A level of transparency now exists that had not before been apparent. According to questionnaires carried out recently, these newly introduced measures have significantly increased the rate of staff satisfaction, which has subsequently led to an increase of 32% in the company's income.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：作为确保 TCP Technologies 每位员工质量的手段，公司开发了一套分级制度，鼓励勤奋工作的精神并认可成就。这种个人分级基于一系列因素，如营业额、工作时长和效率。卡纳每月在内部网站上公布评级，员工不仅可以查看自己的评级，还可以与他人比较。通过这种方法形成了一种良性竞争精神，从而提高了全公司的效率和营业额。卡纳还认为培养多元文化的员工队伍至关重要，以此展现多方面的形象，吸引全球各地的潜在员工。这种文化开放不仅使接收到的承包合同数量增加了7%，也极大地惠及了公司本身。透明度达到了前所未有的水平。根据最近进行的问卷调查，这些新引入的措施显著提高了员工满意度，进而使公司收入增加了32%。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: These figures are truly admirable and serve as a testament to the measures that Khanna has introduced to the workplace at TCP Technologies. In a recent interview published by the Economist, he declared, 'The figures speak for themselves - my system works!' When asked if he had any advice for companies on methods they could employ to streamline workflow and increase turnover, he replied, "It's simple, really. A company must see itself not as one entity comprised of nameless components, but instead as a living organism composed of cells, each one essential to the functioning of the whole. I suggest that the motto by which your management operates will be 'employee first'."
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：这些数字真正令人钦佩，证明了卡纳在 TCP Technologies 工作场所采取的措施。在《经济学人》最近发表的一次采访中，他宣称：“数字不言自明——我的系统有效！”当被问及对公司采用哪些方法来精简工作流程和增加营业额有任何建议时，他回答说：“其实很简单。公司必须把自己看作一个由细胞组成的生命有机体，而不是一个由无名部件组成的实体，每个细胞对整个机体的运作都是必不可少的。我建议你们管理层的座右铭是‘员工第一’。”

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Many benefits have been reaped from the aforementioned changes in management style, such as a significant decrease in staff turnover. This improvement alone has solved many problems that had before stunted the growth of the company. A lot of these improvements came from the realisation that the solution does not have to be produced internally, but can come from any other company. The grading system also immeasurably enhanced the dynamics of the company. The fact that this measuring system is solely produced for staff members and inaccessible by management means that it cannot be used as a judging criterion for promotion. It has proven itself a relaxed and informal means of stimulating workflow.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：上述管理风格的改变带来了许多好处，例如员工流失率显著下降。这一项改进就解决了此前阻碍公司发展的许多问题。很多改进来自于一种认识：解决方案不必内部产生，也可以来自任何其他公司。分级制度也极大地增强了公司的活力。这套评估系统仅面向员工且管理层无法访问，这意味着它不能被用作晋升的评判标准。它已被证明是一种轻松、非正式地激励工作流程的手段。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: When asked about specific features of his managing style, Khanna mentioned that it is important for him to respond personally to any complaints filed by staff members. Having found the existing complaints process slow and ineffective, he introduced a new online system that created a direct line of communication between Khanna and all employees of the company. The complaint form, dubbed by Khanna as a ticket, eradicates the middleman, is easily accessible to all employees online and has an interface that can be instinctively navigated. Any staff-related complaint, such as those relating to air conditioning and food quality, can be submitted directly to Khanna via this online system. Entitlement to vacation is also a popular issue discussed through this forum. The main benefit of using this system is that staff must include their personal details on the ticket before they are able to submit it. In the past, anonymous complaints had been at the root of much confusion and caused many wasted work hours, so the new system has put a ban on this form of complaint.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：当被问及他的管理风格的具体特点时，卡纳提到亲自回应员工的投诉对他来说很重要。在发现现有投诉流程缓慢且无效后，他引入了一个新的在线系统，在卡纳和公司所有员工之间建立了直接沟通渠道。卡纳称之为“工单”的投诉表格消除了中间人，所有员工都可以在线轻松访问，并且界面直观。任何与员工相关的投诉，如空调和食品质量的投诉，都可以通过这个在线系统直接提交给卡纳。休假权利也是通过这个论坛讨论的热门话题。使用该系统的主要好处是，员工在提交之前必须在工单上填写个人信息。过去，匿名投诉是造成混乱和浪费工作时间的根源，因此新系统禁止了这种投诉形式。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: That wraps up the lecture for today. Please remember that attendance is mandatory... (fade out)
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：今天的讲座到此结束。请记住出勤是强制性的……【淡出】
