transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: So I gave you both a task to select an article about a small-scale research project.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：我给了你们两个任务，选择一篇关于小型研究项目的文章。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Both
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 两人：是的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: And I required you to have a trial to replicate the procedures of the research in your own context, I mean, try it out yourself.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：我还要求你们尝试在自己情境中复制研究步骤，我是说，自己试一试。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, and we've done that.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：是的，我们已经做了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: Nice, in this way I want you to tell me a little bit about the article and explain why it started applying crosswords to assist the students to review the exam terminologies.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：很好，我想让你们告诉我一些关于这篇文章的内容，并解释为什么它开始应用填字游戏来帮助学生复习考试术语。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: All right, the article was written by two university professors who had initially used crosswords to help the students revise the terminology for exams.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：好的，这篇文章由两位大学教授撰写，他们最初用填字游戏来帮助学生复习考试术语。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: And the crosswords were designed and installed on computers.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：填字游戏是在电脑上设计和安装的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: And we selected the article because though we weren't familiar with the technique, it seems an accessible topic. You know, using IT to design crosswords for higher education.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：我们选择了这篇文章，因为尽管我们不熟悉这项技术，但它似乎是一个容易上手的主题。你知道，在高等教育中使用信息技术设计填字游戏。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's a good reason. So both of the professors would like to see how well this innovation was received by their students?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：这是一个很好的理由。那么两位教授都想看看他们的学生对这个创新接受得如何？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Both
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 两人：是的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: So what has been going on with your reproducing the research?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：那么你们复制研究的情况如何？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, we collected a series of some terms from our own modules and put them in a list, then we designed a crossword to revise them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：嗯，我们从自己的课程模块中收集了一些术语，列成一个清单，然后设计了一个填字游戏来复习它们。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: Then we invited some of our classmates to try out our crossword and then ask for some feedback from them, you know, like their feelings, views, as well as some suggestions about using this technique.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：然后我们邀请了一些同学尝试我们的填字游戏，并征求他们的反馈，你知道，比如他们的感受、看法，以及关于使用这种技术的一些建议。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: Did you find easy to have people participated in?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：你们觉得让人们参与容易吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: Not really. At first, you know, it was actually hard, but later when we convinced them by talking about the actual benefit that they will get from participating in this research on preparing for an exam which is coming up later this semester...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：不太容易。你知道，起初确实很难，但后来我们告诉他们参与这项研究对准备本学期晚些时候的考试有实际好处……

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: ...it functioned.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：……之后就行得通了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great, so how did you get the feedback from the students that tells you their thought about the crosswords?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：好的，那么你们是如何从学生那里获得反馈，了解他们对填字游戏的看法的？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: By a questionnaire. There were two pages in the original questionnaire and it included lots of x-linked questions. But the whole section about difficulties using IT is now out of date. Even the questionnaire had just been finished a few years ago.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：通过一份问卷。原始问卷有两页，包含很多交叉关联的问题。但关于使用信息技术困难的那部分现在已经过时了。尽管问卷只是几年前才完成的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: So have you done a shorter version?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：所以你们做了一个简短的版本？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure, and then we emailed it to 40 students and received 28 replies. I was disappointed by the fact, but... this was a relatively good result, I mean the responses from we got were well-written, you know, people did take a lot of care on them, but I was still taken aback with the low numbers.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：是的，然后我们通过电子邮件发送给40名学生，收到了28份回复。我对这个结果感到失望，但……这算是一个相对较好的结果了，我的意思是收到的回复写得很好，人们确实花了很多心思，但我仍然对低回复率感到吃惊。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, for an apprentice researcher, it's an important lesson to learn.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：是的，对于初级研究人员来说，这是一个重要的学习经验。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Both
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 两人：是的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: So what was your result?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：那么你们的结果是什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, basically their feedback was extremely positive. The students said that crosswords on a computer really helped them not to get distracted and stay focus on the work in hand, which is better than other ways of doing the revision that are often disturbed by other things.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：嗯，基本上他们的反馈非常积极。学生们说电脑上的填字游戏确实帮助他们不被分心，专注于手头的工作，这比其他常被其他事情干扰的复习方式更好。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, that was really clear. But I was struck by the fact that they hardly featured having fun in their responses. Nor did anything to do with spelling of hard words, which I thought would apparently be a benefit.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：是的，这一点非常明确。但我感到惊讶的是，他们的回答中几乎没有提到“有趣”这一点。也没有提到难词的拼写，而我本以为这显然是一个好处。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: No? Okay.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：没有吗？好的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: Their responses also said that the crosswords hadn't really prompted their general motivation to study, but it had highlighted the gaps in their memory so they can figure out what kind of work was necessary to do further.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：他们的回答还说，填字游戏并没有真正激发他们的一般学习动机，但它突显了记忆中的空白，这样他们就能知道进一步需要做什么样的工作。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right, so how did your findings cope with those done by the original researchers?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：好的，那么你们的发现与原始研究者的发现相比如何？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: There were a couple of similarities but...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：有一些相似之处，但……

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: We still found two primary differences. Compared with females, more males liked the technique, yet the original findings were the reverse case.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：我们还是发现了两个主要差异。与女性相比，更多男性喜欢这种技术，而原始发现却是相反的情况。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: Also, our respondents said they wouldn't mind doing a crossword in the final official exam, even in the original study, it showed that even if crossword makes exams shorter, they would not like it to be included.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：此外，我们的受访者表示他们不介意在最终正式考试中做填字游戏，而在原始研究中，即使填字游戏使考试更短，他们也不希望它被包含在内。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: But for informal purposes, of course, both sets of respondents said doing more crosswords would be a great interest to them, like revision or so.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：但当然，对于非正式用途，两组受访者都说做更多填字游戏对他们来说会很有兴趣，比如复习之类的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right, so let's think about the whole project, and what you've learned from it?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：好的，那么让我们想想整个项目，你们从中学到了什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well. It really took a long time.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：嗯。真的花了很长时间。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, and I don't think we handled that aspect well.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：是的，我觉得我们在那方面处理得不好。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: It could have gone worse. I mean there was not much data collected, so we didn't have to spend ages dealing with it, and since we'd already done a course on numerical data processing, so there wasn't much new for us.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：本来可能更糟。我的意思是收集的数据不多，所以我们不必花很长时间处理，而且我们之前已经上过数值数据处理课程，所以对我们来说没有太多新东西。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, definitely. Anyway, I think our questions designed was good so that the data we collected was manageable.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：是的，肯定。总之，我觉得我们设计的问题很好，所以我们收集的数据是可控的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah. It really helped having the original study to guide us, as it were. And that helped us to see what a good research instrument is.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：是的。有原始研究作为指导确实很有帮助。这帮助我们看到了好的研究工具是什么样的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: What questionnaire should be like.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：问卷应该是什么样的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely, we got a lot from that. But when we were writing up the project, I'm not sure whether we'll know how to acknowledge the work of the original study, you know, our referencing.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：当然，我们从中获益良多。但在撰写项目时，我不确定我们是否知道如何承认原始研究的工作，你知道，我们的引用。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: No, that's what we both need to learn in the future.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：不知道，那是我们俩未来都需要学习的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lila
transcriptSentences.englishText: Actually, that part's been great, find ways to share and support another person.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 莉拉：实际上，那部分很好，找到了分享和支持他人的方式。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's the real plus from the project, learning ways to do that.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：那是这个项目真正的好处，学习如何做到这一点。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Tutor
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, it's obviously been very successful.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 导师：嗯，显然非常成功。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Today, I would like to share something with you about time. Particularly, I'll be looking at the way we think about time, and how these perspectives of time structure our life. Social psychologists have pointed out that there are six ways of thinking about time, which they regard as personal time zones.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：今天，我想和大家分享一些关于时间的内容。具体来说，我将探讨我们思考时间的方式，以及这些时间视角如何构建我们的生活。社会心理学家指出，有六种思考时间的方式，他们将其视为个人时间区域。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The first two types of time zones are based in the past. Past positive thinkers usually spend a major part of their time looking back to the past, which means they are in a state of nostalgia, where they fancy remembering moments of happiness such as birthdays, marriages and important success time in their lives. They are those who have the habit of keeping family records, books and photo albums. The kinds of people living in a past negative time zone are also absorbed by earlier times, but they concentrate on all the negative sides of a life picture such as regrets, failures or poor decisions. They spend plenty of time imagining what life could have been.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：前两种时间区域基于过去。过去积极思考者通常花大部分时间回顾过去，这意味着他们处于怀旧状态，喜欢回忆幸福时刻，如生日、婚礼和生活中重要的成功时刻。他们有保存家庭记录、书籍和相册的习惯。生活在过去消极时间区的人也被过去所吸引，但他们关注生活画面中所有消极的一面，如遗憾、失败或糟糕的决定。他们花大量时间想象生活本来可以怎样。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Then, it is those who live in the present. Present hedonists live their life in pleasure and immediate sensation. Their life motto should be having a good time and avoiding painful experiences. Present fatalists live in the present as well; however, they think this moment is the product of circumstances entirely beyond their control, but it is more a fate. Whether it's poverty, religion or society itself, something prohibits fatalists from thinking that they do perform a role in changing their life outcomes. Life is simply what it is.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：然后，是那些活在当下的人。当下享乐主义者生活在快乐和即时感觉中。他们的生活格言是享受美好时光，避免痛苦经历。当下宿命论者也活在当下；然而，他们认为此刻是完全超出他们控制的环境产物，更像是命运。无论是贫穷、宗教还是社会本身，某些东西阻止宿命论者相信他们能在改变生活结果中发挥作用。生活就是它本来的样子。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: How about the future time zone? People who are sorted into future active group are those who do plans and go for their plans. They don't play but work, and resist temptation. They make decisions in terms of potential consequences, rather than experience itself. The other type of future-oriented perspective is future fatalistic. This group of people holds a belief that there will be a certainty of life after death and certain kind of judgement day when they will be assessed on how virtuously they have had a life and what achievements they have had in their lives.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：未来时间区域呢？被归入未来主动型的人会制定计划并付诸行动。他们不玩乐而是工作，抵制诱惑。他们根据潜在后果做决定，而不是体验本身。另一种面向未来的视角是未来宿命论。这群人相信死后生命的确定性和某种审判日，届时将根据他们生活得有多美德以及生活中的成就来评判他们。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Okay, so much for all the types. You now may ask 'in what ways are our lives influenced by these time zones?' Well, let's start at the beginning. When we were born, no exceptions, everyone was a present hedonist. All the initial needs and demands like being warm, secure, fed and watered were all from that time. But formal education will change the way we think. Each one of us is taught to prevent focusing only on the moment and start to make estimates about the future. But you might be surprised, every nine seconds a child drops out of school in the US. More interestingly, there're much more boys dropping out than girls doing. We may easily draw a conclusion: 'boys aren't as intelligent as girls.' But the evidence doesn't support this. A recent survey indicates that when American boys reach the age of 21, they have spent roughly 10,000 hours on video games and also suggests that they'll never fit in the traditional classroom, because there is a stronger need for those boys to have a certain circumstance in which they are capable of managing their own learning environment.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：好了，这些类型就讲到这里。你现在可能会问“我们的生活如何受这些时间区域的影响？”我们从一开始说起。当我们出生时，没有例外，每个人都是当下享乐主义者。所有初始需求和需要，如温暖、安全、吃饱喝足，都来自那个时期。但正规教育会改变我们的思维方式。我们每个人都被教导不要只关注当下，开始对未来做预估。但你可能惊讶，在美国每九秒钟就有一个孩子辍学。更有趣的是，辍学的男孩比女孩多得多。我们容易得出结论：“男孩不如女孩聪明。”但证据不支持这一点。最近一项调查表明，当美国男孩21岁时，他们大约花了10，000小时在电子游戏上，并且表明他们永远不会适应传统课堂，因为这些男孩更需要一种能管理自己学习环境的情境。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, let's move on to how we do prevention education. All kinds of prevention education are usually targeted at the future time zone. We say 'don't smoke or you'll get cancer', 'get good grades or you won't get a good job.' But as for present-oriented kids, it doesn't make sense. Though they do know the potentially detrimental consequences of their actions, they insist on how they behave because they're not living for the future. They are in the present right now. Logics won't be helping and it's no use reminding them of potential fall-out from their decisions or previous judgement errors. We have to get in their minds just as they're about to make a choice. How we value and use our time is greatly influenced by the time perspectives we have. When Americans come across a question about how busy they are, most of the interviewees usually report being busier than ever before. They admit to sacrificing their relationships, personal time and good sleep during nights for their careers. But 20 years ago, 60% of Americans had sit-down dinners with their families, yet now the number dropped to 20%. However, when they're asked what if there are 8 days in a week, they say 'Oh, that'll be fabulous'. They would spend that time working to achieve more. They're persistently trying to get to the future point of happiness.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：现在，让我们来看看如何进行预防教育。各种预防教育通常针对未来时间区域。我们说“不要吸烟，否则会得癌症”，“取得好成绩，否则找不到好工作。”但对于面向当下的孩子来说，这说不通。尽管他们确实知道行为的潜在有害后果，但他们坚持自己的行为方式，因为他们不是为未来而活。他们就在当下。逻辑帮不上忙，提醒他们决策的潜在后果或过去的判断错误也没有用。我们必须在他们即将做出选择时进入他们的头脑。我们如何评估和利用时间很大程度上受我们拥有的时间视角的影响。当美国人被问到他们有多忙时，大多数受访者通常说比以往更忙。他们承认为了事业牺牲了人际关系、个人时间和夜间良好睡眠。但20年前，60%的美国人有家庭晚餐，而现在这个数字下降到20%。然而，当被问到如果一周有8天时，他们会说“哦，那太好了”。他们会花时间工作以取得更多成就。他们坚持不懈地试图达到未来的幸福点。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, it's of vital importance that we know how other people think about time.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：所以，了解其他人如何思考时间至关重要。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: We tend to think: 'Oh, that person is really irresponsible,' or 'That guy is power hungry,' but often what we care about is not the fundamental personality differences, but only various approaches of thinking about time. Rather than distinctions of characteristics, seeing these conflicts as differences in time perspectives can promote more effective cooperation between people and get the most out of each person's individual strengths.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我们倾向于认为：“哦，那个人真的很不负责任”或“那家伙权力欲很强”，但我们通常关心的不是根本的性格差异，只是各种思考时间的方式。与其看作性格差异，将这种冲突看作时间视角的差异可以促进人们之间更有效的合作，并充分发挥每个人的个人优势。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Harry
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hi, Andrea. The exams have been over, how are you feeling?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈里：嗨，安德莉亚。考试结束了，你感觉怎么样？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Andrea
transcriptSentences.englishText: It's fantastic that it eventually ended, isn't it? And every morning, more sleep. What about you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 安德莉亚：终于结束了，太棒了，对吧？每天早上都能多睡一会儿。你呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Harry
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I've also been sleeping a lot recently. But I have many things to handle before I leave for England. Perhaps you can help me with it. I've had too many stuff that are unlikely to take back with me, but I have no idea how to deal with them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈里：嗯，我最近也睡了很多。但在我去英国之前有很多事情要处理。也许你可以帮我。我有很多东西不太可能带回去，但我不知道该怎么处理。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Andrea
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, what kind of stuff they are, and you prefer to selling them or just giving them away? It depends.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 安德莉亚：嗯，它们是些什么东西，你是想卖掉还是送人？这取决于。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Harry
transcriptSentences.englishText: Umm, basically, everything I have: the printer, the fridge and other cooking stuff that I bought from the former renter, but the sleeping bag may be helpful on some occasions. But the new comers have already bought what they need, so they won't be interested in what I have. And giving them away will cost me too much. I'm not sure how to sell it. Oh, I've also got some clothes and books.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈里：嗯，基本上我所有的东西：打印机、冰箱和其他我从前任租客那里买的烹饪用品，但睡袋在某些场合可能有用。但新生已经买了他们需要的东西，所以对我的东西不感兴趣。送人的话成本太高。我不知道怎么卖。哦，我还有一些衣服和书。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Andrea
transcriptSentences.englishText: Why don't you just take those with you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 安德莉亚：你为什么不直接带走呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Harry
transcriptSentences.englishText: The books weigh a lot, so it will easily surpass the airline's baggage allowance, and that will be another huge expense. And my suitcase can't hold that much clothes I have. Unbelievable, how much things I've got during my living here. Anyway, those summer clothes I have here in Australia won't be very useful in England.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈里：书很重，很容易超过航空公司的行李限额，那会是另一笔大开销。我的行李箱也装不下那么多衣服。难以置信，我在这里住了这么久积攒了这么多东西。反正，我在澳大利亚的这些夏装在英国不太有用。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Andrea
transcriptSentences.englishText: I understand. Well, there is something you can do. First of all, you can put up notices around the campus about the books. You know, in the Student Union Building and in the economics department. There're many notice boards. And also, any places that second and third-year students will see them. People always want to buy cheap textbooks.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 安德莉亚：我理解。嗯，有几种方法。首先，你可以在校园里贴关于书的告示。你知道，在学生活动中心和经济学系。有很多公告板。还有任何大二大三学生会看到的地方。人们总是想买便宜的教科书。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Harry
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good idea, but what should I write on the notices?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈里：好主意，但告示上应该写什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Andrea
transcriptSentences.englishText: Just list the titles and authors of the books, and also with the price you want to charge. Also some basic information of you, of course, like your name, phone number, and you can also put on a little tear of a text.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 安德莉亚：列出书名和作者，还有你想要的价格。当然还有你的基本信息，比如姓名、电话号码，你也可以放一小段可撕下的联系方式。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Harry
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sounds great, and what about the furniture?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈里：听起来不错，那家具呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Andrea
transcriptSentences.englishText: You could try to put on notices about furniture, too. But normally students won't be around all summer, so they may have no interest in buying furniture now. You may also try at a second-hand shop. The store will send someone here and give you a free quote, then you decide whether you want to make a deal. But usually you can't expect a really rewardable price offer.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 安德莉亚：你也可以贴家具的告示。但通常学生夏天不在，所以他们现在可能对买家具不感兴趣。你也可以去二手店试试。店里会派人来给你免费估价，然后你决定是否交易。但通常你不能指望拿到很高的价格。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Andrea
transcriptSentences.englishText: You can also choose to post an advertisement on the Trading Post. Have you heard about that paper? Every week it comes out with advertisements people put about what they want to sell. But you have to pay to have your notice on and then wait for calling. Give as much information as possible and if anyone is interested with your stuff, invite them to come by and check. But making a deal is always difficult.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 安德莉亚：你也可以选择在Trading Post上登广告。你听说过那份报纸吗？每周它都会刊登人们想出售物品的广告。但你需要付费登广告，然后等电话。尽可能多地提供信息，如果有人感兴趣，邀请他们过来看看。但达成交易总是很难。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Harry
transcriptSentences.englishText: I haven't heard about the Post before, but I should read it now and I will put the advertisement about the fridge, the microwave and the furniture on. But I'm not sure whether kitchen stuff is good with this idea.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈里：我以前没听说过这份报纸，但我现在应该读一下，我会登关于冰箱、微波炉和家具的广告。但我不确定厨房用品是否适合这个想法。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Andrea
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, you can donate the kitchen stuff to charity shop or just sell them. Like the Salvation Army or St Vincent de Paul. But maybe you can call a second-hand shop and it can give you a quote first.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 安德莉亚：嗯，你可以把厨房用品捐给慈善商店或直接卖掉。比如救世军或圣文森特·德保罗。但也许你可以先给二手店打电话，让他们先给你报价。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Harry
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure, I will do that, wait for the evaluation result and see whether I should sell them or just give them away. But how about my clothes, still don't know what to do.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈里：当然，我会那样做，等评估结果出来，再看看是卖还是捐。但我的衣服怎么办，还不知道怎么处理。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Andrea
transcriptSentences.englishText: A charity shop will take them too. So long as the clothes are in good condition and although you don't get paid for them, you know someone who really needs those help will be benefited from your clothes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 安德莉亚：慈善商店也会收衣服。只要衣服状况良好，虽然你拿不到钱，但你知道那些真正需要帮助的人会从你的衣服中受益。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Harry
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's very true. I will put the expensive stuff, like the furniture, on advertisements, and donate the clothes and kitchen things. Come on, let's go and buy Trading Post and we can write the offer together.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈里：说得太对了。我会把贵重的东西，比如家具，登广告，把衣服和厨房用品捐掉。来吧，我们去买Trading Post，我们可以一起写报价。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Andrea
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, in fact, I'm interested in buying your microwave as well as fridge, depending on your offer, of course.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 安德莉亚：嗯，实际上，我对你的微波炉和冰箱感兴趣，当然取决于你的报价。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Harry
transcriptSentences.englishText: Okay, let's see how good you are at bargaining.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈里：好的，让我们看看你讨价还价有多厉害。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning, boys and girls. I'm Steven, working as the counselling administrator at College's counselling administration. Today I would like to talk with you about the counselling team of the school and the services you can be offered.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：早上好，同学们。我是史蒂文，学院心理咨询管理部门的管理员。今天我想和大家谈谈学校的心理咨询团队以及你们可以获得的咨询服务。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: There are now three professional counsellors in our team here at St. Court. They are Louise Bagshaw, Tony Denby and Naomi Flynn. Each of them holds regular one-on-one sessions with students, but you cannot start counselling with them until you should make an appointment with Naomi Flynn first. Naomi is an expert in meeting freshmen and delivers a preliminary session in which she will tell you what you can expect from counselling; also she would ask you a few simple questions related to what you would like to discuss. For those who are feeling a bit of worried about the counselling steps, this can be indeed helpful. Naomi is also the best choice for students who can only communicate with a counsellor beyond office hours. She's not in the office on Mondays, but she will start working on Wednesday mornings and works late on Thursday evenings, so before your first class or after your last class on those days, you can see her. Louise is in our drop-in centre office a whole day. If you want to ask some counsellors for help without a prior appointment, she will be the optimal one. But do notice that if you choose this service, Louise will either see you herself, or send you to the next available counsellor. If you want to see certain counsellor each time when you visit, an appointment in advance is strongly recommended. Online or at reception during office hours are booking forms now available.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：目前在圣科特我们的团队中有三位专业心理咨询师。他们是路易丝·巴格肖、托尼·丹比和娜奥米·弗林。他们每个人都定期与学生进行一对一的面谈，但你需要先与娜奥米·弗林预约才能开始咨询。娜奥米是与新生见面的专家，她会进行一次初步会谈，告诉你对咨询可以期待什么；她也会问你一些与你想要讨论的话题相关的简单问题。对于那些对咨询步骤有点担心的人来说，这确实会有帮助。娜奥米也是只能在办公时间之外与咨询师沟通的学生的最佳选择。她周一不在办公室，但周三上午开始工作，周四晚上工作到很晚，所以你可以在那些天第一节课前或最后一节课后找她。路易丝全天在无预约中心办公室。如果你想不提前预约就找咨询师帮忙，她是最佳选择。但请注意，如果你选择这项服务，路易丝要么亲自见你，要么把你转到下一个有空的咨询师。如果你每次都想见特定的咨询师，强烈建议提前预约。现在可以在线或在办公时间在前台获取预约表。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Tony is our latest-joined member of the counselling team. He is the sole male counsellor and has solid foundation and expertise in stress management and relaxation techniques. Anyone who is trying to handle anxiety is encouraged to see him. A variety of techniques, like body awareness, time management and positive reinforcement will be introduced to you by Tony to help you address this problem.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：托尼是我们心理咨询团队中最新加入的成员。他是唯一的男性咨询师，在压力管理和放松技巧方面有扎实的基础和专业知识。任何试图应对焦虑的人都被鼓励去找他。托尼会向你介绍各种技巧，如身体意识、时间管理和正面强化，帮助你解决这个问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Each term, there will be some small team workshops operated by the counselling team, which last for two hours and are all free to the enrolled students. The first workshop we offer is Adjusting. For some people, college education is found to be a big shock. It tends to be simple to get lost after the structured learning surroundings of school. Therefore, what is essential for academic success in this workshop will be shared. As anticipated, this offering is targeting first-year students.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：每学期心理咨询团队会举办一些小型团队工作坊，持续两小时，对所有注册学生免费。我们提供的第一个工作坊是“调整”。对一些人来说，大学教育是一个很大的冲击。在中学结构化的学习环境之后，很容易迷失方向。因此，在这个工作坊中将分享对学业成功至关重要的内容。正如预期，这个课程针对一年级学生。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Getting organised is the service that the second workshop offers, where we are active to motivate you to break off the habit of putting things off. We will try to help you get the most out of your time and find out the optimal balance between academic and recreational activities. In this workshop, we're catering to a broader crowd, ranging from undergraduates to postgraduates.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：“有条理”是第二个工作坊提供的服务，我们积极激励你打破拖延的习惯。我们会努力帮助你充分利用时间，找到学业和娱乐活动之间的最佳平衡。在这个工作坊中，我们面向更广泛的人群，从本科生到研究生。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The next one is a Communication workshop. If you've come from overseas, the way people interact here may be quite different to what you're used to. This workshop will recommend some ways to foreign students about handling many situations. For example, they might find struggling on how to talk with teachers and other staff. It will also cover all aspects of multicultural communication. International students will learn a lot from this class, so we particularly encourage you to come along, but I have to say that occasionally local students can find it helpful as well. Everyone is welcome!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：下一个是“沟通”工作坊。如果你来自海外，这里人们的互动方式可能与你习惯的相当不同。这个工作坊将向留学生推荐一些处理多种情况的方法。例如，他们可能会发现在如何与教师和其他工作人员交谈方面有困难。它还将涵盖跨文化沟通的各个方面。国际学生将从这门课中学到很多，所以我们特别鼓励你来参加，但我必须说偶尔本地学生也会发现它有帮助。欢迎所有人！

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The workshop called Anxiety will be available later on in the year and it will target something you might be familiar with, that is the nerves and the anxiety brought by the coming exams. Lots of students experience their entire academic careers like this, but surely there is a way to solve problems. Welcome to Anxiety workshop and you could learn several ways of relaxation and the proper way of breathe, as well as meditation and other methods to keep calm. This workshop is designed for everyone who is going to take exams.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：名为“焦虑”的工作坊将在今年晚些时候开放，它针对的是你可能熟悉的——即将到来的考试带来的紧张和焦虑。许多学生的整个学术生涯都是这样度过的，但一定有解决问题的方法。欢迎参加“焦虑”工作坊，你可以学习几种放松方法、正确的呼吸方式，以及冥想和其他保持冷静的方法。这个工作坊面向所有将要参加考试的人。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The last workshop we have is the Motivation workshop. The theme for this workshop is how to stay on target and be motivated during the long-run projects. This workshop is only available for research students. Less-advanced students already have some workshops dealing with their needs. Well, that's it, thanks for listening. If you would like to learn more information about our services, do visit us at Counselling Service.

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, hi Jen and Irene! You two are heading to class, aren't you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：哦，嗨，珍和艾琳！你们俩要去上课，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hey Bill, yes, we are just walking there now. It's a little bit early now, though. We still would like to make some preparations for our apparatus for the experiment practice! How about walking with us, come on?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：嗨，比尔，是的，我们正走过去。虽然现在还有点早。我们还想为实验练习准备一些仪器！跟我们一块走吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course, it's really great to catch up! How's it going with your experiment? Have you already chosen the subject you're going to test yet?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：当然，能聊聊太好了！你们的实验进展怎么样？你们已经选好要测试的主题了吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jen
transcriptSentences.englishText: To be honest, so far it is going well, and we're now serving as the laboratory partners responsible for conducting the test. Also, we've decided to test the impacts of the gravitation force on a variety of objects with a number of densities.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 珍：说实话，到目前为止进展顺利，我们现在是负责进行测试的实验伙伴。而且，我们决定测试引力对多种密度物体的影响。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: Interesting indeed, but surely plenty of work for you to do. During the last two weeks, I've been thinking of and planning the test and eventually did it yesterday.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：确实很有趣，但肯定有很多工作要做。在过去两周里，我一直在思考和规划测试，昨天终于完成了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: Goodness Irene, your hard work really left me with a deep impression.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：天哪，艾琳，你的努力真的给我留下了深刻的印象。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: Frankly, I'm into chemistry so much, so for me it's not very much like work. Whenever there is a little free time for me at the weekend, I'd like to spend it in the laboratory on my experiment, which almost feels like a second home to me.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：坦白说，我非常喜欢化学，所以对我来说这不太像工作。每当周末有一点空闲时间，我都喜欢花在实验室做实验，对我来说那里几乎就像第二个家。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jen
transcriptSentences.englishText: What about you, Bill? Which partner are you currently working with?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 珍：你呢，比尔？你现在和哪个伙伴一起工作？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: Me and Kim, we were partnered by the tutor. I've never worked with him before, so I was worried at first that he wouldn't do that well in the lab work, but later it turns out he's so capable.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：我和金，是导师把我们配对的。我以前从没和他合作过，所以一开始担心他在实验室工作中做不好，但后来发现他非常能干。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: I've noticed that he's always very well dressed.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：我注意到他总是穿得很好。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, we share the same tastes in clothes; he's very stylish. But that doesn't keep him from getting hands dirty. He works very hard and makes significant contributions, which I really appreciate.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：是的，我们在服装品味上很相似；他很有型。但这不妨碍他亲自动手。他工作非常努力，做出了重要贡献，我非常欣赏。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Ah, it's great that you and your partner get along with each other well, which I think will bring much more pleasure to your experiments when both of you work well together.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 珍：啊，你和你的搭档相处融洽真是太好了，我觉得当你们俩合作得好时，会给你们的实验带来更多乐趣。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: What do you think of the other people in our group?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：你觉得我们组里的其他人怎么样？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: Most boys are really good at math, which is really helpful when it comes to calculation.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：大多数男生数学都很好，这在计算时很有帮助。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Irene is also good at math, so she contributes a lot because she can do all the equations. I am mainly responsible for all the writing parts, since she finds it difficult. Without help between our partners, we'd probably fail.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 珍：艾琳数学也很好，所以她贡献很大，因为她会做所有的方程。我主要负责所有写作部分，因为她觉得难。如果没有搭档之间的互相帮助，我们可能会失败。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: It can't be too true. And I'm so pleased that we've nearly completed it!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：说得太对了。我很高兴我们快完成了！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Only because you finished the data analysis!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 珍：那是因为你完成了数据分析！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: Come on Jen, you give me too much credit!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：别这么说，珍，你太夸我了！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm so happy that Linda has not been my partner again. In last experiment, Jen and I were grouped with her, which was really like a nightmare.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：我很高兴琳达没有再次成为我的搭档。在上次实验中，珍和我被分到和她一组，那简直是一场噩梦。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, though she always submitted her part of the group work on time, but she never took her phone with her, so it was unlikely for anyone to reach her and vice versa.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 珍：是的，虽然她总是按时提交她的小组工作部分，但她从不带手机，所以别人很难联系到她，反之亦然。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: We were quite annoyed at her attitude, but she was such a hard worker in all fairness, because she realised the amount of work that needed to get a high score.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：我们对她的态度很恼火，但公平地说，她确实很勤奋，因为她意识到要得高分需要做多少工作。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: Jen is so hard-working in fact; she has been invited to work on the professor's individual project.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：事实上，珍非常勤奋；她被邀请参与教授的独立项目了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: Wow, really? That's amazing! Congrats! Do you know why he picked you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：哇，真的吗？太棒了！恭喜！你知道他为什么选你吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jen
transcriptSentences.englishText: I thought that was because I was closer to him, but he told me he was impressed by my always completing reading assignments in time for class.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 珍：我以为是因为我和他更亲近，但他告诉我他对我总是按时完成课前阅读作业印象深刻。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: I bet you will be really popular between the other students when they find out. All of them want to hear about the project.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：我敢打赌当其他学生知道后，你会非常受欢迎。他们都想了解这个项目。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: You can distribute tasks to everyone, so all of them will get the chance to be part in it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：你可以把任务分配给大家，这样所有人都有机会参与其中。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jen
transcriptSentences.englishText: It actually sounds quite good! Could you help me decide who to assign each task to?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 珍：听起来真不错！你能帮我决定把每项任务分配给谁吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure! Now, let's see. Well, Irene finds writing difficult, but that might be a good opportunity for her to practice it by reviewing the bibliography?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：当然！现在，让我们看看。嗯，艾琳觉得写作难，但让她通过审阅参考书目来练习写作可能是个好机会？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: Bibliography, I think, may be a bit too long for me, so the methodology shall be a better choice.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：我觉得参考书目可能对我来说有点太长了，所以方法论会是更好的选择。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure, that makes sense. Bill, you said that Kate is a hard-working girl. So I think she could be given the conclusion part, as it requires plenty of effort.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 珍：当然，有道理。比尔，你说过凯特是个勤奋的女孩。所以我觉得可以给她结论部分，那需要付出很多努力。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: Ok, sure. And I know that Kyle hasn't been feeling well recently, so she could be tasked with the abstract and the acknowledgement for there is very little work involved.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：好的，当然。我知道凯尔最近身体不太好，所以她可以负责摘要和致谢，因为那里涉及的工作很少。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: Jen, would you like to do the literature review part? Basically, there is a lot of work to do but I believe you really enjoy writing, so I think you'll do a good job.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：珍，你愿意做文献综述部分吗？基本上工作量很大，但我相信你真的很喜欢写作，所以我觉得你会做得很出色。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure, sounds great.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 珍：当然，听起来不错。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bill
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right, so now bibliography and the discussion are left to assign. I think Linda will be struggling with the referencing, considering the amount of work. So perhaps, I will take care of that task and she could do bibliography.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 比尔：好的，那么现在只剩下参考书目和讨论部分要分配了。考虑到工作量，我觉得琳达在引用方面会有困难。所以也许我来负责那项任务，她可以做参考书目。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Irene
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's great, guys. Thanks for your help! I'll tell the tutor when he arrives.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾琳：太好了，伙计们。谢谢你们的帮助！等导师来了我会告诉他。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning, everyone! I would like to present the summary of work I've done by now on my research project to look into expertise in creative writing. More importantly, I'm going to share with you the procedure I underwent to collect my interim findings.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家早上好！我想介绍一下到目前为止我在“创造性写作专长”研究项目上的工作摘要。更重要的是，我将与大家分享我收集中期发现的过程。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: At first, I think certain relevant background information about myself should be known to you all. Before I started my current degree course in cognitive psychology, I studied English literature. And as you can imagine, this meant I spent great deal of time thinking about the notion of creativity, and what makes people develop into successful writers.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：首先，我认为你们应该了解一些关于我自己的相关背景信息。在我开始目前的认知心理学学位课程之前，我学的是英国文学。你可以想象，这意味着我花了很多时间思考创造力的概念，以及是什么让人们发展成为成功的作家。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: However, the idea for this research project resulted from a very specific source. I became fascinated with the idea of what makes an expert creative writer. When I read a well-known twentieth century writer's autobiography. I won't say which one at this stage, because I think that might prejudice your interpretation... anyway, this got me thinking about the different routes to expertise. Specifically, I wondered why some people become experts at things whilst others failed to do so, in spite of the fact that they may be equally gifted and work equally hard. I started to read about how other researchers had explored similar questions in other fields. I began to see a pattern, that those studies which involves researching a lab was too controlled for my purpose, and I decided to avoid reading them. I was quite surprised to find that the clearest guidance for my topic came from investigations into what I call practical skills, as such as hairdresser or waiting tables. Most of these studies tended to use a similar set of procedures which I eventually adopted for my own project.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：然而，这个研究项目的想法来自一个非常具体的来源。我对“什么造就了有创造力的写作专家”这个想法着迷。当我读了一位20世纪著名作家的自传时——我现在不会说是哪一位，因为我想这可能影响你们的判断——总之，这让我思考了通向专业能力的不同路径。具体来说，我想知道为什么有些人成为某方面的专家而其他人却没有，尽管他们可能同样有天赋、同样努力。我开始阅读其他研究人员如何在其他领域探索类似问题。我开始看到一个模式，那些涉及实验室研究的研究对我要研究的目的来说太受控制，我决定不读它们。我很惊讶地发现，对于我的主题最清晰的指导来自对我所称的实践技能的研究，如理发师或餐厅服务员。大多数这些研究倾向于使用一套相似的步骤，我最终采纳了这些步骤用于我自己的项目。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'll now explain what these procedures were. I decided to compare what inexperience writers do with what experience writers do. In order to investigate this, I looked for 4 people whom I regarded as real novelists in this field, which proved easy, perhaps unsurprisingly. It proved much harder to locate people with suitably extensive experience, who are willing to take part in my study. I asked the first four to do a SAT writing task and as they wrote to talk into a tape recorder, a technique known as 'think aloud'. This was in order to get experimental data. Whilst they were doing this, a research assistant recorded them with video. I thought it might be helpful for me and my transcriptions later on. I then asked four experienced writers to do it exactly the same task. After this, I made a comparison between the two sets of data and this helps me to produce a framework for analysis. In particular, I identify 5 major stages which all creative writing seemed to go through when generating this genre text. I think it was fairly effective but still needed some work, so I intended to tighten this up later for use with subsequent data sets. And then I wanted to see whether experience writers were actually producing the better pieces of writing. So I asked an editor, an expert in reviewing creative writing, to decide which were the best pieces of evaluations. I was then able to work out which sequence of the five stages seem to lead to the best writing.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我现在来解释这些步骤是什么。我决定比较没有经验的作家和有经验的作家的做法。为了研究这个问题，我找了4位我认为是这个领域的真正小说家，这很容易找到，也许并不意外。更难找到的是具有足够广泛经验并愿意参与我研究的人。我让前四位做一项SAT写作任务，并在写作时对着录音机说话，这种技术被称为“出声思考”。这是为了获取实验数据。在他们做这件事的同时，一位研究助理用视频记录了他们。我认为这对我后来的转录工作会有帮助。然后我让四位有经验的作家做完全相同的任务。之后，我对两组数据进行了比较，这帮助我建立了一个分析框架。具体来说，我识别了在生成这种类型文本时所有创造性写作似乎都会经历的5个主要阶段。我认为这相当有效，但仍需要一些改进，所以我打算稍后收紧这一点，用于后续的数据集。然后我想看看有经验的作家是否确实写出了更好的作品。所以我请了一位编辑——一位评审创造性写作的专家——来决定哪些是最好的作品。然后我就能够找出五个阶段中的哪种顺序似乎能带来最好的写作。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now my findings are by no means conclusive at this point. I still have a long way to go, but if any of you have any questions I'd be happy to answer them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：目前我的发现绝非定论。我还有很多路要走，但如果你们有任何问题，我很乐意回答。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Assistant
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello, this is Preston Community Centre.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：您好，这里是普雷斯顿社区中心。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, hello. My name's Andrew Shepherd. I'm ringing about the classes you offer.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：哦，你好。我叫安德鲁·谢泼德。我打电话来咨询你们提供的课程。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Assistant
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, Mr. Shepherd. Are there any classes in particular that you're interested in?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：好的，谢泼德先生。您对哪些课程特别感兴趣？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, you've got a class called Photography, I believe?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：有的，你们有一门叫摄影的课，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Assistant
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's right. It's the first time we offer this class because many people enquired about it last term. It'll be held in a library not far from our community centre.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：是的。这是我们第一次开设这门课，因为上学期很多人咨询过。上课地点在我们社区中心不远的一个图书馆。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right. I know it's on the weekend, right?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：好的。我知道是在周末，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Assistant
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, it's on Saturday, and it will occupy the whole morning.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：是的，在周六，会占用整个上午。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK. Um, what do I need to bring?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：好的。嗯，我需要带什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Assistant
transcriptSentences.englishText: Obviously, you have to bring your own camera. Some people bring a lot of accessories like an extra lens, but there's really no need for this class. It's mainly focusing on composition really, and getting the most out of the basic camera.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：很明显，您需要自带相机。有些人会带很多配件，比如额外的镜头，但这门课真的不需要。它主要关注构图，以及如何充分利用基础相机。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's exactly what I want. OK, then I've heard there's a class on cooking, right?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：那正是我想要的。好的，我还听说有一门烹饪课，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Assistant
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, it's called French cooking class. As the name suggests, it will teach you cooking skills in French cuisine.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：是的，叫做法式烹饪课。顾名思义，它会教您法式料理的烹饪技巧。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, great. Where will that be held?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：哦，太好了。在哪里上课？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Assistant
transcriptSentences.englishText: This class is special, so we arrange it in a kitchen where we can get the necessary cooking equipment. Let me see, yes, the Anita Kitchen. As for the time of the course, it used to be on the second Tuesday of every month, but there's a small adjustment this time. Although it's still held on a monthly basis, the exact time will be changed to the first Tuesday.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：这门课比较特殊，所以我们安排在一个有必需烹饪设备的厨房里。让我看看，是的，安妮塔厨房。上课时间方面，以前是每月第二个周二，但这次有小调整。虽然仍然是每月一次，但具体时间改到了第一个周二。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, actually it's my wife who's really interested, and I think it's a good fit for her because our daughter has to take a guitar lesson every Tuesday, so my wife is available.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：嗯，实际上是我妻子很感兴趣，我觉得这很适合她，因为我们女儿每周二都有吉他课，所以我妻子有空。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Assistant
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's good. But I have to remind you that aprons are not provided in this class, so when you do come, please bring one with you in case you get dirty when cooking. What's more, don't forget to bring some money with you, as the ingredients for cooking, like vegetables or meat, have to be paid by yourself.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：那很好。但我必须提醒您，这门课不提供围裙，所以来的时候请自带一条，以防烹饪时弄脏。另外，别忘了带些钱，因为烹饪的食材，比如蔬菜或肉类，需要您自己付费。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, useful information to know. Then there's another class that my wife would like to join - that's the Beading class.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：好的，很有用的信息。还有另一门我妻子想参加的课——串珠课。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Assistant
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, I've taken the class myself. The tutor is excellent. Last term it was held in a tennis club, which is going to be redecorated soon, so we plan to change this class to a golf club this time. And it'll be held on the evening of every Wednesday.

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.englishText: Do I have to bring the beads with me?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：我需要自带珠子吗？

transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：如果您愿意，我觉得您可以上我们的绘画课。这门课很受欢迎，所以这学期我们打算搬到一所高中，以获取更大的空间。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.englishText: What time will it be?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：什么时间？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Assistant

transcriptSentences.englishText: The time is good for me. Do I have to bring the paints?

transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：嗯，据我所知，颜料由老师提供。信息上说您只需要带一些画笔。

transcriptSentences.englishText: I see.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：我明白了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, just another question about the Beading class. I've just remembered my wife asked me to find out the exact time - when will the first class begin?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：好的，还有一个关于串珠课的问题。我刚想起来我妻子让我问一下具体时间——第一节课什么时候开始？

transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：听起来合理。那关于地点，在俱乐部里，具体是哪个房间？

transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：好的，还有一个问题。停车方便吗？

transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：很遗憾告诉您，停车位只对俱乐部的高级会员开放。但如果您开车，俱乐部对面有一个停车场，就在车站旁边。只需支付少量停车费。

transcriptSentences.englishText: OK. That's all I want to know. I'll call you later after I discuss it with my wife. Thank you very much.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 男士：好的。这就是我想了解的全部了。我和妻子商量后再给您打电话。非常感谢。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Assistant
transcriptSentences.englishText: You're welcome. Bye!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 助理：不客气。再见！

transcriptSentences.englishText: Bye!

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good afternoon, our beloved listeners. Welcome to today's Capturing the Moment programme. Today, we have Darren Almond here with us. He's a college student who has just won an award for his set of shots of red squirrels. Welcome, Darren. Now, can you tell us a bit about this lovely creature and how you managed to take such wonderful photos?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：下午好，我们亲爱的听众朋友们。欢迎来到今天的“捕捉瞬间”节目。今天我们请到了达伦·阿尔蒙德。他是一位大学生，刚刚凭借一组红松鼠的照片获奖。欢迎你，达伦。现在，你能给我们讲讲这种可爱的动物，以及你是如何拍出如此精彩的照片的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Darren
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, the red squirrel is Britain's only native squirrel. It's graceful and athletic. Its Latin name 'Sciurus Vulgaris' comes from the Greek words, describing a common type of animal which sits in the shadow of its own tail. At first, I thought this description was funny and was a kind of exaggeration. But now I realize that this name suits them very well. Their fluffy tails under the sun normally cast a big shadow over themselves. You will be lucky to see a red squirrel in the areas where they still survive, due to its timid nature and decreasing number in the wild. In the late 1800s when grey squirrels, an exotic species, were first introduced into Britain, there were only about 20,000 red squirrels left, the majority of which lived in the north of England. The greys carry a disease called the squirrelpox virus which could lead to the death of red squirrels. But their number had already declined before the disease spread there. The shrinking population actually corresponds to decreases in the number of nuts available, the red squirrels' primary food source. I accidentally left some nuts in my garden one day. And I found they had been eaten the next morning. It could have been rats as they have a very similar food category to red squirrels. But I knew it was red squirrels because of their different feeding habits. Rats bite a hole in the nuts, whereas red squirrels crack the nuts in half and eat the kernels. After a week or so, the red squirrels became regular visitors to my garden, making them ideal subjects for my photography project. Unfortunately, I had to shoot only in my garden, partly because I couldn't find another spot to sight red squirrels on a regular basis. Also, this could block out any outside distractions, and I could focus solely on my subject. During the shooting, other animals like birds got caught in the frame together sometimes. I'm more than satisfied with my photos. Even though I only practiced a few times and used just a second-hand camera from my friend, my great mentor helped me with the shooting. I got great tutorials from him and was able to shoot better photos.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达伦：嗯，红松鼠是英国唯一的本土松鼠。它优雅而敏捷。它的拉丁名“Sciurus Vulgaris”来自希腊语，描述了一种坐在自己尾巴阴影下的常见动物。起初，我觉得这个描述很有趣，有点夸张。但现在我意识到这个名字非常适合它们。它们蓬松的尾巴在阳光下通常会在自己身上投下大片阴影。在红松鼠仍然存活的地区看到它们是幸运的，因为它们在野外天性胆小且数量在减少。在19世纪末，灰松鼠作为一种外来物种首次被引入英国时，红松鼠只剩下约2万只，其中大部分生活在英格兰北部。灰松鼠携带一种叫做松鼠痘病毒的疾病，可能导致红松鼠死亡。但在疾病传播之前，它们的数量已经在下降。种群的缩小实际上与坚果数量的减少相对应，坚果是红松鼠的主要食物来源。有一天我偶然在花园里留了一些坚果。第二天早上我发现它们被吃掉了。可能是老鼠，因为它们与红松鼠的食物种类非常相似。但我确定是红松鼠，因为它们的进食习惯不同。老鼠在坚果上咬洞，而红松鼠把坚果咬成两半吃果仁。大约一周后，红松鼠成了我花园的常客，这使它们成为我摄影项目的理想对象。不幸的是，我只能在我的花园里拍摄，部分原因是找不到其他地方可以定期看到红松鼠。此外，这可以排除外界干扰，我可以专注于我的主题。拍摄过程中，有时其他动物如鸟类也会一起入镜。我对自己的照片非常满意。虽然我只练习了几次，用的也只是从朋友那里买的二手相机，但我的良师在拍摄上帮助了我。从他那里我得到了很好的指导，能够拍出更好的照片。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.englishText: Thank you, Darren. The award-winning photos will be on display in a local museum for the coming month. We are looking forward to the exhibition. So, tell us about the award.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：谢谢你，达伦。这些获奖照片将在当地博物馆展出一个月。我们很期待这次展览。那么，给我们讲讲这个奖吧。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Darren
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK. I sent my portfolio for the competition hosted by a national newspaper. I wasn't expecting the third prize. So, when they notified me of the result on the phone, I was really excited.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达伦：好的。我把作品集寄去参加了一家全国性报纸举办的比赛。我没料到会得三等奖。所以，当他们电话通知我结果时，我非常激动。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.englishText: Do you have some tips for our audience to help improve their photography skills?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 女士：你对我们的听众有什么提高摄影技巧的建议吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Darren
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course. Here are three things I think photographers can work on to get a better shot. First of all, good composition is key to a lovely shot. Normally, an image's centre of interest is placed at one of the intersections that trisect the whole picture. In order to achieve balance, a 'Secondary Object', so to speak, can be added to the scene at the opposing intersection. So, for instance, in one of my shots, a red squirrel at the top left is staring at a nut at the lower right corner. This is called 'the Rule of Thirds'. Lighting is another essential element if you want to be rewarded with a superb photo. The direction of the light falling on your subject is most important of all. You need to look at your subject carefully and watch how the shadows fall. If you're able to choose the time of day to shoot your pictures, lighting is most ideal in the late afternoon. Try to position yourself so that the sun hits your subject from the side. This helps create a 3D effect in the picture. To further improve on your photography skills, it is advised to take detailed notes of timing, position, weather, etc. By doing so, it is easier to review and adjust accordingly, and there is always room for improvement.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达伦：当然。我认为摄影师可以在三个方面下功夫来拍出更好的照片。首先，好的构图是好照片的关键。通常，图像的兴趣中心被放在三等分整个画面的交叉点上。为了达到平衡，可以在对面的交叉点添加一个所谓的“次要物体”。例如，在我的一张照片中，左上角的一只红松鼠正盯着右下角的一颗坚果。这叫做“三分法则”。如果你想拍出优秀的照片，光线是另一个必不可少的元素。光线照射主体的方向是最重要的。你需要仔细观察你的主体，观察阴影的落点。如果你能选择一天中的拍摄时间，傍晚的光线是最理想的。尽量让自己处于阳光从侧面照射主体的位置。这有助于在画面中创造3D效果。为了进一步提高摄影技巧，建议详细记录时间、位置、天气等。这样做更容易回顾和相应调整，总有改进的空间。

transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：水葫芦生长在热带国家。它有美丽的紫蓝色花朵，但每个人都讨厌它。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: Why is that?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：为什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: Water hyacinth, as the world's worst invasive aquatic plant, has attracted significant attention. Millions of these plants grow in rivers and lakes and have brought huge environmental and cultural problems to the local people. Farmers cannot travel in boats on the water, and thus cannot fish in it. In addition, heavy free-floating mats of water hyacinth are clogging the dam at the power station in West Africa. Turbines of the power station are often shut down because of the intertwined leaves. Dams often cease to function as a result, severely restricting the electricity generation. Dense mats of water hyacinth also shade the surface and prevent algae growth, thus limiting the production of oxygen and threatening the survival of fish.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：水葫芦作为世界上最糟糕的入侵性水生植物，引起了广泛关注。数以百万计的这些植物生长在河流和湖泊中，给当地人民带来了巨大的环境和文化问题。农民不能在水中行船，因此不能在水中捕鱼。此外，厚重的水葫芦漂浮层堵塞了西非发电站的大坝。发电站的涡轮机经常因为缠绕的叶子而关闭。大坝因此常常停止运作，严重限制了发电。密集的水葫芦层也遮蔽水面，阻止藻类生长，从而限制了氧气的产生，威胁鱼类的生存。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: So where did water hyacinth originate from?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：那水葫芦最初来自哪里？

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: Water hyacinth is native to Amazon Basin in Latin America. It has spread mainly to the tropics and subtropics throughout much of the world since the 1800s. Later, it was introduced into Europe and Africa as an ornamental garden pond plant due to its beauty. Flowers of this plant were being sold in local markets in African countries as a source of income for women. Since the 1900s, this weed has infested lakes, rivers and creeks of the delta areas in West Africa.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：水葫芦原产于拉丁美洲的亚马逊盆地。自19世纪以来，它主要传播到世界各地的热带和亚热带地区。后来，它因其美丽被作为观赏性池塘植物引入欧洲和非洲。这种植物的花在非洲国家的当地市场被出售，成为女性的收入来源。自20世纪以来，这种杂草已经侵染了西非三角洲地区的湖泊、河流和小溪。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: I guess whoever introduced this plant had never expected the disastrous impact it would have on the local ecological environment. What kind of habitat does water hyacinth thrive most in?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：我猜引入这种植物的人从未预料到它会对当地生态环境造成灾难性的影响。水葫芦在什么样的栖息地中生长最为繁盛？

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, it has been discovered that the nutrient-rich environment contributes significantly to the rapid proliferation of this weed, which obtains its nutrients directly from the water. This is normally compounded with a decrease of nutrients along the river banks.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：嗯，已经发现营养丰富的环境对这种杂草的快速繁殖有很大贡献，它直接从水中获取营养。这通常与河岸养分的减少同时发生。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: Why is that?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：这是为什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: The main reason for soil nutrient loss is that local residents cut down trees. Excessive deforestation accelerates soil erosion, which indirectly compounds this issue. Without enough trees to retain nutrients in the soil, frequent rain might partly aggravate this by carrying some of the nutrients into the waterways.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：土壤养分流失的主要原因是当地居民砍伐树木。过度砍伐森林加速了土壤侵蚀，间接加剧了这个问题。没有足够的树木来保留土壤中的养分，频繁的降雨可能会将部分养分带入水道，从而部分加剧这一问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: Are there any effective measures to control or even eradicate this weed?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：有什么有效的措施来控制甚至根除这种杂草吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, a number of approaches have been widely applied throughout the world. Among them, biological control is the most widely favoured long-term control method by introducing a type of insect that feeds on water hyacinth. So far, Nigeria has used this method for 6 months. However, water hyacinth won't be removed immediately. The side effects of this method on local ecology will remain unforeseen for years because it takes time for this external insect species to reach a density sufficient enough to affect ecological development.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：是的，世界上已经广泛应用了多种方法。其中，生物控制是最受青睐的长期控制方法，通过引入一种以水葫芦为食的昆虫。到目前为止，尼日利亚已经使用了这种方法6个月。然而，水葫芦不会立即被清除。这种方法对当地生态的副作用将在多年内无法预知，因为这种外部昆虫物种需要时间达到足以影响生态发展的密度。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: Then what about other approaches? Is there a quicker way to control it?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：那其他方法呢？有更快的控制方法吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, the mechanical removal of water hyacinth is seen as the best short-term solution. This option includes harvesting plants and in-site cutting. This method can immediately open physical space for fish and boat traffic. It is, however, inefficient for workers to process extensive areas, and costly to use large cutting and dredging equipment. Ironically, it costs even more to dispose of this plant than to remove it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：嗯，机械去除水葫芦被视为最佳的短期解决方案。这个方案包括收割植物和现场切割。这种方法可以立即为鱼类和船只通行开辟物理空间。然而，对工人来说处理大面积区域效率低下，使用大型切割和挖掘设备成本高昂。讽刺的是，处理这种植物的费用甚至比移除它还要高。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: Can we make use of this weed and turn it into something good?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：我们能利用这种杂草，把它变成有用的东西吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now scientists think that water hyacinth can be useful. The plant itself, although more than 95% water, has a fibrous tissue and a high energy and protein content, and can be used for a variety of useful applications.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：现在科学家认为水葫芦可以有用。这种植物本身虽然超过95%是水，但含有纤维组织和高能量和蛋白质含量，可用于多种有用的用途。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: So what do people do with water hyacinth that is initially removed?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：那么人们最初清除的水葫芦是怎么处理的？

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: First, the cut-down water hyacinth is left to dry under the sun for a few days before being mixed with ash and animal manure. The mixture can be used as alternative soil rather than fertiliser. It can grow crops with increased yield.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：首先，割下的水葫芦在阳光下晒几天，然后与灰烬和动物粪便混合。这种混合物可以用作替代土壤而不是肥料。它可以种植作物并提高产量。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds interesting.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：听起来很有意思。

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: Mushroom farmers can benefit from water hyacinth as well. Using the mixture mentioned earlier, mushrooms generally grow much faster so that farmers can harvest mushrooms sooner, which enables them to make money faster.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：蘑菇种植者也能从水葫芦中受益。使用上述混合物，蘑菇通常生长得更快，农民可以更快地收获蘑菇，从而更快地赚钱。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: I see. It can be used to grow oyster and straw mushrooms, right?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：我明白了。它可以用来种植平菇和草菇，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes. In India, attempts have been made to grow these types of edible mushrooms organically utilizing water hyacinth. These mushrooms provide sufficient nutritional values including minerals and high-quality protein which are essential to people's level of fitness.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：是的。在印度，已经尝试利用水葫芦有机种植这类食用菌。这些蘑菇提供足够的营养价值，包括矿物质和高品质蛋白质，对人们的健康水平至关重要。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right. Are there any other measures taken to utilise water hyacinth?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：好的。还有采取其他措施利用水葫芦吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: In South-east Asia, people feed cows using chopped water hyacinth mixed with other vegetables. Then the waste from cows is treated to produce methane gas, which can be used as fuel for cooking, lighting or powering an engine. And with global warming getting worse, developing alternative sources of energy will be more urgent than ever.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：在东南亚，人们用切碎的水葫芦与其他蔬菜混合喂牛。然后处理牛的粪便产生甲烷气体，可用于烹饪、照明或发动机的燃料。随着全球变暖日益严重，开发替代能源将比以往任何时候都更加紧迫。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Arya
transcriptSentences.englishText: Maybe in the future people will love water hyacinth instead of hating it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 艾莉亚：也许将来人们会喜欢水葫芦而不是讨厌它。

transcriptSentences.speaker: John
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, that's very likely if we can make full use of this weed.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 约翰：是的，如果我们能充分利用这种杂草，这是很有可能的。

questions.promptText: Nanotechnology and Its Applications: Complete the answer: ______
People are worried that nanotech products are______
+ The availability of ______ in our diet (e.g, in potatoes) is greatly improved.
The packaging costof______ is particularly reduced.
+ Nanotechnology can increase the ______ of food.
+ The efficiency of ______ is increased.
Nanotubes allow more ______ to enter veins,
+ As the most popular material, ______ is used to kill bacteria,

Nanoparticles protect skin from the ______ and help to improve the ability

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Today's lecture is the first of a series of lectures on nanotechnology. Nanotechnology, sometimes shortened to 'nanotech', refers to the manipulation of matter on an atomic and molecular level. It's a science, engineering and technology conducted at the nanoscale, which is about 1 to 100 nanometres. It is the study and application of extremely small things and can be used across all the other science fields. Just how small is that? A nanometre is one-billionth of a metre.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：今天的讲座是纳米技术系列讲座的第一讲。纳米技术，有时简称为“nanotech”，指的是在原子和分子水平上对物质的操纵。它是在纳米尺度（约1到100纳米）上进行的科学、工程和技术。它是对极小事物的研究和应用，可以用于所有其他科学领域。那到底有多小？一纳米是十亿分之一米。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The idea of nanoscale research first started from a physicist called Richard Feynman in 1959. He envisioned a process in which scientists would be able to manipulate and control individual atoms and molecules. In fact, it wasn't until 1981, with the invention of a special kind of microscope, that modern nanotechnology truly began.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：纳米尺度研究的想法最早始于1959年一位名叫理查德·费曼的物理学家。他设想了一个过程，科学家将能够操纵和控制单个原子和分子。事实上，直到1981年，随着一种特殊显微镜的发明，现代纳米技术才真正开始。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Even though nanotechnology has created many new materials and devices with a vast range of applications, there is always concern over these unnatural products. Many people are worried that they may pose a threat to the environment, health and safety, also known as EHS. In order to better understand and evaluate the potential harm, risk assessment has been introduced. There are also ongoing international collaborations on nanoEHS research and related policy issues.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：尽管纳米技术创造了大量具有广泛应用的新材料和设备，但人们总是对这些非自然产品感到担忧。许多人担心它们可能对环境、健康和安全构成威胁，这也被称为EHS。为了更好地理解和评估潜在危害，引入了风险评估。此外，在纳米EHS研究和相关政策问题上，也有持续的国际合作。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Despite the concern, nanotechnology has benefited society in unexpected ways. In the food processing industry, nanotechnology is leveraged against iron deficiency which triggers anaemia. For example, by reducing the particle size in potatoes, this new technology improves the bioavailability of this nutritional ingredient without the tendency to cause colour and odour changes. In terms of packaging, nanomaterials are more economical and are used in all sorts of products, chocolate in particular. Nanotechnology can also enhance the flavour of food. On a domestic scale, we expect more 'smart' furniture, which is made of shape memory alloys, to be manufactured.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：尽管有担忧，纳米技术仍以意想不到的方式造福社会。在食品加工行业，纳米技术被用来应对引发贫血的铁缺乏症。例如，通过减少土豆中的颗粒大小，这项新技术提高了这种营养成分的生物利用度，而不会引起颜色和气味的变化。在包装方面，纳米材料更经济，被用于各种产品，尤其是巧克力。纳米技术还可以增强食品的风味。在家庭层面，我们期待更多由形状记忆合金制成的“智能”家具被制造出来。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: But nanotechnology has much wider application than this and could also help develop sustainable agriculture. It offers great potential to strengthen the effect of fertilisers, thereby minimising the environmental impact and boosting the productivity of plants in the soil.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：但纳米技术的应用远不止于此，它还可以帮助发展可持续农业。它在增强肥料效果方面具有巨大潜力，从而最大限度地减少对环境的影响，提高土壤中植物的生产力。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: In the area of medicine, bioengineers have developed simple and inexpensive nanoscale delivery vehicles. Conductors like carbon nanotubes have been invented with varying structures. Such nanotubes have become increasingly attractive to researchers because of their ability to efficiently deliver drugs into veins. This means that higher doses of drugs loaded on them can be transported from the administration sites to the effects-related sites, such as cancer focuses, thus decreasing toxic side effects while increasing the treatment effects.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在医学领域，生物工程师已经开发出简单廉价的纳米级递送载体。已经发明了具有不同结构的碳纳米管等导体。这类纳米管因其能有效地将药物输送到血管中而越来越受研究人员的青睐。这意味着载有更高剂量药物的纳米管可以从给药部位运送到效应相关部位，如癌症病灶，从而降低毒副作用，同时提高治疗效果。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The research team has also developed a widely accepted material that can be used to coat different surfaces, including wood, plastic and glass. It is mainly comprised of silver. Such nanoparticles can eventually kill some microbes due to the antiseptic properties. The whole process is simple, easy to apply, and more importantly, harmless to the environment. Surprisingly, nanotechnology has major implications for our health as well. By changing the metabolic rate through a particular type of protein, obese patients are able to burn calories faster even under a high-calorie diet. Therefore, treatment programs are provided for patients to lose weight by disposing of excess fat in a relatively safer manner. The finding may help explain why overweight people struggle to lose weight. Their stored fat is actively fighting against their efforts to burn it off at the molecular level. Further research is mainly focused on the clinical and commercial development of therapies for obesity, diabetes and other associated conditions such as heart disease.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：研究团队还开发了一种被广泛接受的材料，可用于涂覆不同的表面，包括木材、塑料和玻璃。它主要由银组成。由于抗菌特性，这种纳米颗粒最终可以杀死一些微生物。整个过程简单易行，更重要的是对环境无害。令人惊讶的是，纳米技术对我们的健康也有重大影响。通过一种特定类型的蛋白质改变代谢率，肥胖患者即使在高热量饮食下也能更快地燃烧卡路里。因此，为患者提供了通过相对更安全的方式消除多余脂肪来减重的治疗方案。这一发现可能有助于解释为什么超重的人很难减肥。他们储存的脂肪在分子水平上积极地对抗他们燃烧脂肪的努力。进一步的研究主要集中在肥胖、糖尿病和心脏病等相关疾病的临床和商业疗法开发上。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: In terms of cosmetics, the applications of nanotechnology and nanomaterials can be found in many products. There are two main uses for nanotechnology in cosmetics. The first one is that nanoparticles are commonly used as UV filters in anti-aging suncare products to avoid skin damage caused by the sun. In addition, nanotechnology has played an important role in delivering active ingredients to the skin. The mechanism proves to improve the bioavailability of actives and enhance skin hydration.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在化妆品方面，纳米技术和纳米材料的应用可以在许多产品中找到。纳米技术在化妆品中有两个主要用途。首先，纳米颗粒通常被用作抗衰老防晒产品中的紫外线过滤剂，以避免阳光造成的皮肤损伤。此外，纳米技术在将活性成分输送到皮肤方面发挥了重要作用。该机制证明可以提高活性物的生物利用度，增强皮肤水合作用。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The wide variety of nanotechnology applications leave no doubt that this field will only continue to get more exciting, and I look forward to seeing these developments further branch out.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：纳米技术应用的广泛性毫无疑问地表明，这一领域只会继续变得更加激动人心，我期待看到这些发展进一步拓展。
