transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Music is a natural part of our daily lives. Whether we are at home, in the car, on public transport, or walking down the street, we are often surrounded by music. We listen to it on our phones, through speakers, or on our computers. Additionally, we're frequently immersed in music that we have not selected, such as that played in stores, on trains, or even in places like doctors' offices, where it becomes part of our background environment. This leads to an interesting question: how do babies engage with music?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：音乐是我们日常生活中自然的一部分。无论我们在家、在车里、在公共交通工具上，还是走在街上，我们经常被音乐包围。我们在手机、音箱或电脑上听音乐。此外，我们经常沉浸在并非自己选择的音乐中，比如商店里、火车上，甚至在医生办公室等地方播放的音乐，它成为我们背景环境的一部分。这就引出一个有趣的问题：婴儿如何与音乐互动？

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: A tremendous amount of research has focused on understanding how very young children respond to music. Studies have shown that babies can recall music that was played or sung to them prior to birth. My own research shows that this ability can last until a baby is 15 months old.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大量研究集中于了解幼儿如何对音乐做出反应。研究表明，婴儿能回忆起出生前播放或唱给他们听的音乐。我自己的研究表明，这种能力可以持续到婴儿15个月大。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Research into how babies respond to music reveals that they are more sophisticated listeners than we assume. During their first year, babies perform even better than adults in some tasks, such as recognising changes that have been made in musical sequences. It suggests that we engage with music from the very start of life.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：关于婴儿如何对音乐做出反应的研究表明，他们是比我们想象的更复杂的听众。在生命的第一年，婴儿在某些任务中甚至比成年人表现得更好，比如识别音乐序列中的变化。这表明我们从生命一开始就与音乐互动。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: One of the most important studies in this field was carried out in 1976 by Helmut Moog. He studied 500 children, from infants to five-year-olds, and found that babies started responding to music just a few weeks after birth. By 12 months, they were able to imitate the melodies of songs sung to them. Moog's research has provided valuable insights into how young children engage with music, though less is known about the responses of two to three-year-olds. Moog did find that when music was played, children aged two tended to move a great deal. However, by age three this behaviour decreased, and children began to use music more as a tool for interaction.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：该领域最重要的研究之一由赫尔穆特·穆格于1976年进行。他研究了500名从婴儿到五岁的儿童，发现婴儿在出生后几周就开始对音乐做出反应。到12个月时，他们能够模仿唱给他们听的歌曲旋律。穆格的研究为幼儿如何与音乐互动提供了宝贵的见解，尽管对两到三岁儿童的反应了解较少。穆格确实发现，当播放音乐时，两岁的孩子往往会有大量动作。然而，到了三岁，这种行为减少了，孩子们开始更多地将音乐用作互动的工具。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: A more recent study I've conducted has used a technique known as experience sampling. Through this method, I have found that children today are exposed to an enormous amount of music. Songs and tunes designed specifically for children are the most popular, especially television theme tunes and songs on children's websites. Nowadays, this type of music is more commonly accessed through digital devices such as smartphones, tablets, or computers, rather than traditional radio broadcasts, as was the case in the past. Furthermore, pop music is also frequently played for children, often not by their choice though. Many mothers and fathers use music to accompany daily routines like having meals or driving their children around. Older siblings also play a crucial role in shaping younger children's musical preferences. In my study, one seven-year-old boy's musical tastes were greatly affected by his older sister. Over time, he became a fan of rock music, despite his young age. He wasn't making these choices independently; rather, he was being shaped by the music that was being played in his home. This is a good example of how children's musical preferences can be shaped by their environment and the people around them. So, why do children enjoy certain types of music? My research has found that there is no clear link between the music they enjoy and their personality at this age. However, it seems these connections might develop as children grow older. By then, their tastes in music could reflect their individual characteristics more clearly.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我进行的一项较新的研究使用了经验取样技术。通过这种方法，我发现现在的孩子接触到大量的音乐。专门为儿童设计的歌曲和曲调最受欢迎，尤其是电视主题曲和儿童网站上的歌曲。如今，这类音乐更常通过智能手机、平板电脑或电脑等数字设备获取，而不是像过去那样通过传统广播收听。此外，流行音乐也经常放给孩子们听，不过往往不是他们自己选择的。许多父母用音乐来陪伴日常活动，如用餐或开车接送孩子。年长的兄弟姐妹在塑造年幼孩子的音乐偏好方面也起着关键作用。在我的研究中，一个七岁男孩的音乐品味受到了他姐姐的很大影响。随着时间的推移，尽管年纪很小，他成了摇滚乐迷。他不是独立做出这些选择的；而是被他家里播放的音乐所塑造。这是一个很好的例子，说明儿童的音乐偏好是如何被环境和周围人塑造的。那么，为什么孩子喜欢某些类型的音乐呢？我的研究发现，在这个年龄段，他们喜欢的音乐与个性之间没有明确的联系。然而，这些联系似乎会随着孩子长大而发展。到那时，他们的音乐品味可能会更清楚地反映他们的个人特征。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: To conclude, I'd like to mention a few additional points. First of all, music has a strong influence on young people. One of the most important functions of music in children's lives is a social one. Singing songs together, dancing, or debating which song to play next helps children develop socially. In my research, I've found that very few young children listen to music alone. Only one child in my study did so regularly. In my view, music is something that really ought to be shared. In this sense, technology has made it easier for families to enjoy music together. Internet platforms and social media give everyone access to a wealth of music and offer new ways to share musical experiences. Music is no longer just an individual activity.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：最后，我想补充几点。首先，音乐对年轻人有很强的影响。音乐在儿童生活中最重要的功能之一是社交功能。一起唱歌、跳舞，或争论接下来放哪首歌，有助于儿童的社交发展。在我的研究中，我发现很少有年幼的孩子独自听音乐。我的研究中只有一个孩子经常这样做。在我看来，音乐是应该被分享的东西。从这个意义上说，技术让家庭更容易一起享受音乐。互联网平台和社交媒体让每个人都能接触到丰富的音乐，并提供分享音乐体验的新方式。音乐不再只是一种个人活动。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Taking an interest in the music children listen to can offer parents and other family members a better understanding of what's happening with them. Thus, it gives parents a starting point for discussing their children's feelings. While musical preferences are personal, they are shaped by factors like family influence, exposure to different music, and the social context in which the music is heard...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：对孩子们听的音乐产生兴趣，可以让父母和其他家庭成员更好地了解他们的状况。因此，这为父母讨论孩子的感受提供了一个起点。虽然音乐偏好是个人的，但它们受到家庭影响、接触不同音乐的机会以及听音乐的社会背景等因素的影响……

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hi, I'm calling about the part-time job you advertised recently.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：嗨，我打电话来是关于你们最近广告上的兼职工作。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, you mean the delivery driver role?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：哦，您是说送货司机岗位？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: No, not that one. I'm actually asking about the general assistant position. My son's interested in it---I've already picked up an application form from one of your staff.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：不，不是那个。我其实是问一般助理职位。我儿子对它感兴趣——我已经从你们一位员工那里拿了一份申请表。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: Got it! Well, we've got a vacancy coming up at our Newmarket Road branch when it opens next month. Or there's one available right now at the Station Road branch. Is that the one you mean?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：明白了！嗯，我们纽马克特路分店下个月开业时会有一个空缺。或者车站路分店现在有一个空缺。您说的是那个吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, it's the current one I'm asking about.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：是的，我问的是现在这个。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK. So, in terms of working hours, we're really looking for someone who can do Monday and Wednesday afternoons, or Thursday and Friday afternoons.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：好的。就工作时间而言，我们想要的是能在周一和周三下午，或者周四和周五下午工作的人。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hmm, he's busy volunteering during the week. Could Sundays work instead?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：嗯，他平时要忙志愿服务。周日可以吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure, as long as he can do a full day on Sunday, that's absolutely fine.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：当然可以，只要他能在周日工作一整天，那完全没问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's no problem at all.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：那完全没问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：太好了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Could you tell me a bit about what the job involves?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：你能告诉我这份工作具体做什么吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course. Let me just pull up the details. So, the main duties are working on the checkout, taking payments and helping customers with their questions. Occasionally, people might ask about gardening products, and there's a fair bit of lifting too because some of the stock's pretty heavy. So, he'll need to be reasonably fit.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：当然。让我调出详细信息。主要职责是在收银台工作、收款和回答顾客问题。偶尔有人会问园艺产品，而且也有不少搬运工作，因为有些库存相当重。所以他需要有相当好的体能。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's fine---he works out regularly and does lots of heavy jobs at home. But to be honest, he doesn't know much about plants, so he might not be able to answer specialist questions.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：那没关系——他经常锻炼，在家也做很多重活。但老实说，他对植物了解不多，所以可能无法回答专业问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: No worries about that. We don't expect new staff to know everything about gardening---our senior team deals with most of those queries.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：那不用担心。我们不指望新员工了解园艺的一切——我们的资深团队处理大部分这类咨询。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK, that's good to know. Anything else?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：好的，那就好。还有其他吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, during summer we'll also need him to help with watering the plants.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：是的，夏天我们还需要他帮忙给植物浇水。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sounds manageable.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：听起来可以应付。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: Perfect. Now, there are a few qualities we look for in candidates. First, good communication skills are a must because first impressions really matter. How would you describe his personality?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：完美。现在，我们对候选人有一些品质要求。首先，良好的沟通能力是必须的，因为第一印象真的很重要。您怎么描述他的性格？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: He's polite and pretty sociable. I believe he'd be a good fit.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：他很有礼貌，也很善于社交。我相信他会很合适。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's great. The other thing is basic maths---he needs to be comfortable working out discounts and so on.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：那很好。另一件事是基础数学——他需要能熟练计算折扣等。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, that's no issue---he's good at that.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：哦，那没问题——他擅长那个。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: Is he still in school?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：他还在上学吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, but he's just finishing up for the summer. He's free for an interview this week if that works for you.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：是的，但他快要放暑假了。如果方便的话，他这周可以来面试。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: Let me check... How about Wednesday at 10 am?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：让我看看……周三上午10点怎么样？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's actually the morning of his final exam. Could we make it later---say around 2.35?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：那实际上是他期末考试的那个上午。我们能改晚一点吗——比如下午2：35左右？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: I've got something then, but I can move it. Yeah, that time works.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：那时我有点事，但可以调整。好的，那个时间可以。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hope that's not too much trouble.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：希望不会太麻烦。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: No problem at all. And what's his name?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：完全没问题。他叫什么名字？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Ethan Steel.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：伊桑·斯蒂尔。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: Got it. So, Ethan's interview will be with me---Miranda Rapana. That's spelled R-A-P-A-N-A.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：记下了。那么，伊桑的面试由我负责——米兰达·拉帕纳。拼写是R-A-P-A-N-A。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sorry, let me write that down---I've got a terrible memory!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：抱歉，让我记下来——我记性太差了！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: No worries. And can you remind him to call me the day before to confirm? My number's 0213038874.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：没关系。还有，你能提醒他前一天打电话给我确认吗？我的号码是0213038874。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Will do. Anything else he needs to bring?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：会的。他还需要带什么吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: Just his passport, so we can check he's eligible to work here.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：只需要他的护照，这样我们可以确认他有资格在这里工作。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Caller
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course---I'll let him know. Thanks so much for your help.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 来电者：当然——我会告诉他。非常感谢你的帮助。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Miranda
transcriptSentences.englishText: You're welcome! Looking forward to meeting Ethan.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 米兰达：不客气！期待见到伊桑。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Morning, everyone! I'm Jesse Sampson, the coordinator of Middletown Urban Farming Scheme---or MUFS, as we usually call it. This programme's been a real success in helping city residents grow their own fruit and vegetables---basically turning them into urban farmers, if that's what they're into. You might be wondering who actually started MUFS. Well, the idea of urban farming has been around for ages, especially among town planners. But in our case, it was actually a bunch of local business owners---myself included who decided to kick things off. Later on, some agriculture experts from the university jumped on board as well.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家早上好！我是杰西·桑普森，米德尔敦城市农业计划——简称MUFS——的协调员。这个计划在帮助城市居民种植自己的水果和蔬菜方面取得了真正的成功——基本上是把他们变成了城市农民，如果他们喜欢的话。你们可能想知道是谁发起了MUFS。嗯，城市农业的想法已经存在很久了，尤其是在城市规划者中。但在我们的案例中，实际上是一群当地企业主——包括我自己——决定启动的。后来，一些大学的农业专家也加入了进来。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, what did MUFS set out to achieve? It wasn't about cutting carbon emissions or anything like that---at least not at the start. The main aim was to make better use of empty or unused land around the city. Over time, though, we realised there was another big plus: encouraging people to eat fresh, homegrown produce really helps improve their diets.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：那么，MUFS的目标是什么？并不是关于减少碳排放之类的——至少一开始不是。主要目标是更好地利用城市周围空置或未使用的土地。不过随着时间的推移，我们意识到还有另一个大的好处：鼓励人们吃新鲜的自产农产品真的有助于改善他们的饮食。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, who's taking part? Well, schools have been very active, and we've also had a good response from company employees, so the message is definitely getting through there. But next year, we'll be focusing on getting community centres for senior citizens involved because, so far, their participation's been pretty low.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：那么，谁在参与？嗯，学校一直很积极，公司员工的反应也很好，所以信息肯定传到了那里。但明年，我们将重点让老年人社区中心参与进来，因为到目前为止，他们的参与度相当低。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, MUFS is built around a great group of gardening enthusiasts. They might not know every detail about every plot, but they really know their way around a garden. Most of them are amateurs, but they're more than happy to chat with members and share hands-on tips. Just don't expect them to answer really technical questions like the Latin names of plants---that's not their thing.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：MUFS是围绕一群热情的园艺爱好者建立的。他们可能不了解每个地块的每个细节，但他们真的很懂园艺。他们中的大多数是业余爱好者，但他们非常乐意与成员聊天并分享实用技巧。只是别指望他们回答像植物拉丁名这样真正的技术性问题——那不是他们的专长。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: We also want to make sure people with physical disabilities can join in. We're currently working on a scheme to loan out specially adapted gardening tools, so those who can't use standard equipment aren't left out. That service isn't quite ready yet, but at the moment, we do provide free window boxes and large containers. Members just need to bring their own soil and compost.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我们也想确保身体残疾的人可以参与。我们目前正在制定一项计划，出借经过特殊改造的园艺工具，这样那些不能使用标准设备的人不会被排除在外。这项服务还不太完善，但目前我们确实提供免费的窗台花盆和大容器。成员只需自带土壤和堆肥。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: One thing I'm especially proud of is what we've done with local schools---both primary and secondary. At first, teachers thought the scheme would just be handy for science lessons, and they were right about that. It hasn't lowered school meal costs like some hoped, but there's been an unexpected bonus: students have become much more aware of their environment, and they really want to keep public spaces clean and tidy.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我特别自豪的一件事是我们与当地学校——小学和中学——所做的工作。起初，老师们认为这个计划只对科学课有用，他们说得没错。它并没有像一些人希望的那样降低学校餐费，但有一个意想不到的额外收获：学生们对环境的意识大大提高了，他们真的想保持公共空间的干净整洁。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Outside schools, lots of businesses and organisations have been really generous, offering free resources and services. Let me give you a few examples. The city hospital, for instance---they prepare thousands of meals every day for patients---runs a course led by their kitchen manager. It teaches our members how to cook a wide range of dishes using vegetables.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在学校之外，许多企业和组织非常慷慨，提供免费资源和服务。让我举几个例子。例如，市医院——他们每天为病人准备数千顿饭——开设了一门由他们的厨房经理主讲的课程。它教我们的成员如何用蔬菜烹饪各种菜肴。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The local government's also been very supportive. They own a big glasshouse that the parks department normally use to grow flower seedlings in winter. They've now given MUFS members free access to it so we can get our own seedlings off to a good start.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：当地政府也非常支持。他们有一个大温室，公园部门通常冬天用来培育花苗。他们现在让MUFS成员免费使用，这样我们可以让我们的幼苗有一个良好的开端。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: And the university? They've been fantastic too. If our members send them a soil sample, they'll run tests to figure out the best plants, fertilisers, and nutrients for that specific soil.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大学呢？他们也棒极了。如果我们的成员给他们寄一份土壤样本，他们会进行测试，找出最适合那种特定土壤的植物、肥料和养分。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, and to top it off, a local supermarket is offering classes on how to lose weight and stay healthy with a sensible diet.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：哦，最重要的是，一家当地超市正在提供关于如何通过合理饮食减肥和保持健康的课程。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right---let's move on to the practical side of how the scheme works...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：好了——让我们继续谈谈这个计划如何运作的实际方面……

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Morning, Olive. I hear you wanted some feedback on your assignment?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：早上好，奥利芙。我听说你想要一些关于你作业的反馈？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's right. I've analysed different media platforms for advertising and pulled out some key points.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：是的。我分析了不同的广告媒体平台，并提炼出了一些关键点。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great, let's start.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：很好，我们开始吧。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: For the introduction, I'm planning to highlight one main advantage of each medium. Like with trade publications, the big plus is you're reaching your target audience---people already interested in the industry.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：对于引言，我计划突出每种媒体的一个主要优势。比如行业出版物，最大的好处是你能触及目标受众——已经对该行业感兴趣的人。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Exactly. That's why they're such a popular choice in the business community. So, did you look at email advertising?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：正是。这就是为什么它们在商界如此受欢迎。那么，你看过电子邮件广告吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yep! It's got lots of benefits, but the standout for me is how direct it is---you can send your message straight to people without going through any middlemen.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：是的！它有很多好处，但对我来说最突出的是它的直接性——你可以把信息直接发送给人们，无需通过任何中间人。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: True. Another bonus is you can give real-time updates with the latest information.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：没错。另一个好处是你可以提供最新信息的实时更新。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, but I didn't really want to focus on that because loads of media channels can do that now.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：是的，但我不想太关注这一点，因为现在很多媒体渠道都能做到。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Fair enough. What about general-interest magazines? How do you see them?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：有道理。那大众兴趣杂志呢？你怎么看它们？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, their biggest strength is they last longer than most other print media. Unlike newspapers that get tossed quickly, magazines hang around because of their high production quality---glossy pages, nice layouts, and things like that.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：嗯，它们最大的优势是比大多数其他印刷媒体寿命更长。不像报纸很快被扔掉，杂志因为其高质量的制作——光亮的纸张、漂亮的版面设计等——而留存更久。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good point. Not the greenest option, but they often get passed on rather than binned right away.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：说得好。虽然不是最环保的选择，但它们经常被传阅而不是马上被丢弃。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Moving on to websites, the advantages are pretty obvious---they make a business look modern and professional. But what I really want to stress is that a website gives you access to international markets.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：转向网站，优势很明显——它们让企业看起来现代而专业。但我真正想强调的是，网站让你进入国际市场。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Exactly---basically no limits at all.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：正是——基本上没有任何限制。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Then there's cinema advertising. The downside is the audience is too broad---you can't really target a specific group. But the huge plus is people can't skip it. They have to sit through the ad.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：然后是影院广告。缺点是受众太广泛——你无法真正针对特定群体。但巨大的优点是人们无法跳过。他们必须从头看到尾。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely. They can't just click away or walk out easily.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：绝对。他们不能随便点掉或轻易走出去。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: I also thought about trade fairs, but the problem is they only last a couple of days, so I wasn't sure what to focus on. Any ideas?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：我也考虑过交易会，但问题是它们只持续几天，所以我不确定该关注什么。有什么想法吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, think about their practical benefits. They're a brilliant way to make new contacts, exchange information, even bump into someone who'd be great to work with.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：嗯，想想它们的实际好处。它们是建立新联系、交流信息、甚至偶遇适合合作的人的绝佳方式。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, I didn't think of that!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：哦，我没想过这个！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Overall, Olive, your introduction sounds solid. Keep going.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：总的来说，奥利芙，你的引言听起来很扎实。继续。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Will do.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：我会的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right, let's talk about the main section of your assignment.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：好的，我们来谈谈你作业的主要部分。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: I've decided to focus on TV advertising.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：我决定专注于电视广告。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK. What angles are you going to cover, and why?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：好的。你打算涵盖哪些角度，为什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'll start with budgeting. I've found some good tips for planning TV ad budgets. Some are obvious---like it's way cheaper if the company can produce the ad in-house. But the most important one is setting aside a backup fund to keep campaigns running during a business downturn. That way you can maintain brand presence---even if you have to cut back on frequency or stick to off-peak hours.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：我会从预算开始。我找到了一些规划电视广告预算的好建议。有些很明显——比如如果公司能在内部制作广告会便宜得多。但最重要的是预留备用资金，以便在商业低迷时期保持活动运行。这样你就能维持品牌存在——即使你必须削减频率或坚持在非高峰时段投放。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Something's better than nothing. Smart move.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：有总比没有好。明智之举。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: I also wanted to include something about TV companies making ads, but I'm not sure it fits.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：我还想加入一些关于电视公司制作广告的内容，但我不确定是否合适。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, your reading list has an article on the benefits of working with TV companies to create ads. But does it really fit your focus?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：嗯，你的阅读清单上有一篇关于与电视公司合作制作广告的好处的文章。但它真的符合你的重点吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sort of. The thing is, I've only looked at American TV companies, not European or Asian ones.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：算是吧。问题是，我只看过美国电视公司，没有看欧洲或亚洲的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Then it might pull you off track if you go into all that.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：那如果你深入讲那些，可能会让你偏离主题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, I don't want to add another thousand words!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：是的，我可不想再增加一千字！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Fair enough. So, what methods do you think companies can use to check if their ads will work?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：有道理。那么，你认为公司可以用什么方法来检查他们的广告是否有效？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Past experience helps, but trends change. What worked last year might flop now because consumer behaviour shifts.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：过去的经验有帮助，但趋势会变化。去年有效的方法现在可能会失败，因为消费者行为在转变。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Very true. Anything else?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：非常正确。还有别的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: They could ask employees for keywords to describe the product and build those into the ad.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：他们可以询问员工描述产品的关键词，并将这些关键词融入广告中。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Or better still, show the ad to some clients, watch their reactions, and tweak it before launch.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：或者更好的是，把广告展示给一些客户，观察他们的反应，在发布前进行调整。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good idea! At the end of the day, customer feedback matters most. Oh---can I attach a video clip to my assignment?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：好主意！归根结底，客户反馈最重要。哦——我可以在作业中附上一段视频片段吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely---great idea! Just make sure you explain why it's relevant.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：当然可以——好主意！只要确保你解释为什么相关就行了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Got it. I've got one where the actor has this squeaky voice that totally clashes with the product it probably puts people off.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：明白了。我有一段视频，演员的声音很尖利，与产品完全不搭，可能会让人反感。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Perfect example. Same thing happens when the background music's wrong it kills the message. Include it, but explain why.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：完美的例子。背景音乐不对的时候也会发生同样的情况——它会毁了信息。加入它，但要解释原因。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: No problem.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：没问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Carlsen
transcriptSentences.englishText: Looks like you've got most of this figured out. Nice work!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡尔森博士：看起来你已经把大部分内容弄清楚了。做得好！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Olive
transcriptSentences.englishText: Thanks so much for your help!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 奥利芙：非常感谢你的帮助！

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Today, we're going to look at how adding drama activities---like role-play---into your teaching can bring all sorts of benefits across different subject areas. There's loads of evidence out there showing that drama can really help with a child's personal development.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：今天，我们将探讨将戏剧活动——如角色扮演——融入教学如何在不同学科领域带来各种好处。大量证据表明，戏剧确实有助于儿童的个性发展。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: To start with, giving children a chance to express themselves freely, especially in a group setting, helps build their confidence. It encourages them to share their own thoughts and ideas. This is especially helpful for those who are a bit shy or introverted - kids who might be reluctant to join in with more traditional classroom tasks. Just getting up and speaking or acting in front of their classmates---even in a fun or playful way---can gradually help them become more comfortable expressing themselves.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：首先，给孩子们自由表达的机会，尤其是在小组环境中，有助于建立他们的自信心。这鼓励他们分享自己的想法和意见。这对那些有点害羞或内向的孩子尤其有帮助——那些可能不愿意参与更传统课堂任务的孩子。只要在同学面前站起来说话或表演——即使是以有趣或好玩的方式——也能逐渐帮助他们更自如地表达自己。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Another great benefit comes from unscripted and improvised activities where kids use their imagination. When done in a supportive environment, these kinds of activities give them a chance to take creative risks without the fear of being judged. They can say what they're really thinking, even things they might usually keep to themselves. This kind of freedom helps them think more creatively---something that's really useful when they face new or unfamiliar situations.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：另一个巨大的好处来自无剧本和即兴活动，孩子们在其中发挥想象力。在支持性的环境中进行时，这类活动让他们有机会承担创造性风险，而不必担心被评判。他们可以说出自己真正的想法，甚至那些他们通常藏在心里的话。这种自由有助于他们更有创造性地思考——这在面对新的或不熟悉的情况时非常有用。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, drama isn't just about personal growth---it can also really support a child's learning. Because drama activities are usually done in groups, kids have to learn the skills of listening to each other and working together. In fact, success in drama often depends on good teamwork---everyone needs to play their part. When children learn to be more responsible, it can also affect their schoolwork and day-to-day behaviour. Of course, these are just some of the ways drama can help in the classroom. There's a lot more to explore, and I'd really encourage you to read up more on the topic after the lecture.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：戏剧不仅仅关乎个人成长——它也能真正支持孩子的学习。因为戏剧活动通常在小组中进行，孩子们必须学习倾听彼此和合作的技能。事实上，戏剧的成功往往取决于良好的团队合作——每个人都需要扮演好自己的角色。当孩子们学会更有责任感时，这也会影响他们的学业和日常行为。当然，这些只是戏剧在课堂上有所帮助的一些方式。还有更多值得探索，我真心鼓励你们在讲座后多阅读这方面的内容。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: So let's talk a bit more about role-play, which is one of the most powerful drama tools you can use with children. These days, it's widely recognised that role-play can be a great form of therapy for kids who might be going through tough times. When children act out situations that are similar to their own experiences but not exactly the same---it gives them a non-threatening space to reflect on their behaviour. They can think through what they've done, look at the choices they've made, and even try out different ways of dealing with challenges.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：那么让我们多谈谈角色扮演，这是你可以与孩子一起使用的最强大的戏剧工具之一。如今，人们普遍认为角色扮演对可能经历困难时期的孩子来说是一种很好的治疗形式。当孩子们表演与自己经历相似但不完全相同的场景时——这给他们一个没有威胁的空间来反思自己的行为。他们可以思考自己所做的事情，审视自己做出的选择，甚至尝试不同的应对挑战的方式。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: One really powerful technique is role reversal. For example, imagine a child who's been bullying others is asked to play the role of a victim in a classroom activity. It might sound simple, but it can have a real impact. Experiencing what it's like to be on the receiving end of that behaviour can help build empathy. It allows the child to understand how their actions affect others---without having to confront them directly or make them feel defensive.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：一个非常强大的技巧是角色反转。例如，想象一个曾经欺负别人的孩子被要求在课堂活动中扮演受害者的角色。听起来很简单，但能产生真正的效果。体验处于那种行为接收端的感觉有助于建立同理心。它让孩子理解自己的行为如何影响他人——而不必直接面对他们或让他们产生防御心理。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: More broadly, role-play also gives teachers a way to explore sensitive or even taboo topics in a safe environment. Children are more likely to open up and express their views when they feel they won't be judged. And when they do, it helps them think more deeply about their own opinions and values essentially, it builds their self-awareness and strengthens their sense of morality. These are key components of developing well-rounded social skills.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：更广泛地说，角色扮演也为教师提供了一种在安全环境中探索敏感甚至禁忌话题的方式。当孩子们感到自己不会被评判时，他们更可能敞开心扉表达自己的观点。当他们这样做时，这有助于他们更深入地思考自己的观点和价值观——本质上，这建立了他们的自我意识并增强了他们的道德感。这些是发展全面社交技能的关键组成部分。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, let's zoom in on a specific subject---history---and think about how drama can make history lessons more engaging. One of the best ways to bring the past to life is through classroom drama. When kids take part in re-enacting historical events or taking on the roles of key figures, it boosts their participation in the lesson.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：现在，让我们聚焦一个特定学科——历史——思考戏剧如何让历史课更有吸引力。让过去变得鲜活的最好方法之一就是通过课堂戏剧。当孩子们参与重演历史事件或扮演关键人物的角色时，这能提高他们在课堂上的参与度。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: But it's not just about having fun---it also helps with memory. For example, acting out a historical debate or a conflict helps students remember not just what happened, but why it happened. They explore the motivations behind decisions and the challenges people faced. It gives them a much deeper, more meaningful understanding of historical events---and makes the facts stick in their memory more easily.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：但这不仅仅是为了好玩——它也有助于记忆。例如，表演一场历史辩论或冲突，不仅帮助学生记住发生了什么，还记住为什么会发生。他们探索决策背后的动机和人们面临的挑战。这让他们对历史事件有了更深刻、更有意义的理解——也让事实更容易留在他们的记忆中。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: You can also get students to use role-play to solve historical problems. For instance, you might ask them to figure out how to defend a town under attack, or choose the best location for a new settlement. These kinds of tasks don't just teach history---they also help develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：你也可以让学生用角色扮演来解决历史问题。例如，你可以让他们想办法保卫一个被攻击的城镇，或者为新定居点选择最佳位置。这类任务不仅教授历史——它们也有助于培养批判性思维和解决问题的技能。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Alright, now it's time for some planning. I'd like you to break into groups and start brainstorming ideas on how you could include drama activities in your next teaching practice. Think creatively---and have fun with it!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：好的，现在到了规划时间。我想让你们分成小组，开始集思广益，思考如何将戏剧活动融入你们的下一次教学实践中。创造性思考——并享受这个过程！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Eli
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hi there. I've just moved to Avondale and I'm a bit confused about the waste collection. Could you please tell me how it works here?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 伊莱：你好。我刚搬到埃文代尔，对垃圾收集有点困惑。你能告诉我这里是怎么运作的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rue
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course! We've recently updated our collection schedule. Rubbish collection in Avondale was on Thursday, but we've shifted to Tuesday based on resident feedback. To ensure timely collection, we advise placing the waste at the designated collection points the night before.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 鲁：当然！我们最近更新了收集时间表。埃文代尔的垃圾收集原本在周四，但根据居民反馈改到了周二。为确保及时收集，我们建议在前一天晚上将垃圾放在指定的收集点。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Eli
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's great to know. What time does the collection usually start?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 伊莱：很高兴知道这个。收集通常几点开始？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rue
transcriptSentences.englishText: Our trucks are scheduled to commence operations at 8.15 am. Collection timing is set after the morning rush hour which is the busiest between 6.30 and 7.30 am. This helps avoid traffic problems and keeps things running smoothly.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 鲁：我们的卡车计划在上午8：15开始作业。收集时间设定在早高峰之后，早高峰最繁忙的时间是早上6：30到7：30之间。这有助于避免交通问题并保持运行顺畅。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Eli
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good! I have an old television to get rid of. How do I dispose of that properly?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 伊莱：好的！我有一台旧电视要处理。我该怎么正确处置它？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rue
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm afraid we are unable to offer the specialised facilities for recycling televisions. They require special handling. I recommend nearby retailers or local waste centres, as they often run recycling programmes for such items.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 鲁：恐怕我们无法提供回收电视机的专门设施。它们需要特殊处理。我推荐附近的零售商或当地废物中心，它们经常为这类物品开展回收项目。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Eli
transcriptSentences.englishText: Alright, I'll look into that. Well, do you provide a doorstep collection service for regular waste?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 伊莱：好的，我会去了解一下。那你们提供常规垃圾的上门收集服务吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rue
transcriptSentences.englishText: Actually, we've had to put that service on hold because we're short of staff at the moment. What I can tell you is that all the major rubbish collection sites are clearly marked on the map on our website, so you can quickly locate the nearest one.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 鲁：实际上，我们不得不暂停这项服务，因为目前人手不足。我能告诉你的是，所有主要垃圾收集点都在我们网站的地图上清楚标出，所以你可以快速找到最近的一个。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Eli
transcriptSentences.englishText: What steps should we follow to prepare recyclables properly?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 伊莱：我们应该遵循哪些步骤来正确准备可回收物？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rue
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, we strongly recommend using the specialised sorting bags available at grocery stores. They're great for keeping all your different recyclables separate, which really helps things run more smoothly at our facility.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 鲁：嗯，我们强烈建议使用杂货店有售的专用分类袋。它们非常有助于将不同类型的可回收物分开，这能让我们的设施运行更顺畅。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Eli
transcriptSentences.englishText: Cool! That's a good idea. How can families improve recycling effectiveness?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 伊莱：酷！这是个好主意。家庭如何提高回收效率？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rue
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, the main thing is just to make sure you're sorting everything into the right categories---you know, plastics, paper, and so on. That way, there's less contamination and the whole system works much better. Of course, trying to cut down on non-recyclable waste in the first place makes a big difference too.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 鲁：哦，主要的事情就是确保你把所有东西都分到正确的类别里——你知道，塑料、纸张等等。这样污染就更少，整个系统运行得更好。当然，首先尽量减少不可回收垃圾也会产生很大不同。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Eli
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's clear. For items like cans, bottles, and glass, are there any specific guidelines we should follow?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 伊莱：明白了。对于罐子、瓶子和玻璃之类的物品，有什么具体指南需要遵守吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rue
transcriptSentences.englishText: Definitely. The first thing to do is peel off any labels from bottles or cans---that helps us make higher-quality recycled products.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 鲁：当然有。首先要做的是撕掉瓶子或罐子上的任何标签——这有助于我们制造更高质量的回收产品。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Eli
transcriptSentences.englishText: Do I need to empty juice bottles, even if there's just a little bit left inside?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 伊莱：我需要清空果汁瓶吗，即使里面只剩一点点？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rue
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely, that's actually the second step! Any liquid left can contaminate other materials and cause a real mess. Plus, it makes the bottles lighter to carry. And also---please give them a quick rinse before tossing them in the bin. Even a little leftover liquid can gum up the whole process. Keeping things clean also helps keep recycling costs down.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 鲁：当然，这实际上是第二步！任何残留的液体都会污染其他材料并造成大麻烦。而且，这样瓶子搬起来也更轻。还有——请扔进垃圾桶前快速冲洗一下。即使一点点残留液体也会影响整个流程。保持清洁也有助于降低回收成本。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Eli
transcriptSentences.englishText: What about paper items like pizza boxes? How should I deal with those? Are they recyclable?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 伊莱：像披萨盒这样的纸质物品呢？我应该怎么处理？它们可回收吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rue
transcriptSentences.englishText: While most paper can be recycled, pizza boxes need to be free from any food residue. Even minor contamination can cause mould and make the recycling process harder. What's more, egg cartons require separate disposal, as they are made differently.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 鲁：虽然大多数纸张可以回收，但披萨盒必须没有任何食物残留。即使是轻微的污染也会导致发霉，使回收过程更加困难。更重要的是，鸡蛋盒需要单独处理，因为它们的制作材料不同。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Eli
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's really helpful. Thank you for all the advice. It's great to know how much of a difference small actions can make.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 伊莱：这真的很有帮助。谢谢你的所有建议。知道小行动能带来多大的不同真是太好了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rue
transcriptSentences.englishText: You're very welcome. If you have any more questions, feel free to reach out.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 鲁：不客气。如果你还有其他问题，随时联系。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Presenter
transcriptSentences.englishText: Welcome back to our regular coverage of local events. Today, we're joined by Jake Connelly, who's been exploring our local music scene. Jake, I hear you've been diving into our community choir activities recently and had quite the adventure!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 主持人：欢迎回到我们定期的地方活动报道。今天，杰克·康纳利加入了我们，他一直在探索我们当地的音乐场景。杰克，我听说你最近深入参与了我们的社区合唱团活动，经历了一场相当精彩的冒险！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely! I've got to admit, I was a little nervous at first about my singing skills, but I decided to go for it and joined rehearsals at the town's three biggest choirs: the Mitchell's Town Choir, the Blackvale Male Voice Choir, and the Caroline Singers. What really struck In fact, all three groups are currently looking for new members who love singing. It's a great way to break away from your routine and try something completely new.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：确实！我得承认，一开始我对自己的歌唱技巧有点紧张，但我决定去试试，参加了镇上三个最大的合唱团的排练：米切尔镇合唱团、布莱克维尔男声合唱团和卡罗琳歌手合唱团。事实上，这三个团体目前都在寻找热爱歌唱的新成员。这是打破日常惯例、尝试全新事物的好方法。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Presenter
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's wonderful to hear! So, how did you choose between them?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 主持人：听起来太好了！那么，你是怎么在他们之间做选择的？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: Actually, choosing the right choir really depends on your musical taste. Both Blackvale and Mitchell's Town offer a wide range of music styles. But, if you're more into classical music, Caroline Singers might be the best fit, as they tend to focus on madrigals -those are sung without instruments. Besides the musical styles, these choirs also offer some pretty unique opportunities outside of just performing. If you're looking to connect with fellow music lovers, Mitchell's Town is a great choice. Beyond performances, they also organise group outings to operas and music festivals---a great way to socialise and meet new people. But it's not all fun and singing there're also chances to win awards! For example, Mitchell's Town is hoping to make it to the finals of the Melody Competition in Atlanta. Meanwhile, Blackvale currently holds the Counter Male Voice Choir Award, presented by the director of the London Opera. Another exciting opportunity is the chance to record music. Unlike Blackvale and Caroline Singers, who have already recorded their own albums, Mitchell's Town has just finished recording their first CD, set to be released in December. Additionally, if you're interested in giving back to the community, joining a choir is a great way to do that. Mitchell's Town often performs for seniors and people with disabilities, while Blackvale donates a portion of its profits to local charities.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：实际上，选择合适的合唱团真的取决于你的音乐品味。布莱克维尔和米切尔镇都提供广泛的音乐风格。但如果你更喜欢古典音乐，卡罗琳歌手可能是最合适的，因为它们倾向于专注于牧歌——那是无伴奏演唱的。除了音乐风格，这些合唱团在表演之外还提供一些相当独特的机会。如果你想与其他音乐爱好者建立联系，米切尔镇是个不错的选择。除了表演之外，他们还组织去歌剧和音乐节的团体出游——这是社交和结识新朋友的好方式。但这并不全是乐趣和歌唱——也有机会获奖！例如，米切尔镇希望进入亚特兰大旋律比赛的决赛。同时，布莱克维尔目前拥有对唱男声合唱团奖，由伦敦歌剧院院长颁发。另一个激动人心的机会是录制音乐的机会。与已经录制了自己专辑的布莱克维尔和卡罗琳歌手不同，米切尔镇刚刚完成了他们的第一张CD录制，计划在12月发行。此外，如果你有兴趣回馈社区，加入合唱团是一个很好的方式。米切尔镇经常为老年人和残疾人表演，而布莱克维尔将其部分利润捐赠给当地慈善机构。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Presenter
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, some might think, 'I'd love to join, but my time is completely taken up by work and family.' Is there a practical solution for busy people?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 主持人：现在，有些人可能会想：“我很想加入，但我的时间完全被工作和家庭占据了。”对于忙碌的人来说，有什么实际的解决方案吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes---starting a choir at work! It's a growing trend at companies of all sizes, and I visited the choir at John White, an accounting firm, to learn more. I spoke with the choir's organiser, Brenna Jensen, who explained why people enjoy joining a workplace choir. She mentioned that while some folks might see it as a good opportunity to network or practise singing, it really allows people to switch off and focus on something completely different. Research isn't conclusive on whether choirs boost staff loyalty or attendance. But companies like John White actually encourage employees to start choirs because it can help create a healthier working environment. For instance, co-workers who barely interacted before often bond and grow closer through rehearsals. Brenna also stressed you can start small. They started four years ago with only five members. Now they have 19, with about 12 people attending rehearsals. Many people can't make it after work, but they manage to fit it in during working hours.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：是的——在工作场所组建合唱团！这是各种规模公司中日益增长的趋势，我参观了约翰怀特（一家会计师事务所）的合唱团来了解更多。我与合唱团的组织者布伦娜·詹森谈了谈，她解释了为什么人们喜欢加入工作场所合唱团。她提到，虽然有些人可能认为这是建立社交网络或练习歌唱的好机会，但它实际上让人们可以放下工作，专注于完全不同的东西。关于合唱团是否能提高员工忠诚度或出勤率，研究尚无定论。但像约翰怀特这样的公司实际上鼓励员工组建合唱团，因为它有助于创造更健康的工作环境。例如，以前几乎没有互动的同事往往通过排练建立联系并变得更加亲近。布伦娜还强调可以从小规模开始。他们四年前开始只有五名成员。现在有19人，大约12人参加排练。很多人下班后没时间，但他们设法在工作时间内安排。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Presenter
transcriptSentences.englishText: And how do workplace choirs actually schedule rehearsals to make this work? You know, with everyone's busy schedules?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 主持人：那工作场所合唱团实际上是怎么安排排练来让这行得通的？你知道，每个人都很忙？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jake
transcriptSentences.englishText: At John White, midday works best since not everyone's on the same schedule. Early mornings or late afternoons can be tough for some people. John White is more than willing to support the choir. Members need to pay a small joining fee for refreshments and special choir shirts, while the company brings in a professional vocal coach for regular sessions, free for choir members. Well, if you're thinking about joining or starting a choir, just take that first step!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：在约翰怀特，中午效果最好，因为不是每个人的日程都相同。清晨或傍晚对有些人来说可能很困难。约翰怀特非常愿意支持合唱团。成员需要支付少量入会费用于茶点和特别合唱团衬衫，而公司会聘请专业的声乐教练定期授课，对合唱团成员免费。好了，如果你在考虑加入或组建合唱团，就迈出第一步吧！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: Rose, you know, that career mentoring initiative? I think it's such an excellent concept, don't you? I mean, for language students like us, it's incredibly beneficial to connect with proper practitioners in industries we aspire to join after graduation.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：罗斯，你知道那个职业指导计划吗？我觉得这是个非常好的理念，你不觉得吗？我是说，对于我们这样的语言专业学生来说，与毕业后想进入的行业的实际从业者建立联系是非常有益的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, absolutely! I'd say it's been probably one of the most valuable experiences we've had this year.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：哦，绝对！我会说这可能是我们今年最有价值的经历之一。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, how did you first hear about this programme? Was it through the university or someone you know?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：那么，你最初是怎么听说这个项目的？是通过大学还是通过你认识的人？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I came across the programme details online after someone on my course recommended it, so I decided to just give it a go. What about you, Jack?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：嗯，我是在网上看到项目详情的，是课程上有人推荐的，所以我决定试试看。你呢，杰克？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: A friend in my tutorial group mentioned it, and after that our tutor thought it would be a great opportunity for everyone. She even shared some success stories from previous participants.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：我辅导课上的一个朋友提到了它，之后我们的导师觉得这对每个人来说都是个很好的机会。她甚至分享了一些往期参与者的成功故事。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Cool. But I don't remember seeing you at the orientation session, you know, the one where they assigned mentors and explained how to get the most out of the mentoring framework.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：酷。但我不记得在迎新会上看到你，你知道，就是分配导师并解释如何充分利用指导框架的那次。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, I was there, but arrived a bit late. It was a nuisance for me that it was held so far from the campus centre.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：哦，我去了，但到得有点晚。对我来说它离校园中心那么远有点麻烦。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Definitely a long walk! I ended up missing half of my Spanish translation seminar later that afternoon. Fortunately, the meeting was worthwhile, wasn't it?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：确实要走很远！结果我错过了那天下午西班牙语翻译研讨课的一半。幸运的是，那次会议很值得，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah. Most participants appear to have benefited from it. I've heard loads of positive feedback from others in our year.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：是的。大多数参与者似乎都从中受益。我听到我们这一年级的其他人的很多积极反馈。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Actually, I've been wondering---what motivated the mentors to get involved? It must be quite challenging for them to fit this in alongside their already busy careers.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：实际上，我一直在想——是什么促使导师们参与进来的？对他们来说，在已经很忙的职业之余安排这个一定很有挑战性。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: I hope it's fulfilling for them too. But from what I have heard, most mentors agreed to participate because they wanted to give back to the university since they were alumni themselves.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：我希望这对他们来说也有成就感。但据我所知，大多数导师同意参与是因为他们想回馈大学，因为他们自己就是校友。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Interesting. I always assumed their main goal was to help graduates enter specific fields they're passionate about.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：有意思。我一直以为他们的主要目标是帮助毕业生进入他们热爱的特定领域。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: By the way, how did you usually communicate with your mentor? Did you meet up in person or mostly talk online?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：顺便问一下，你通常怎么和你的导师交流？是见面还是主要在网上聊？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Mostly online, which worked quite well. It was great because I could still see him even though he lives right at the other end of the country. How about you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：主要是线上，效果很好。很好的是即使他住在国家的另一端，我也能见到他。你呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: We tried the same, but it didn't work out too well for us. So we switched to emailing each other once a week. This method suited me better because it gave me time to reflect on her questions thoroughly, rather than having to come up with an answer straight away.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：我们也试过同样的方式，但对我们来说效果不太好。所以我们改成了每周邮件联系一次。这种方式更适合我，因为它给了我时间仔细思考她的问题，而不是必须马上给出答案。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sounds great. Well, my first interaction with my mentor was interesting but a bit challenging.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：听起来不错。嗯，我和导师的第一次互动很有趣但也有点挑战性。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: Maybe it's because you weren't clear on your goals initially? I faced similar confusion at the start.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：也许是因为你一开始目标不明确？我一开始也遇到了类似的困惑。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Luckily, that wasn't an issue for me. As my mentor had taken the same course, he really got my situation. It was just that I misunderstood one of his questions and gave some idiotic answers. Anyway, it all got much better once I got the hang of it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：幸运的是，那对我来说不是问题。因为我的导师上过同样的课程，他真的很理解我的情况。只是我误解了他一个问题，给了一些愚蠢的回答。总之，一旦我掌握要领后就好多了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: Overall, did your mentor influence your original plans much?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：总的来说，你的导师对你的原计划影响大吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Let me think... No, not really. Did yours?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：让我想想……不，不太大。你的呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: She didn't comment on my dissertation topic choice. But she did make me reconsider my intention to get a job in France next year. I've also decided to take some different modules next term, but that wasn't really based on her advice.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：她没有评论我的论文选题。但她确实让我重新考虑了明年在法国找工作的打算。我也决定下学期选一些不同的模块，但那不是基于她的建议。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, what specific topics did you talk about with your mentor? For me, she was really helpful with my CV, and we also worked on improving my interview skills.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：那么，你和导师具体谈了哪些话题？对我来说，她在我的简历上帮了大忙，我们也一起提高了我的面试技巧。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: We did too. I mean about the interviews rather than the CV. Although I'd already mapped out a five-year career plan, my mentor gave me some really valuable advice about choosing a master's programme after graduation.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：我们也谈了。我是说关于面试而不是简历。虽然我已经规划了五年的职业计划，但我的导师给了我一些关于毕业后选择硕士项目非常宝贵的建议。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm not planning on a postgraduate degree myself. The best part was figuring out what I'm skilled at and what I need to work on to get ahead in this field.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：我自己不打算读研究生。最好的部分是弄清楚我擅长什么，以及我需要努力改进什么才能在这个领域取得进步。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, my mentor started by making me think about that too, which was actually really revealing for me. So, for the programme next year, there's definitely room for improvement. What would you suggest? There was a suggestion to have an initial face-to-face meeting with all mentors and students, but I reckon it's not really necessary. The student-only briefing we had was spot-on for giving us a sense of what's to come.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：是的，我的导师也让我从思考那点开始，这对我来说确实很有启发性。那么，对于明年的项目，肯定有改进的空间。你有什么建议？有人建议所有导师和学生先进行一次面对面的会议，但我认为这真的没有必要。我们只对学生开的简报会让我们对即将发生的事情有了很好的了解。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: I completely agree. Though, I wish the programme had kicked off right at the start of the academic year instead of halfway through. This would allow earlier engagement.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：我完全同意。不过，我希望项目能在学年一开始就启动，而不是到一半才开始。这样可以更早参与。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Rose
transcriptSentences.englishText: Fair enough. They did alright matching us up with mentors, nevertheless, perhaps they needed a bit more training for the mentors. Mine was great, but not everyone had the same luck.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 罗斯：有道理。他们在给我们匹配导师方面做得还可以，不过，也许他们需要对导师进行更多培训。我的导师很棒，但不是每个人都有同样的运气。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jack
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's true. Well, some mentors took on one student this term, while others had two or more. But it doesn't appear to have made much difference, so it's probably not worth worrying about. Okay, let's...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 杰克：确实。嗯，这学期有些导师带了一个学生，而有些带了两个或更多。但这似乎没有产生太大影响，所以可能不值得担心。好了，让我们……

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello, everyone! Welcome to today's session on our Textiles with Business Studies course. This innovative course actually results from a collaboration between the Faculty of Arts and Architecture and the Business School, allowing us to offer this undergraduate and integrated Master's course.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家好！欢迎来到今天的课程介绍，主题是我们的纺织与商业研究课程。这门创新课程实际上是艺术与建筑学院和商学院合作的成果，使我们能够提供这门本科和综合硕士课程。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: As the course has undergone significant development over the years, we have gained valuable experience. Its growing popularity is clearly evidenced by the number of participants here today. Now, through a new partnership with the Faculty of Engineering, we're also able to offer a really exciting opportunity to those who would like to further diversify and carry their learning forward into new disciplines.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：随着这门课程多年来的显著发展，我们积累了宝贵的经验。它日益增长的受欢迎程度显然可以从今天在座的参与者数量看出。现在，通过与工程学院的新的合作关系，我们也能够为那些希望进一步多样化并将学习延伸到新学科的人提供一个非常激动人心的机会。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The primary objective of this course is to cultivate forward-thinking and highly motivated textile practitioners within the disciplines of knitted textiles, an increasingly popular area, as you can see on the catwalks textiles, and of course woven textiles.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：这门课程的主要目标是在针织纺织（一个日益流行的领域，正如你在时装秀上看到的那样）、纺织，当然还有机织纺织等学科中培养有远见、积极进取的纺织从业者。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Beyond technical skills, we equip our students with a comprehensive understanding of business practices integral to the textile sector. To make sure students are industry-ready, we incorporate practical work placements into the curriculum, providing hands-on experience relevant to their future careers. A key feature of these placements is their focus on the global market. We aim to position studio work within this increasingly vital context.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：除了技术技能，我们还为学生提供对纺织行业不可或缺的商业实践的全面理解。为了确保学生做好行业准备，我们将实际工作实习纳入课程，提供与未来职业相关的实践经验。这些实习的一个关键特点是它们对全球市场的关注。我们的目标是将工作室工作置于这个日益重要的背景下。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Let's now discuss the structure of the course, starting with the first year. During this year, students are introduced to three core textile disciplines through a rotation of modules. The main emphasis is on experimentation and exploration, and students are required to present evidence of visual research which must be supported by documentation and proposals for its application. This foundational year sets the stage for more advanced learning in subsequent years. In the second year, students apply their design and technical skills to real-world scenarios. A distinctive feature of our programme is the opportunity to choose an extra module on the traditional processes of design. We've found this provides a crucial historical perspective on their work. This is especially useful before introducing students to more advanced techniques, such as computer-aided design. At the end of the second year, students face an important choice: they can either complete the course after the third year with a Bachelor of Arts degree, or continue into the fourth year and earn a Master of Design degree. Students can also have tutorials to help them with that decision. We are always committed to providing comprehensive support for our students throughout their academic journey.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：现在让我们讨论课程结构，从第一年开始。在这一年，学生通过模块轮换接触三个核心纺织学科。主要重点是实验和探索，学生需要展示视觉研究的证据，必须有文件记录和应用建议作为支持。这一基础年为后续几年的更高级学习奠定了基础。在第二年，学生将设计和技术技能应用到现实场景中。我们课程的一个显著特点是可以选择一个关于传统设计过程的额外模块。我们发现这为他们的作品提供了至关重要的历史视角。这在向学生介绍更高级技术（如计算机辅助设计）之前尤其有用。在第二年结束时，学生面临一个重要选择：他们可以在第三年后完成课程获得文学士学位，或者继续进入第四年获得设计硕士学位。学生也可以参加辅导课来帮助他们做决定。我们始终致力于在整个学术旅程中为学生提供全面的支持。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The third year is dedicated to consolidating the knowledge gained through a method known as reflective practice. This approach encourages students to look back on their work, critically analyse and evaluate their experiences, and deepen their understanding in both academic and professional contexts. During this year, students are required to produce a dissertation on a topic of their choice, as well as a portfolio showcasing their textile collections. In addition, to support the commercial aspect of the course, students need to submit a business plan on potential career opportunities.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：第三年致力于通过一种称为反思实践的方法来巩固所获得的知识。这种方法鼓励学生回顾他们的作品，批判性地分析和评估他们的经验，并在学术和专业背景下加深理解。在这一年，学生需要就自己选择的主题撰写一篇论文，以及展示他们纺织作品集的作品集。此外，为了支持课程的商业方面，学生需要提交一份关于潜在职业机会的商业计划。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Many of our graduates go on to pursue careers directly within the textile industry, with roles such as stylists and retail managers being common. In fact, the career opportunities for our graduates extend far beyond these traditional roles. For example, careers in journalism for those with a talent for words, or trend forecasting for those with their eyes on the future. Looking ahead, we are confident that the scope of opportunities for our graduates will continue to expand, and we are excited to see where their careers will take them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我们的许多毕业生直接进入纺织行业从事职业，常见的职位有造型师和零售经理等。事实上，我们毕业生的职业机会远远超出这些传统角色。例如，有文字天赋的人可以从事新闻工作，有远见的人可以从事趋势预测。展望未来，我们有信心毕业生的机会范围将继续扩大，我们期待看到他们的职业发展。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: If you're interested in applying to this programme and would like to discuss it further, we invite you to return tomorrow for a brief interview. This will allow us to assess your suitability for the course and provide you with personalised feedback to guide your application. Many students who haven't previously studied textiles or business are often pleasantly surprised to discover how well their skills fit the programme. Following that, you'll proceed with the standard application process. We look forward to potentially welcoming you to our vibrant academic community.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：如果你有兴趣申请这个项目并希望进一步讨论，我们邀请你明天回来进行简短的面试。这将让我们评估你是否适合这门课程，并为你提供个性化反馈以指导你的申请。许多以前没有学过纺织或商科的学生经常惊喜地发现他们的技能非常适合这个项目。之后，你将进入标准申请流程。我们期待有可能欢迎你加入我们充满活力的学术社区。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning, Future Guard Insurance. Julie speaking. How can I help you today?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：早上好，未来卫士保险公司。我是朱莉。今天能为您效劳吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Morning, Julie. I've got an insurance policy with you and I'm calling to make a claim.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：早上好，朱莉。我在你们这里买了保险，打电话来理赔。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure. Let's get you sorted. Is this for your car, your home, or something else?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：好的。我们来处理。是汽车保险、房屋保险还是其他？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: It's for my home insurance.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：是房屋保险。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Got it. I'll just need to confirm a few details, so I can pull up your file. Could I have your reference number?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：明白了。我需要确认一些细节，以便调出您的档案。能告诉我您的参考编号吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, it's JXY465773.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：好的，是JXY465773。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Thanks. And the name on the policy?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：谢谢。保单上的姓名是？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's Maximo Black.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：马克西莫·布莱克。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great. Can you give me the address you've got on file?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：好的。能告诉我您留档的地址吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: 89 Crown Road.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：皇冠路89号。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Crown as in a royal crown?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：皇冠是 royal crown 的那个 crown吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Exactly.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：正是。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Perfect. That's in Bampton, right? Everything matches so far. And the postcode?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：好的。是在班普顿，对吧？目前所有信息都对得上。邮编是？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: BA43 9TH.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：BA43 9TH。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Thanks for that. Just scrolling through your account... Ah, I see you've made a claim with us before. Is that right?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：谢谢。我在翻阅您的账户记录……啊，我看到您之前在我们这里理赔过。对吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah. Someone broke in and took my son's bicycle, even though it was locked up in the garage. Luckily they didn't take the car. Bit of a hassle, but the claim went smoothly. That was a relief.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：是的。有人闯进来偷了我儿子的自行车，虽然它锁在车库里。幸好他们没偷车。有点麻烦，但理赔过程很顺利。那让我松了一口气。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: And that was in the last 12 months, wasn't it?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：那是在过去12个月内，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hmm... yeah, about 10 months back. We've been extra careful since then, but now we've got a new problem.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：嗯……是的，大约10个月前。之后我们格外小心了，但现在又有了新问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sorry to hear that.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：很抱歉听到这个。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right, let's talk about this claim. Can you tell me what happened?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：好的，我们来说说这次理赔。能告诉我发生了什么吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, we were away at my parents' over the weekend. When we came back last night, we opened the front door and were met with... chaos. The place was flooded. Pretty bad.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：嗯，我们周末去我父母家了。昨晚回来时，打开前门，迎接我们的是一片……狼藉。房子被淹了。相当严重。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh no, that sounds awful. What sort of damage are we talking about?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：哦不，听起来真糟糕。是什么样的损坏？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: The hallway ceiling had partially collapsed, with water dripping through. We were just stunned.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：走廊天花板部分坍塌了，水直往下滴。我们当时都惊呆了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: I can imagine. Did you check other rooms straight away?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：我能想象。你马上检查了其他房间吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah. We ran upstairs to see what was going on. The bathroom floor was soaked. Worse still, water had seeped through into the bedroom. The carpet wasn't totally ruined, but the wall was covered in water stains.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：是的。我们跑到楼上看看发生了什么。浴室地板全湿了。更糟的是，水已经渗到了卧室。地毯没有完全毁掉，但墙上全是水渍。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sounds like the leak had been going for a while. Did you find out the cause?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：听起来漏水已经持续一段时间了。你们找到原因了吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, we got a plumber in first thing this morning. He found a leaking pipe in the upstairs bathroom. Said it was old and worn out probably been slowly dripping for days.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：找到了，我们一早请了水管工来。他在楼上浴室发现了一根漏水的管子。说那根管子老旧磨损了，可能已经慢慢滴了好几天了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's frustrating. Water damage can be a real headache. Did you take any photos?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：那真让人恼火。水损真的很麻烦。你们拍照了吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh yes, loads. The plumber even took a few for his records.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：哦是的，拍了很多。水管工还拍了几张做记录。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great. That'll help with the claim. We'll send a loss adjuster round to check the damage. Let's see... the earliest we can do is Tuesday morning. Does that work for you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：太好了。那对理赔有帮助。我们会派一位损失理算员去检查损坏情况。让我看看……最早可以安排的是周二上午。您方便吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: That should be fine. I'm busy this afternoon and Wednesday, but I'll make sure someone's home for the inspection.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：应该没问题。我今天下午和周三很忙，但我会确保有人在家配合检查。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Perfect. Anything else I should know?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：好的。还有别的我需要知道的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes---our main entrance is actually on the side of the building, not the front. Could be tricky to find. There's a supermarket right across the street you can use as a landmark. I'll also put a note on the front door with directions.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：是的——我们的大门其实在楼侧面，不在正面。可能不太好找。街对面有一家超市，可以作为地标。我也会在前门贴一张带指引的便条。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Brilliant. I'll pass that on to the adjuster. Once the inspection's done, we'll process the claim and keep you updated by email.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：好的。我会转告理算员。检查完成后，我们会处理理赔，并通过邮件通知您进展。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: OK. Sounds good.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：好的。听起来不错。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, one more thing---make sure you keep receipts if you have to buy anything to secure the property before we pay out.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：哦，还有一件事——如果在我们赔付之前您需要购买任何东西来保护房产，请保留好收据。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Got it. Thanks for the tip.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：明白了。谢谢提醒。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: No problem. That's all from my side. If you think of anything else, just give us a ring.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：不客气。我这边就这些了。如果您还有其他问题，随时给我们打电话。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Will do. Thanks for your help, Julie.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：好的。谢谢你的帮助，朱莉。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julie
transcriptSentences.englishText: You're welcome. Take care, and I hope the repairs go smoothly. Bye now.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉：不客气。保重，希望维修一切顺利。再见。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Maximo
transcriptSentences.englishText: Bye.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马克西莫：再见。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hi everyone! It's great to see so many familiar faces---and quite a few new ones---here today. I'm Laura Wilson, and I head up the External Partnerships Office here at River Mead School. I'm really excited to share some good news with you. We've decided to open up some of our campus facilities to the local community, which we think will help us build an even stronger connection with the people we're proud to be part of. I'll take just a few minutes to give you a quick run-through of what's on offer.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家好！很高兴今天看到这么多熟悉的面孔——还有不少新面孔。我是劳拉·威尔逊，负责里弗米德学校的对外合作办公室。我很高兴能与大家分享一些好消息。我们决定向当地社区开放部分校园设施，我们认为这将帮助我们与那些我们自豪地成为其中一员的人们建立更紧密的联系。我会花几分钟时间简要介绍一下所提供的设施。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: First up, our brand-new theatre. The idea behind it is to give local audiences more chances to see top-quality productions. As well as being a venue for local professional drama companies, we're also planning to bring in both national and international groups---from up-and-coming companies to ones that are already well-known.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：首先是我们的全新剧院。其背后的理念是为本地观众提供更多观看高质量演出的机会。除了作为本地专业剧团演出场所外，我们还计划引进国内和国际的剧团——从新兴剧团到已广为人知的剧团。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The programme for our first season is already online, and I think you'll be impressed. Alongside music and dance, we'll have plays by contemporary writers, and a good chunk of the shows will be aimed at kids and families. You might notice that November's looking a bit empty---that's because the Canadian State Acrobatic Troupe had to cancel their visit. But don't worry---we're working on booking a replacement, and we'll share the details soon.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：我们第一季的节目单已经在网上了，我想你们会感兴趣的。除了音乐和舞蹈，我们还将上演当代剧作家的作品，很大一部分演出将面向儿童和家庭。你们可能注意到11月份看起来有点空——那是因为加拿大国家杂技团不得不取消了他们的访问。但别担心——我们正在预订替代演出，会尽快分享细节。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: People often ask us about how the theatre's funded. We do get a bit of money from government subsidies, but most of it will come from ticket sales. That's why we'd really appreciate it if you could help spread the word the bigger our audiences, the more we can invest back into the theatre. And if you want to support us on a regular basis, you can join our sponsorship scheme. Sponsors get perks like behind-the-scenes access to rehearsals and early previews of upcoming shows.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：人们经常问我们剧院是如何获得资金的。我们确实从政府补贴中获得一些资金，但大部分将来自门票销售。这就是为什么我们非常希望你们能帮忙宣传——观众越多，我们能投入剧院的资金就越多。如果你愿意定期支持我们，可以加入我们的赞助计划。赞助者可以获得幕后参观排练和即将上演节目的早期预览等特权。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: But it's not just the theatre; we've also got a small museum here on campus, showcasing historical artefacts---many of them found when the school was being built. It's completely free to visit. We also have a modern, fully equipped sports hall. Students use it during term time, but it's open to the public during the school holidays. And don't forget our cafeteria---it's a bit of a social serving a range of food and drinks every day for staff and visitors. Definitely worth a stop!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：但不仅仅是剧院；我们校园里还有一个小型博物馆，展示历史文物——其中许多是在学校建造时发现的。参观完全免费。我们还有一个现代化、设备齐全的体育馆。学生在上课期间使用，但在学校假期向公众开放。别忘了我们的食堂——它有点像一个社交中心，每天为员工和访客提供各种食品和饮料。绝对值得一去！

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right, let me talk you through the campus map you've got in front of you. The theatre's opposite Car Park P2, on the south side. Just a reminder---you can only park in the designated areas, P1 and P2. We've also added a brand-new car park right at the northern end of the campus, which should make it easier to find a space when things get busy.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：好的，让我给你们讲解一下面前的校园地图。剧院在P2停车场的对面，在南侧。提醒一下——你们只能在指定区域P1和P2停车。我们在校园最北端增加了一个全新的停车场，这样在人流拥挤时应该更容易找到车位。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: If you're coming by bus, there's a regular service from the city centre to the school. It stops at the roundabout where the bus turns around---that's your stop, as it doesn't go further up to Park Road.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：如果乘坐公交车，从市中心有定期班车到学校。它在公交车掉头的环岛处停靠——那就是你们的站点，因为它不再继续驶向公园路。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: To get to the sports hall, take the right fork just after you come through the main entrance, go past the classroom block, then straight across the roundabout. You'll find the sports hall a bit further along on your right. It's a big, well-equipped space---perfect for anything from basketball to badminton.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：去体育馆的话，从正门进入后在第一个岔路口走右边，经过教学楼，然后直行穿过环岛。再往前走一点，体育馆就在你们右手边。这是一个宽敞、设备齐全的场地——适合从篮球到羽毛球等各类运动。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The cafeteria is at the corner of Park Road and Renne's Drive, on the north side of Park Road. There are a few different ways to get there. And if the weather's nice, you can eat outside and enjoy the lovely views of the campus---it's a great spot to relax.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：食堂在公园路和伦恩路的拐角处，公园路北侧。有几条不同的路线可以到达那里。如果天气好，你可以在户外用餐，欣赏校园的美景——这是一个放松的好地方。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: As for the museum, it's pretty central. From the main entrance, turn left, then take the first right, and you'll see it straight ahead at the junction. That's about it from me---I'm happy to take any questions you've got.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：至于博物馆，它在相当中心的位置。从正门出发，左转，然后第一个路口右转，你会看到它就在交叉路口正前方。我就说这些了——我很乐意回答你们的任何问题。
