transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello, Dr Mahoney. Do you have a moment? I've got a few questions about my assignment and I'd really like your feedback.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：你好，马奥尼博士。您有时间吗？我关于作业有几个问题，很想听听您的反馈。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course, Zoey. That's what I'm here for. I've just finished reading through your essay on global marketing. Overall, it's nicely written, and I have to say I'm impressed.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：当然，佐伊。这就是我的工作。我刚读完你关于全球营销的论文。总体而言，写得很好，我得说我很欣赏。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, that's such a relief to hear. Thanks so much. When you gave us the task last week, the first idea that popped into my head was to focus on the chocolate industry.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：哦，听到这个我松了口气。非常感谢。上周您给我们布置任务时，我脑海里的第一个想法是聚焦于巧克力行业。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: A smart choice. It's a sector with plenty to explore. I liked that you brought advertising into the discussion---it plays a huge role in marketing. And you highlighted the importance of the domestic market right at the beginning, which was excellent. But one thing you didn't touch on was how different flavours or ingredients of chocolate perform in different markets. That can have a big influence on the sales figures across countries.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：明智的选择。这是一个有很多值得探索的行业。我喜欢你把广告带入讨论——它在营销中起着重要作用。你在开头就强调了国内市场的重要性，这很好。但你没有涉及的一点是巧克力不同的口味或配料在不同市场的表现。这可能会对各国销售数据产生很大影响。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: Ah, you're right. Honestly, I didn't think that was something I needed to cover. I'll make sure to include it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：啊，您说得对。老实说，我没觉得那是我需要涵盖的内容。我会确保把它加进去。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good. You know, the global market is vital for many multinational companies. As they fight to grow their market share, the competition just gets fiercer.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：好的。要知道，全球市场对许多跨国公司至关重要。随着它们努力扩大市场份额，竞争只会更加激烈。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, I suppose product quality and smart marketing strategies are the real drivers of sales, right?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：那么，我认为产品质量和明智的营销策略才是销售的真正驱动力，对吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, partly. But actually, the key to long-term performance in international markets is making sure the company is profitable both at home and abroad. Without steady revenue streams, businesses simply don't have the resources---or the motivation---to expand.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：嗯，部分正确。但实际上，在国际市场取得长期业绩的关键是确保公司在国内外都盈利。没有稳定的收入来源，企业就没有资源——也没有动力——去扩张。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: That makes sense. I read about a case where some companies really struggled with overseas campaigns. There was this chocolate brand that spent heavily on international advertising. Even though they kept a strong brand image and followed global standards, sales were disappointing because the campaign ignored the actual needs of local customers.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：有道理。我读过一个案例，一些公司在海外推广中确实遇到了困难。有一个巧克力品牌在国际广告上投入巨大。尽管他们保持了强大的品牌形象并遵循全球标准，但销售令人失望，因为该推广活动忽视了当地客户的实际需求。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: Exactly. That's a classic mistake. If companies don't understand their target demographic, no amount of spending will save them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：正是。这是一个经典错误。如果公司不了解目标人群，花再多钱也救不了他们。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: What's interesting is that this chocolate company was originally Brazilian. But investors from our country bought it two years ago.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：有趣的是，这家巧克力公司最初是巴西的。但两年前我们国家的投资者收购了它。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, I remember that acquisition. Once the new investors stepped in, they introduced a whole set of new management policies.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：是的，我记得那次收购。新投资者接手后，他们引入了一整套新的管理政策。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right. Some of those policies were fine, but they replaced all the Brazilian managers with their own people, assuming they'd handle the local regulations better. That move could cause some serious complications.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：是的。其中一些政策还不错，但他们用自己的人替换了所有巴西经理，认为他们能更好地处理当地法规。这一举动可能会引起一些严重的复杂情况。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: I think you're spot-on. By the way, I can see you've done a lot of background reading on global trade. Have you taken any related courses?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：我认为你说得很对。顺便说一句，我看得出你对全球贸易做了很多背景阅读。你上过相关课程吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, I took one last term. It was really informative. And I even finished a book on global marketing afterwards.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：是的，我上学期上了一门。真的很有信息量。之后我甚至读完了一本关于全球营销的书。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: Excellent. If you want to build on that, I'd suggest studying global management next. It'll give you deeper insights into how international businesses actually operate.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：很好。如果你想在此基础上继续深入学习，我建议下一步学习全球管理。它会让你更深入地了解国际企业的实际运作方式。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds useful. I'll definitely think about it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：听起来很有用。我一定会考虑的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, about those companies I asked you to research last week---what did you find?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：现在，关于我上周让你们研究的那些公司——你发现了什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, their strategies are quite different. Take Drayman's, the medical company. They shifted their headquarters to a new city last year to take advantage of tax incentives.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：嗯，它们的策略相当不同。以医疗公司Drayman's为例。他们去年将总部迁到了一个新城市，以利用税收优惠。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's true. And since the move, their business has grown steadily. So the decision clearly worked. How about Multiplan?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：是的。搬迁后，他们的业务稳步增长。所以这个决定显然奏效了。Multiplan呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: At first they grew rapidly, but then they pushed ahead with a global expansion before really establishing themselves at home. I thought that was a bit premature.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：起初他们增长迅速，但后来在国内尚未站稳脚跟就推进了全球扩张。我认为那有点操之过急。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: I agree. Companies need to secure their domestic base first. And Elbies?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：我同意。公司需要先稳固国内市场。Elbies呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: They're very effective at negotiating prices with distributors, which cuts costs dramatically and boosts profit margins. That strategy is paying off for them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：他们在与分销商谈判价格方面非常有效，这大幅降低了成本并提高了利润率。这一策略正在为他们带来回报。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: Nicely observed. And Grandview, the hotel chain?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：观察得很好。那连锁酒店Grandview呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: Their performance last year was pretty sluggish. But towards the end of the year, they started recruiting more experienced staff. That could bring about positive changes soon.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：他们去年的表现相当疲软。但在年底，他们开始招聘更有经验的员工。那可能很快就会带来积极的变化。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely. Having skilled employees is crucial. Lastly, Emerson, the printer company?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：绝对。拥有熟练员工至关重要。最后是打印机公司Emerson呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Zoey
transcriptSentences.englishText: They've improved product quality by managing their supply chain more efficiently. Overall, I think all these companies provide great lessons for smaller businesses facing similar challenges.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 佐伊：他们通过更高效地管理供应链提高了产品质量。总的来说，我认为所有这些公司都为面临类似挑战的小企业提供了很好的经验教训。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Mahoney
transcriptSentences.englishText: Exactly. That's why I wanted you to look at these cases. I'm glad you've taken away the key points.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 马奥尼博士：正是。这就是我想让你们研究这些案例的原因。很高兴你掌握了关键要点。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good afternoon, everyone. In our previous lectures, we've been examining prehistoric civilisations in Europe. Today, however, I would like to switch over to Asia, and focus on the earliest recognised period of Japanese history- the Jomon period. This was a civilisation that goes back around 15,000 years, and it was far more sophisticated than one might expect.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家下午好。在之前的讲座中，我们一直在研究欧洲的史前文明。然而，今天我想转向亚洲，聚焦于日本历史上最早被认可的时期——绳文时代。这是一个大约可以追溯到15，000年前的文明，它比人们可能想象的要复杂得多。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, the term 'Jomon' literally translates as 'cord-marked' in Japanese. It derives from the rope-like patterns you see decorating their pottery. The Jomon period is considered a crucial stage in Japan's late Stone Age. Most scholars agree it spanned from approximately 12000 BCE to 300 BCE, bridging the Palaeolithic and Neolithic ages. In other words, it represents a culture that endured for more than 10,000 years---one of the longest continuous prehistoric traditions anywhere in the world.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：现在，“绳文”一词在日语中字面意思是“绳纹式的”。它来源于你在他们陶器上看到的绳状图案装饰。绳文时代被认为是日本石器时代晚期的一个关键阶段。大多数学者认为它大约跨越了公元前12000年到公元前300年，连接了旧石器时代和新石器时代。换句话说，它代表了一种持续了10，000多年的文化——是世界上最长的持续史前传统之一。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, where did the Jomon people come from? Well, the question remains debated. But one common idea is that, during the Ice Age, sea levels were considerably lower, and there was a land bridge connecting the Japanese islands to mainland Asia. People are thought to have crossed over while tracking the large animals they were hunting. Subsequently, when the ice melted and the seas rose again, Japan became isolated, and those groups evolved into its first permanent settlers.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：那么，绳文人来自哪里？嗯，这个问题仍在争论中。但一个普遍的观点是，在冰河时期，海平面相当低，有一座陆桥连接日本列岛和亚洲大陆。人们被认为是在追踪他们狩猎的大型动物时越过陆桥的。随后，当冰层融化、海平面再次上升时，日本变得孤立，这些群体演变成了它的第一批永久定居者。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The start of the Jomon period coincided with the end of the Ice Age. As the climate warmed up, evaporation accelerated, forests expanded rapidly, and more plant and animal species appeared. This gave people a much wider choice of food, which in turn had a profound influence on their way of life.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：绳文时代的开始恰逢冰河时代的结束。随着气候变暖，蒸发加快，森林迅速扩大，更多的动植物物种出现。这给了人们更广泛的食物选择，这反过来对他们的生活方式产生了深远的影响。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: From excavations of shell mounds, we know the Jomon people lived off a mix of seafood, hunting, and plant gathering. They had a particular preference for shellfish and nuts. What's interesting is that plant gathering actually played a greater role than fishing or hunting. That shows how attuned they were to their environment---they used resources very efficiently and in a sustainable way. Because they were such skilled hunters, gatherers and fishers, they had little immediate need to develop farming at this stage. For plant collection, they used knives and axes; for fishing, they had hooks, harpoons, and nets; and for hunting, they employed arrows. Some of these tools even served multiple purposes for example, they could be used both for getting food and for protecting clans against wild animals. That tells us their survival strategies were in fact highly advanced.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：从贝冢的发掘中，我们知道绳文人以海鲜、狩猎和植物采集为生。他们特别喜欢贝类和坚果。有趣的是，植物采集实际上比捕鱼或狩猎发挥了更大的作用。这表明他们与环境是多么协调——他们非常高效且可持续地利用资源。因为他们是非常熟练的猎人、采集者和渔夫，他们在这一阶段几乎没有发展农业的迫切需要。植物采集使用刀和斧头；捕鱼使用鱼钩、鱼叉和渔网；狩猎使用箭。其中一些工具甚至有多种用途——例如，它们既可以用于获取食物，也可以用于保护部落免受野生动物侵害。这告诉我们他们的生存策略实际上非常先进。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Another major innovation of the Jomon people was the production of pottery---which is one of the reasons this era is so renowned. Pottery changed their diet because they could cook food in different ways, like boiling, drying, or smoking. And this led to a fundamental lifestyle change: instead of moving around all the time, they started to settle down. They built round villages, typically accommodating about 50 inhabitants, mostly in southwestern Honshu where the climate was best suited to their way of life.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：绳文人的另一项重大创新是陶器的生产——这也是这个时代如此著名的原因之一。陶器改变了他们的饮食，因为他们可以用不同的方式烹饪食物，如煮、晒干或熏制。这导致了根本性的生活方式改变：他们不再四处迁徙，而是开始定居下来。他们建造圆形村庄，通常容纳大约50名居民，主要在本州西南部，那里的气候最适合他们的生活方式。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Unlike many early human societies that lived in caves, the Jomon built pit dwellings dug several feet into the ground. Inside, they set up hearths made of stones, usually with several holes. Archaeologists believe that some of these were used as stoves, while others functioned as storage pits or cooking facilities.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：与许多住在洞穴里的早期人类社会不同，绳文人建造了深入地下几英尺的竖穴式住宅。在里面，他们用石头搭建炉床，通常有几个洞。考古学家认为，其中一些用作炉灶，而另一些用作储存坑或烹饪设施。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: During the early and middle Jomon periods, the population increased significantly, as demonstrated by large-scale excavations. The climate back then was warmer than it is today, which made it easier for communities to grow. This population boom illustrates not only human adaptability but also the increasing social organisation of communities. And some elements of Japanese culture like traditional marriage rituals may indeed trace their origins back to this period.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在绳文时代早期和中期，人口显著增加，正如大规模发掘所证明的那样。那时的气候比今天温暖，这使得社区更容易发展。这一人口激增不仅说明了人类的适应性，也说明了社区社会组织的发展。日本文化的一些元素，如传统婚姻仪式，可能确实可以追溯到这一时期。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: In the later Jomon period, there were signs of the very beginnings of farming. Although modest in scale, this development was still important, as it laid the groundwork for the Yayoi period, which followed from about 300 BCE to 300 CE. During the Yayoi, rice cultivation became the economic mainstay, and agriculture spurred the emergence of city-states and the earliest forms of government.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在绳文时代后期，出现了农耕开始的迹象。虽然规模不大，但这一发展仍然很重要，因为它为弥生时代奠定了基础，弥生时代大约从公元前300年持续到公元300年。在弥生时代，水稻种植成为经济支柱，农业促进了城邦和最早政府形式的出现。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: By the end of the Jomon period, though, the climate cooled once more. Food became scarce, populations shrank in some areas, and communities grew increasingly isolated. That basically brought the era to a close. But even so, its legacy continued to shape Japan's cultural and historical trajectory for centuries to come.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：然而，到了绳文时代末期，气候再次变冷。食物变得稀缺，一些地区的人口减少，社区变得越来越孤立。这基本上结束了这个时代。但即便如此，它的遗产在接下来的几个世纪里继续塑造着日本的文化和历史轨迹。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello, HomeEase Rental Agency, Posy speaking. How can I help you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：您好，HomeEase租赁公司，我是波西。能为您效劳吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, hello, my name's Dario and I'm ringing about the flat you've got advertised. Is it still available?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：哦，你好，我叫达里奥，我打电话来问你们广告上的那套公寓。还空着吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, it is. Can I just ask---how did you hear about it? From a friend, or did you see it advertised somewhere?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：是的，还空着。我能问一下——您是怎么听说的？从朋友那里，还是在哪里看到广告的？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: I actually spotted it in the newspaper.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：我其实是在报纸上看到的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right, I see. So, what would you like to know?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：好的，明白了。那您想了解什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I'll be sharing with a friend. We're finishing university soon and need somewhere new fairly quickly. Could you give me a few more details?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：嗯，我会和一个朋友合租。我们很快就要大学毕业了，需要尽快找个新住处。您能给我更多细节吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course. The landlord's name's Mary. It's a two-bedroom flat, and it'll be ready from the first of next month.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：当然。房东叫玛丽。这是一套两居室公寓，下个月一号就可以入住。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: Next month---that's 1 June, isn't it?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：下个月——那是6月1日，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's right. Will that work for you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：没错。您方便吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, that's fine.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：好的，没问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Lovely. The rent is $13,000 this year---up from $11,000 last year---because Mary had it refurbished a few months back. She repainted the walls, put in new kitchen units, things like that.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：好的。今年的租金是13，000美元——比去年的11，000美元涨了——因为玛丽几个月前对房子进行了翻新。她重新粉刷了墙壁，安装了新的厨柜之类的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: A bit steep, but still within budget. What else did she change?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：有点高，但还在预算内。她还改了些什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: She added modern lighting and new carpets. And the floors used to be marble, but now they're wood, which makes the place feel warmer and cosier. All the upgrades were done to improve the tenants' quality of life.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：她增加了现代照明和新地毯。地板以前是大理石的，现在是木头的，让房子感觉更温暖舒适。所有升级都是为了改善租户的生活质量。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sounds good. What about appliances?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：听起来不错。家电呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: She thought about fitting a dishwasher, but there wasn't enough space in the kitchen. Still, you've got all the basics---air conditioning, a fridge, and a microwave.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：她考虑过安装洗碗机，但厨房空间不够。不过，基本家电都有——空调、冰箱和微波炉。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great. And for laundry?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：太好了。那洗衣服呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: There's a shared washing machine in the laundry room on the first floor. You'll need a card to use it, but it's open to all residents and the staff clean it regularly.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：一楼洗衣房有一台共用洗衣机。需要用卡才能用，但所有住户都可以用，工作人员会定期清洁。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's fine. Oh, and does the kitchen have a cooker? I really like cooking from scratch.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：那没问题。哦，厨房有炉灶吗？我真的很喜欢从零开始做饭。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, there's an induction hob. Mary actually suggests using it out on the balcony---you can get some fresh air while you cook.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：有的，有一个电磁炉。玛丽实际上建议在阳台上用——做饭的时候可以呼吸新鲜空气。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: Ha, nice idea!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：哈，好主意！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: By the way, I'm really into cycling. Is there anywhere to park bikes?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：顺便问一下，我很喜欢骑自行车。有地方停自行车吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: There isn't a dedicated room for them, but there are racks just outside the main entrance, so it's quite handy.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：没有专门的房间，但正门外有车架，所以很方便。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good to know. And what about CCTV?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：知道了。那有监控摄像头吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hmm, I'm not sure about that---I'll need to check with Mary. What I do know is there are security guards on duty round the clock, patrolling the building and grounds.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：嗯，我不太确定——我需要和玛丽确认。我知道的是有保安24小时值班，在大楼和场地巡逻。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's reassuring. Are there any other facilities I should know about?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：那让人放心。还有其他设施我应该知道的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Let me think... Oh yes, there's a brand-new gym on the first floor. It's got basic kit and even a swimming pool. They're offering free swimming lessons at the moment, which is a nice bonus.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：让我想想……哦对了，一楼有一个全新的健身房。有基本的器材，甚至还有一个游泳池。他们目前正在提供免费游泳课，这是个不错的额外福利。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's brilliant! Can I arrange a viewing?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：太棒了！我能安排看房吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely. The landlord's free next Monday, if that works for you.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：当然可以。房东下周一有空，如果您方便的话。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: Let me check... the 19th? Yeah, I can make it that evening.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：让我看看……19号？好的，我那天晚上可以。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Perfect. What time? She needs to head off by 8.30 at the latest.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：完美。什么时间？她最晚8：30要离开。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: How about 7.40? It'll take me a while to get there from university.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：7：40怎么样？从大学过去要花点时间。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure, that's fine.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：好的，没问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: And where exactly should we meet?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：那具体在哪里见面？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: At the flat itself. The address is 236 Kerridge Road---that's K-E double R-I-D-G-E. I'll meet you at the main entrance. The building's easy to spot---it's a modern five-storey block with a glass frontage.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：就在公寓本身。地址是克里奇路236号——拼写是K-E-双写R-I-D-G-E。我在正门等你。这栋楼很容易找到——是一栋现代的玻璃面五层楼。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: Got it. Last thing---how do I get there from the bus station?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：明白了。最后一个问题——从公交车站怎么去那里？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Just take the bus to the stop with the same name as the road. Get off on the west side of the junction. You'll see a big red-brick multi-storey building---that's the library. Keep walking straight on and you'll pass a park on your right. The flat's directly opposite it, so you can't miss the building.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：坐公交车到与这条路同名的车站。在交叉路口西侧下车。你会看到一栋红砖多层建筑——那是图书馆。一直往前走，你会经过右手边的一个公园。公寓就在公园正对面，所以你不会错过那栋楼。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dario
transcriptSentences.englishText: Perfect. Thanks a lot for your help!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 达里奥：太好了。非常感谢您的帮助！

transcriptSentences.speaker: Posy
transcriptSentences.englishText: Not at all. Take care see you soon!
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 波西：不客气。保重，很快见！

A. roughly two centuries ago,

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hi everyone, welcome to Urupukapuka Island! It's a stunning spot, full of fascinating nature and history, and I'm sure you'll love it here. My name's Stellan Colby, and I'll be your guide today. Before we set off, let me give you some quick background about the island, along with a few tips for your visit.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家好，欢迎来到乌鲁普卡普卡岛！这是一个令人惊叹的地方，充满了迷人的自然和历史，我相信你们会喜欢这里的。我叫斯特兰·科尔比，今天由我做你们的导游。在我们出发之前，让我给你们一些关于这个岛的基本背景，以及一些参观小贴士。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, first things first. Urupukapuka is actually the largest of the 140 islands that make up the Bay of Islands. Both the Maori and later European settlers lived here. The Maori were the first people to arrive, long before Europeans turned up about 200 years ago. Back then, there were around 2,000 Maori living on the island. Archaeological evidence suggests they probably settled here about 1,000 years ago, and the remains they left behind give us lots of insight into their daily lives.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：首先，乌鲁普卡普卡实际上是构成岛屿湾的140个岛屿中最大的一个。毛利人和后来的欧洲定居者都曾在这里居住。毛利人是第一批到达的人，远早于大约200年前欧洲人的出现。那时，岛上大约有2，000名毛利人居住。考古证据表明，他们大概在1，000年前在这里定居，他们留下的遗迹让我们对他们的日常生活有了很多了解。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, what did they live on? Well, most of their food came from the waters around the island---which were, and still are, teeming with fish. They did try to grow potatoes, but the soil here isn't nearly as fertile as it is on the mainland. Another major difficulty was the lack of trees, which made it hard to build houses and canoes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：那么，他们以什么为生？嗯，他们的大部分食物来自岛屿周围的水域——那里过去和现在都盛产鱼类。他们确实尝试过种植土豆，但这里的土壤远不如大陆肥沃。另一个主要困难是缺乏树木，这使得建造房屋和独木舟变得困难。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The island also holds great cultural and spiritual significance for the Maori, so please be respectful, especially around archaeological sites. Feel free to take photos---no problem at all. Some people think you should keep your voice down or remain silent, but honestly, that's not necessary. Just remember: eating or drinking at sacred sites is not allowed. Elsewhere on the island, though, you're welcome to enjoy your snacks and drinks.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：该岛对毛利人还具有重要的文化和精神意义，所以请保持尊重，尤其是在考古遗址周围。随意拍照——完全没问题。有些人认为你应该压低声音或保持沉默，但说实话，这没有必要。只要记住：在神圣场所不允许吃喝。不过，在岛上的其他地方，你可以享用零食和饮料。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: One more important reminder: do keep an eye on the time. Once the last ferry has gone, there's no other way off the island. Normally the last one leaves at six pm, but as today's a public holiday the six o'clock service won't be running. The very last ferry is at five pm sharp, so please make sure you're at the wharf by 4.50 at the latest.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：还有一个重要提醒：注意时间。一旦最后一班渡轮离开，就没有其他方式离开岛屿了。通常最后一班是下午6点出发，但今天是公共假日，6点的班次不运行。最后一班渡轮是下午5点整，所以请确保最迟在4：50到达码头。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Alright, let's talk about the highlights you can explore here. Take out your map---we're right at the bottom, at the wharf where the ferry dropped us off.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：好的，让我们谈谈你们可以在这里探索的亮点。拿出你们的地图——我们就在最底部，渡轮送我们到达的码头。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: The first stop is the hill fortress. Before Europeans came, Maori tribes often fought one another, so they built fortresses in strong positions---usually on hilltops or along ridgelines. Many of these were very cleverly designed and are really worth seeing. To get there, head straight from the wharf, take the second path on the right, follow the track behind Puka Bay, and the fortress is right at the tip of the headland.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：第一站是山丘要塞。在欧洲人到来之前，毛利部落经常互相争斗，所以他们在地势险要的地方建造要塞——通常在山顶或山脊线上。其中许多设计非常巧妙，真的很值得一看。到达那里：从码头直走，在第二个路口走右边的小路，沿着普卡湾后面的小径走，要塞就在海角的顶端。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Another must-see is the Maori village. It shows how the Maori lived and gives you a real sense of their daily life. From the wharf, follow the path to the shelter, go past the lookout on your right, and the village is just a bit further on the left.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：另一个必看之处是毛利人村庄。它展示了毛利人的生活方式，让你真正感受到他们的日常生活。从码头出发，沿着小路走到庇护所，经过右边的观景台，村庄就在左边稍远一点的地方。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: If you'd rather not walk too far, have a look at the food storage pits. They're like cellars that kept food cool. From the wharf, turn left down to Paradise Bay, then turn left again along the beach path the pits are very close by.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：如果你不想走太远，可以看看食物储存坑。它们就像地窖，用来保持食物凉爽。从码头出发，左转下到天堂湾，然后沿海滩小路再次左转——储存坑就在很近的地方。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: For those happy to walk a bit more, the garden terraces are fantastic. Just keep going past the shelter, then turn right at the first intersection. The terraces also give you a wonderful panoramic view of Palm Bay.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：对于那些愿意多走一点的人，花园梯田很壮观。只要走过庇护所，然后在第一个十字路口右转。梯田还能让你欣赏到棕榈湾的精彩全景。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Families with children often enjoy the gun diggers' pits, though they are a bit further away. From the wharf, turn left, then turn right at the first intersection and keep straight on. Don't turn left to Indigo Bay---just carry on, and you'll find them on the northern cliffs.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：带孩子的家庭通常喜欢炮坑，虽然它们有点远。从码头出发，左转，然后在第一个十字路口右转并直走。不要左转去靛蓝湾——继续走，你会在北部悬崖上找到它们。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: And finally, the meeting house. It's really close by---just walk up to the shelter, turn left, and it's right there in front of you. The Maori used it for all sorts of gatherings celebrations, funerals, and other important events.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：最后是集会屋。它真的很近——走到庇护所，左转，它就在你面前。毛利人用它来举行各种集会——庆祝活动、葬礼和其他重要活动。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Okay, that's the overview of the island's main sites. If you've got any questions, just ask---I'm here to help...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：好了，这就是岛上主要景点的概述。如果你们有任何问题，尽管问——我随时帮助……

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hi, Camille. How's it all going?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：嗨，卡米尔。一切都好吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh, hi, Sebastian. Honestly, I'm feeling a bit stressed at the moment, so I'm really glad you're here. I need to talk to you about my upcoming teaching placement. It's my very first one, and I don't quite know what to expect. Plus, it's going to be assessed as part of my degree.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：哦，嗨，塞巴斯蒂安。老实说，我现在有点压力，所以真的很高兴你在这里。我需要和你谈谈我即将到来的教学实习。这是我的第一次，我不太清楚会是什么情况。而且，它将被评估，算作我学位的一部分。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm sure you'll do brilliantly. You'll be paired with an experienced teacher for mentoring, and they'll give you ongoing guidance and support throughout. Is there anything in particular you're worried about?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：我相信你会做得很出色的。你会和一位有经验的老师配对接受指导，他们会在整个过程中给予你持续的指导和支持。有什么特别担心的事吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, it just feels like I have too much on my plate. I've got assignments from my university tutor, lesson plans to put together, and I also have to sit in on other teachers' lessons. It's a lot to juggle. That said, the practical side doesn't really worry me. I've done some volunteering before with students, so I feel confident about classroom management. And I'm pretty sociable and generally get on well with people so that's not a major concern either.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：是的，就是感觉我手头的事情太多了。我有大学导师布置的作业，要准备教案，还必须旁听其他老师的课。要兼顾的事情太多了。不过，实践方面我其实不担心。我以前和学生一起做过一些志愿者工作，所以我对课堂管理有信心。我也很善于社交，通常和人相处得很好，所以那也不是主要问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: I get that. I had exactly the same worries during my first placement, but it all worked out fine.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：我理解。我第一次实习时也有完全相同的担忧，但一切都很顺利。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's reassuring! I knew you'd be the best person to ask. So, what should I be preparing now? Should I start drafting detailed lesson plans?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：那让人放心！我就知道问你是最好的。那么，我现在应该准备什么？我应该开始起草详细的教案吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: I wouldn't go that far. And I definitely wouldn't waste time trying to research the students beforehand---you'll have plenty of chances to get to know them once you're there. What I would do is check the dress code. It's worth finding out in advance, because expectations can vary a lot from one school to another.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：我不会做到那一步。而且我绝对不会浪费时间事先研究学生——你到了那里会有很多机会了解他们。我会做的是检查着装要求。提前弄清楚是值得的，因为不同学校的期望可能有很大差异。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good point---I'll do that. During the placement, my supervisor will observe my lessons and give feedback afterwards. How should I approach those feedback sessions? Should I raise any issues I'm having with the students?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：说得好——我会的。在实习期间，我的导师会观察我的课，并在之后给予反馈。我应该如何对待这些反馈会议？我应该提出我在学生方面遇到的任何问题吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: Not really. Your supervisor already knows all about the students and the challenges they face. The whole purpose of those sessions is to focus on your teaching.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：不太需要。你的导师已经了解学生和他们面临的挑战。那些会议的全部目的是聚焦于你的教学。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right. So, should I point out the parts of the lesson I thought went well, to make sure the supervisor notices them?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：好的。那么，我应该指出我认为课上得好的部分，以确保导师注意到它们吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: If you did something particularly effective, your supervisor will probably pick up on it. The best thing you can do is use the opportunity to get advice on how to improve.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：如果你做了特别有效的事情，你的导师可能会注意到。你能做的最好的事情是利用这个机会获得关于如何改进的建议。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: Okay, that's clear. I really want to do well in my first placement. What should I be prioritising?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：好的，清楚了。我真的很想在第一次实习中做好。我应该优先考虑什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: The focus changes with each placement. For example, in the final one, you'll need to show how you can put theory into practice. But the first placement is more about getting a sense of what a teacher actually does, both inside and outside the classroom. Later placements are more about refining your teaching skills.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：每次实习的重点都不同。例如，在最后一次实习中，你需要展示如何将理论付诸实践。但第一次实习更多是了解教师实际做什么，无论是在课堂内还是课堂外。之后的实习更多是完善你的教学技能。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's helpful. I also wonder who I should turn to if I run into problems. If the issue is with my supervisor, I'm not sure I could raise it directly with them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：那有帮助。我也想知道如果遇到问题我应该找谁。如果问题出在我的导师身上，我不确定我能否直接向他们提出。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: Actually, your supervisor should always be your first port of call if you have a problem. They're the best person to help. You should only go to your university tutor as a last resort.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：实际上，如果你有问题，你的导师应该是你第一个求助的人。他们是最能帮助你的人。只有在万不得已时才去找你的大学导师。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yeah, that makes sense. And I suppose going straight to the headteacher would be a bad idea---it might make things awkward for my supervisor.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：是的，有道理。我想直接去找校长会是个坏主意——那可能会让我的导师处境尴尬。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: What qualities did your supervisors have that impressed you? I think it would be good to emulate them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：你的导师有哪些品质让你印象深刻？我想效仿他们会是好事。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: Let me think. My first supervisor, Bill Dyson, was excellent. He really cared about his students and always took the time to make sure they understood difficult concepts. If anyone was still struggling, he'd find another way to explain it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：让我想想。我的第一位导师比尔·戴森非常出色。他真的很关心他的学生，总是花时间确保他们理解困难的概念。如果有人还是不懂，他会找另一种方式解释。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's brilliant! What about others?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：太棒了！那其他人呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: They all stood out in their own way. For instance, Heather Moran was fantastic at collaborating with other staff. She was always happy to listen to colleagues and share her insights with them.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：他们每个人都以自己的方式脱颖而出。例如，希瑟·莫兰在与同事合作方面非常出色。她总是乐于倾听同事的意见并分享她的见解。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's so kind of her! I really hope I get someone who can patiently help me get started.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：她真好！我真的希望能遇到一个能耐心帮助我起步的人。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm sure you will. Another supervisor I had, Dan Shaw, taught me a lot about classroom management. He was approachable but firm, making it clear from day one who was in charge, and setting out the rules.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：我相信你会遇到的。我的另一位导师丹·肖教了我很多关于课堂管理的东西。他平易近人但很坚定，从第一天起就明确谁说了算，并制定了规则。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: I've always admired teachers like that.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：我一直很钦佩那样的老师。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: Same here. Dawn Edwards, who supervised me last year, had exceptional professional self-awareness.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：我也是。去年指导我的道恩·爱德华兹有非凡的专业自我意识。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: Do you mean she knew a lot about various subjects?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：你是说她了解很多不同学科？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: No---I mean she could immediately recognise what hadn't gone well in a lesson, and she had a very clear sense of what she needed to work on.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：不——我是说她能立即意识到一堂课中哪里做得不好，而且她对自己需要改进的地方有非常清晰的认识。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: I really value that kind of self-reflection---it's such an important quality.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：我真的很看重那种自我反思——这是非常重要的品质。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Sebastian
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely. My most recent supervisor, Elliot Smith, had a really creative approach to teaching. He used stories, games, and other engaging methods to make even the driest material lively and imaginative.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 塞巴斯蒂安：绝对。我最近的导师埃利奥特·史密斯有一种非常有创意的教学方法。他用故事、游戏和其他吸引人的方法，让即使是最枯燥的材料也变得生动有趣、富有想象力。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Camille
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds really effective! I bet the students loved it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 卡米尔：听起来真的很有效！我敢打赌学生们很喜欢。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning, everyone. Today, we'll continue our lecture series on recycling, with a particular focus on scrap metal -that is, pieces of metal that have been discarded and are no longer of use.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家早上好。今天，我们将继续我们的回收利用系列讲座，特别关注废金属——即那些被丢弃、不再有用的金属碎片。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Contrary to popular belief, recycling is far from a modern invention. In fact, it has been practised in various forms for centuries. For example, the ancient Greeks and Romans collected scrap metal such as copper and bronze to cast statues. In these societies, scrap metal was highly valued and put to a variety of uses, ensuring that nothing went to waste.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：与普遍看法相反，回收利用远非现代发明。事实上，它以各种形式被实践了几个世纪。例如，古希腊人和古罗马人收集废金属，如铜和青铜，来铸造雕像。在这些社会中，废金属被高度重视，并被用于各种用途，确保没有任何东西被浪费。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Over time, scrap metal recycling has grown into a major global industry. In some countries, it has even become an important export sector. Take the US, for instance, where the scrap metal trade dates back to the 19th century, a period of rapid urbanisation. Metal dealers spotted an opportunity to profit from abandoned machinery and tools left on farms as families moved from rural areas to cities. Today, some of these early dealers have expanded into multinational corporations, supplying metal to buyers around the world.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：随着时间的推移，废金属回收已发展成为一个重要的全球产业。在一些国家，它甚至已成为重要的出口部门。以美国为例，废金属贸易可以追溯到19世纪，那是一个快速城市化的时期。随着家庭从农村地区迁往城市，金属经销商发现了从农场废弃的机械和工具中获利的机会。今天，其中一些早期经销商已发展为跨国公司，向世界各地的买家供应金属。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: But why is scrap metal so essential today? One key factor is the ongoing positive evolution within the economy of many nations. As incomes rise, so too does the demand for consumer goods many of which require metal in their production. From household appliances to vehicles and construction materials, metal is integral to modern life.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：但为什么废金属在今天如此重要？一个关键因素是许多国家经济持续的积极发展。随着收入增加，对消费品的需求也随之增加，其中许多产品的生产需要金属。从家用电器到车辆和建筑材料，金属是现代生活不可或缺的一部分。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Another driver of demand for recycled metals concerns specific types of metal, such as copper. Although copper is still relatively abundant, its quality has declined in recent years. This makes recycling copper especially attractive, as it helps maintain the high standards required for industrial and technological applications.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：对回收金属需求的另一个驱动因素涉及特定类型的金属，如铜。虽然铜仍然相对丰富，但其质量近年来有所下降。这使得回收铜特别有吸引力，因为它有助于维持工业和技术应用所需的高标准。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Furthermore, a rapidly expanding sector has significantly increased the demand for scrap metal---some of you might have guessed it---the electronics sector. Consider how many devices you've replaced in recent years smartphones, laptops, tablets, and more. What happens to the old ones? Unfortunately, many are simply discarded, ending up in landfills, with their metal components wasted. Recycling these materials not only conserves resources, but it also reduces the environmental impact associated with mining and pollution.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：此外，一个快速扩张的领域显著增加了对废金属的需求——你们有些人可能已经猜到了——电子行业。想想你们近年来更换了多少设备——智能手机、笔记本电脑、平板电脑等等。旧设备会怎样？不幸的是，许多只是被丢弃，最终进入垃圾填埋场，其金属部件被浪费。回收这些材料不仅节约资源，还减少了与采矿和污染相关的环境影响。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Given the high demand for recycled metals, where are researchers and engineers seeking new sources? One promising area is roadways. In the UK, for instance, vehicles release tiny traces of platinum that accumulate over time. Interestingly, certain plants growing along roadsides can absorb metals from the soil efficiently, presenting a potential source for recovery.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：鉴于对回收金属的高需求，研究人员和工程师正在哪里寻找新的来源？一个有前景的领域是道路。例如，在英国，车辆会释放出微量的铂，随着时间的推移而积累。有趣的是，沿路边生长的某些植物可以有效地从土壤中吸收金属，这提供了一个潜在的回收来源。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sweden is another country making significant strides in this area. As it was historically a major cotton producer, researchers there are examining old cotton factories that have been closed down. These abandoned sites contain substantial amounts of metal embedded in walls and floors, which can be melted down and reused.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：瑞典是该领域取得重大进展的另一个国家。由于历史上是主要的棉花生产国，那里的研究人员正在检查已关闭的旧棉纺织厂。这些废弃的厂址在墙壁和地板中含有大量金属，可以熔化和再利用。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: In addition, beneath many Swedish cities lie outdated pipes that once supplied gas to local neighbourhoods. Although no longer in use, they represent another valuable source of scrap metal. The challenge, however, is to extract the metal without causing major disruption to surrounding areas---particularly local residents and traffic.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：此外，许多瑞典城市地下埋有曾经为当地社区供气的过时管道。虽然不再使用，但它们是另一个有价值的废金属来源。然而，挑战在于如何在不对周围区域——特别是当地居民和交通——造成重大干扰的情况下提取金属。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Once scrap metal is identified, the next step is extraction and separation. This can be tricky, especially with complex waste such as electronics, which often contain mixtures of metals. However, it is achievable. For example, if you want to separate iron from non-magnetic metals like silver or gold found in old phones or computers, you can use magnetism. As long as the magnet is larger than the components it needs to attract, effective separation is possible.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：一旦确定了废金属，下一步就是提取和分离。这可能很棘手，尤其是对于电子垃圾等复杂废物，它们通常含有金属混合物。然而，这是可以做到的。例如，如果你想从旧手机或电脑中的银或金等非磁性金属中分离铁，你可以使用磁力。只要磁铁比它需要吸引的部件大，有效的分离就是可能的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: At the same time, engineers are developing innovative methods to improve metal recovery. In the UK, one researcher is experimenting with bacteria that could potentially help extract precious metals from waste. This technique is still at the trial stage, but if successful, it could revolutionise the recycling process, making it more efficient and environmentally friendly. If you're interested, I can explain the theory behind it in our next lecture...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：与此同时，工程师们正在开发创新方法来提高金属回收率。在英国，一位研究人员正在试验用细菌帮助从废物中提取贵金属。这项技术仍处于试验阶段，但如果成功，它可能彻底改变回收过程，使其更高效、更环保。如果你们感兴趣，我可以在下次讲座中解释其背后的理论……

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Flippedville Country Market, Bryce speaking. How can I help?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：弗利普维尔乡村市场，我是布莱斯。能为您效劳吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hi, Bryce. It's Julianna. I was wondering if we could set up a couple of stalls at your market to sell some of our products.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：嗨，布莱斯。我是朱莉安娜。我想问一下我们能不能在你的市场里设几个摊位卖我们的产品。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course, happy to help. I'll just need a few details first. Could you give me your full name, please?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：当然，很高兴能帮忙。我只需要先了解一些信息。能告诉我您的全名吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure. It's Julianna Baker.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：当然。朱莉安娜·贝克。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Thanks, got that. And what's the name of your business?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：谢谢，记下了。您的店铺叫什么名字？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: It's Sunrise Farm. We only changed it recently from Sunrise Estate, so you might not have heard the new name yet.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：叫日出农场。我们最近才从日出庄园改过来，所以您可能还没听说过新名字。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Ah yes, I remember the old name. So you're based fairly close by, aren't you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：啊是的，我记得旧名字。所以你们的店就在附近吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Exactly, we're only about five kilometres away.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：是的，我们只有大约五公里远。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Brilliant---we love to support local producers. Could I take your contact number?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：太好了——我们喜欢支持本地生产商。能告诉我您的联系电话吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Of course. It's 0407551827.

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right, I've noted that down. Is that your mobile?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：好的，我记下了。是您的手机吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, that's right.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：是的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Great. And could I have your address as well?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：好的。那您的地址呢？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, it's 798 Sycamore Road, Flippedville.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：好的，是弗利普维尔的西卡莫尔路798号。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Perfect, thanks.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：好的，谢谢。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, let's talk about what you'd actually like to sell.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：现在，我们来谈谈您实际想卖什么。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, I've been to the market before and noticed there are already quite a few vegetable stalls, so for our first stall we'd like to sell flowers instead. We'll pick them fresh each morning before coming. We've been growing them for about a year now. We do grow fruit as well, but at the moment it's just for ourselves--- maybe later we'll sell that too.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：嗯，我之前去过市场，注意到已经有几个蔬菜摊位了，所以我们的第一个摊位想卖花。我们会在每天早上来之前采摘新鲜的。我们已经种了大约一年了。我们也种水果，但目前只是自己吃——也许以后也会卖。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Lovely---that'll make a nice addition. I'm sure people will be interested.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：太好了——那会是个不错的补充。我相信人们会感兴趣的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's what we're hoping.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：我们正是希望如此。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: And will you be selling anything else from that stall?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：那你们还会在那个摊位卖其他东西吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Oh yes---my husband's really good at woodwork. He spends most of his spare time on it, and I've finally persuaded him to start selling what he makes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：哦是的——我丈夫很擅长木工。他把大部分空闲时间都花在这上面，我总算说服他开始卖他做的东西了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's great. What sort of things does he make?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：太好了。他做些什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Mainly furniture---all beautifully crafted from locally sourced wood.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：主要是家具——都是用本地木材精美制作的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Excellent. We already have some people selling glassware and ceramics will fit in really well.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：好极了。我们已经有一些人卖玻璃制品和陶瓷了，你们会很好地融入进来。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Glad to hear that. Would it be possible for us to choose where our stall is located?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：很高兴听到这个。我们能选择摊位的位置吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, no problem. The market stretches quite a way---one end's by the town centre, the other's down by the river.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：可以，没问题。市场延伸得很长——一端在镇中心，另一端在河边。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: We'd prefer the river end---it'd be lovely to have the view while we're working.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：我们更喜欢河边那端——工作时能欣赏风景会很惬意。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: It really is a nice spot. Now, what size stall would you like?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：那确实是个好位置。那你们想要多大的摊位？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm not sure. What's the standard size?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：我不太确定。标准尺寸是多少？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: The standard is 3.6 metres wide by 5.4 metres long.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：标准是3.6米宽乘5.4米长。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hmm... that might not be big enough.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：嗯……那可能不够大。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's fine---we also offer a larger one, 7.5 metres long.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：没问题——我们也提供更大的，7.5米长。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds better---we'll take the bigger one.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：听起来好多了——我们要大的那个。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Brilliant, I'll put that down. You did say you wanted more than one stall, didn't you?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：好的，我记下来。您说过想要不止一个摊位，对吧？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, that's right. We also run a small café in town.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：是的。我们在镇上还经营一家小咖啡馆。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: So will the second stall be for coffee?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：那第二个摊位是卖咖啡的？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Actually, we specialise in tea. It's all organic and already quite popular locally.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：实际上，我们专营茶。都是有机的，在当地已经相当受欢迎了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sounds great. Just to let you know, if you're serving food or drinks you'll need a food licence---it's one of the market rules.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：听起来不错。提醒您一下，如果你们供应食品或饮料，需要食品许可证——这是市场规定之一。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: No problem, we've already got one.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：没问题，我们已经有了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Excellent. And will you be selling anything else?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：太好了。那你们还会卖其他东西吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Probably. We've recently started making our own brand of chocolate, so we'll bring along a few varieties to see how they go.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：可能会。我们最近开始制作自己品牌的巧克力了，所以我们会带几种来试试看。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Brilliant idea. Where would you like this stall to be?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：好主意。这个摊位你们想放在哪里？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Near the entrance, if possible---it should get the most footfall.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：如果可能的话，靠近入口——那里人流量应该最大。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's a really popular spot, but I'll see what I can do. Any other requirements?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：那是个很受欢迎的位置，不过我会尽力安排的。还有其他要求吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Julianna
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, we'll need a stall with electricity for our equipment. And we'll bring our own chairs, if that's OK.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 朱莉安娜：是的，我们需要一个有电的摊位来使用设备。我们也会自带椅子，如果可以的话。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Bryce
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely fine. Now, let's move on to...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 布莱斯：完全可以。现在，让我们继续……

transcriptSentences.speaker: Presenter
transcriptSentences.englishText: Hello, everyone! Next week sees the return of our town's annual International Week, an event that's been running for several years now. I'm delighted to be joined today by the organiser of this much-loved celebration, Lowell Moran. Lowell, could you tell us how it all began?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 主持人：大家好！下周我们镇上一年一度的国际周又要回来了，这个活动已经举办好几年了。今天我很高兴请到了这个深受喜爱的庆祝活动的组织者——洛厄尔·莫兰。洛厄尔，你能告诉我们它是怎么开始的吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lowell
transcriptSentences.englishText: Thanks for having me. I'm really pleased to be here. Well, it all started five years ago on a cold February day. I was chatting with a few local businesspeople about what we could do to brighten up August, when the weather's decent and the children are off school until September. Someone suggested that, given how diverse our community is, we ought to hold an international event to celebrate it. The original idea was simply to invite people to share aspects of their home countries, and we all thought it was brilliant. The very first celebration was just a one-day affair, featuring three countries. But it went down a storm---one of the town's biggest newspapers even covered it. The response was incredible---loads of people wanted to get involved. So the following year, despite the higher costs, we stretched it to a full week.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 洛厄尔：谢谢邀请我。我很高兴来到这里。嗯，这一切始于五年前一个寒冷的二月天。我当时和几个当地商人聊天，讨论我们能在八月做点什么让气氛活跃起来——那时天气不错，孩子们也在九月之前不用上学。有人提议，鉴于我们社区的多样性，我们应该举办一个国际活动来庆祝。最初的想法只是邀请人们分享他们祖国的文化元素，我们都觉得这主意很棒。第一次庆祝活动只有一天，展示了三个国家。但它大受欢迎——镇上最大的报纸甚至报道了它。反响非常好——很多人都想参与。所以第二年，尽管成本更高，我们还是把它延长到了一整周。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Presenter
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's quite a progression! So, what form does the event take these days?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 主持人：真是相当大的进展！那么，现在这个活动是什么形式？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lowell
transcriptSentences.englishText: These days, the first six days each spotlight a different country, and then on the final day---weather permitting---we throw a street party near the town hall. There's live music from the local radio station, all sorts of food, and plenty of games. If it rains, as it did last year, we simply move everything to the school gym. That worked perfectly well---everyone still had a great time. Preparations kick off in January, when applications open for groups keen to host a themed day for their country. People don't need to belong to an official cultural group---anyone who identifies with a country can send in a proper plan. The committee chooses the most creative ideas. Funding isn't a big issue at that stage, because we do have access to grants. We also arrange a space for each group to run their activities. Sadly, we can't use the town stadium for the larger outdoor events this year as it's already booked, but the community centre very kindly lets us use its open-air car park instead. Local businesses have been hugely supportive as well. Lots of traders lend us things like tables and amplifiers free of charge for the week, and the committee deals with all the administration. The town library also makes a contribution, by putting on displays of books linked to the countries we're featuring. It gives the whole celebration an extra educational angle.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 洛厄尔：现在，前六天每天聚焦一个不同的国家，然后在最后一天——天气允许的话——我们在市政厅附近举办街头派对。有当地电台的现场音乐、各种食物和很多游戏。如果下雨——就像去年那样——我们就把所有东西搬到学校体育馆。那样效果也很好——大家还是玩得很开心。准备工作在一月开始，届时向有兴趣为他们的国家主办主题日的团体开放申请。人们不必属于官方文化团体——任何认同某个国家的人都可以提交合适的计划。委员会会选择最有创意的想法。在那一阶段资金不是大问题，因为我们确实能获得拨款。我们也会为每个团体安排活动场地。遗憾的是，今年我们不能使用镇体育场举办大型户外活动，因为它已经被预订了，但社区中心很友善地让我们使用他们的露天停车场。当地企业也非常支持。很多商家在一周内免费借给我们桌子和扩音器等东西，委员会处理所有行政事务。镇图书馆也做出了贡献，摆放了与我们展示的国家相关的书籍。这给整个庆祝活动增加了一个额外的教育视角。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Presenter
transcriptSentences.englishText: Lowell, could you tell us what forms these cultural activities usually take during the themed days?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 主持人：洛厄尔，你能告诉我们这些文化活动在主题日通常以什么形式呈现吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lowell
transcriptSentences.englishText: Each country's themed day usually includes something special---maybe a performance, an exhibition, or a demonstration. For example, people might show how to make traditional crafts, or put on a photography exhibition of famous landmarks.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 洛厄尔：每个国家的主题日通常包括一些特别的内容——也许是一场表演、一个展览或一次演示。例如，人们可能会展示如何制作传统手工艺，或者举办著名地标的摄影展。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Presenter
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds fantastic. Can you give us a sneak preview of this year's highlights?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 主持人：听起来很棒。你能给我们提前透露一下今年的亮点吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Lowell
transcriptSentences.englishText: We've got some brilliant events lined up! Monday is Mexico Day, and the group are preparing a show that promises to be as fiery as their famous chilli peppers. Expect plenty of singing, playing songs, and drumming---all of which are bound to get you moving. On Tuesday it's South Africa Day, featuring an exhibition of traditional robes and dresses worn at ceremonies and dances---some of them are said to be worth more than their weight in gold. Wednesday will be Indonesia Day---and that's definitely one for the foodies. Two women will be showing how to prepare iconic Indonesian dishes and sauces. You'll be able to take photos at each stage, so you can recreate them easily at home. Then on Thursday we've got Canada Day. Moving beyond the stereotype of Canadians as only rugged outdoor types, they'll demonstrate how they carve delightful figures of animals from local legends---like birds and bears out of native wood, using just a knife. And Friday will be Italy Day...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 洛厄尔：我们安排了一些精彩的活动！周一是墨西哥日，该团体正在准备一场表演，据说会像他们著名的辣椒一样火热。会有很多唱歌、演奏和击鼓——这些肯定会让你动起来。周二是南非日，将展出在仪式和舞蹈中穿的传统长袍和服饰——据说其中一些价值连城。周三是印度尼西亚日——这绝对是美食爱好者的最爱。两位女士将展示如何制作标志性的印尼菜肴和酱料。你可以在每个阶段拍照，这样你在家也能轻松复制。周四是我们加拿大日。超越加拿大人只属于粗犷户外类型的刻板印象，他们将展示如何用本土木材雕刻当地传说中的动物形象——比如鸟和熊，只用一把刀。周五是意大利日……

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good morning, Jonathan---come in! You emailed me about your presentation. What's the topic again?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：早上好，乔纳森——请进！你给我发了邮件关于你的展示。主题是什么来着？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, Dr Harper. It's for the product development course, but I'm a bit stuck.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：是的，哈珀博士。是关于产品开发课程的，但我有点卡住了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Don't worry. Have you narrowed it down to a particular product?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：别担心。你缩小到某个特定产品了吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: I've decided to focus on a type of mosquito net.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：我决定专注于一种蚊帐。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Really? What made you pick that?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：真的吗？是什么让你选这个的？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: Well, last summer I travelled across Africa with a friend who's studying medicine. We dropped by a medical centre in a region badly affected by malaria. While my friend was talking to a doctor, I got chatting with one of the administrators---and I discovered they've seen far fewer cases of malaria since these nets became widely available. That really grabbed my attention.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：嗯，去年夏天我和一个学医的朋友一起穿越非洲旅行。我们顺便去了一个受疟疾严重影响地区的医疗中心。当我的朋友和医生交谈时，我和一位管理人员聊了起来——我发现自从这些蚊帐广泛使用以来，他们看到的疟疾病例少了很多。这真的引起了我的注意。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Fascinating. But mosquito nets aren't new, are they? I seem to remember they've been used in Japan for centuries.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：有意思。但蚊帐不是新东西吧？我好像记得日本已经用了几个世纪了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's right. In fact, legend has it Cleopatra used one in ancient Egypt---so that might be the earliest record. Later, they were also used in India, though it's possible they were invented there independently. At first, they were made from silk, then cotton, and nowadays they're usually synthetic fibres. The real breakthrough came in the mid-20th century when insecticide-treated nets were developed for the military. The chemical they used back then was DDT---but it turned out to be harmful to people as well as mosquitoes.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：没错。事实上，传说克利奥帕特拉在古埃及用过蚊帐——所以那可能是最早的记录。后来，印度也用过，虽然有可能它们是独立发明的。起初，它们是丝绸做的，然后是棉布，现在通常是合成纤维。真正的突破是在20世纪中期，当时为军方开发了经杀虫剂处理的蚊帐。他们当时使用的化学物质是DDT——但结果发现它对人和蚊子都有害。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: And is that still a problem with modern nets?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：那现代蚊帐还有这个问题吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: Not at all. Thanks to new technology, the chemicals used today are completely safe for humans, even with daily use. They're also odourless. The only drawback is that people have to spray the nets regularly.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：完全没有。由于新技术，如今使用的化学物质对人类完全安全，即使每天使用也没问题。它们也没有气味。唯一的缺点是人们必须定期喷洒蚊帐。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Which must be tricky in remote areas, where supplies aren't easy to get hold of.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：这在偏远地区肯定很麻烦，那里不容易获得补给。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: Exactly.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：正是。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, tell me more about the particular net you're looking at.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：那么，告诉我更多关于你正在研究的特定蚊帐。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: It's called Olyset, developed by a Japanese company. Unlike traditional nets, the insecticide is built into the fibres and released gradually, rather than just sprayed on the surface. The overall amount of chemicals used isn't much different, though.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：它叫Olyset，由一家日本公司开发。与传统蚊帐不同，杀虫剂被嵌入纤维中并逐渐释放，而不是仅仅喷洒在表面。不过，使用的化学物质总量差别不大。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: I see---so no need for constant re-spraying. Does it work against more mosquito species as well?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：我明白了——所以不需要不断重新喷洒。它也能对付更多的蚊子种类吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: That hasn't been fully proven yet. But what we do know is that Olyset nets are tougher and much less likely to tear. They last at least five years, compared with one or two for most other nets.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：这还没有被完全证实。但我们知道的是Olyset蚊帐更结实，更不容易撕裂。它们至少能用五年，而大多数其他蚊帐只能用一两年。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds very promising.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：听起来很有前景。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Now, in your seminar, will you also set it in a wider context?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：那么，在你的研讨课上，你也会把它放在更广泛的背景中吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, I'm planning to present it as a case study in product development. I'll begin with some background and explain why this innovation was necessary.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：是的，我计划把它作为产品开发中的一个案例研究来展示。我会从一些背景开始，解释为什么这项创新是必要的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Such as?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：比如？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'll talk about vector-borne diseases, especially malaria, and why there's such an urgent demand for new solutions. Some of the audience may not realise just how widespread the problem is.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：我会谈谈媒介传播疾病，特别是疟疾，以及为什么对新解决方案有如此迫切的需求。一些听众可能没有意识到这个问题有多普遍。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: That sounds sensible.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：听起来很合理。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: I've pulled together some statistics on global malaria cases each year. I want to show those---the numbers are pretty shocking.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：我收集了一些关于每年全球疟疾病例的统计数据。我想展示那些——数字相当惊人。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Quite right. Malaria is still one of the world's most serious health challenges. If you can also track down figures on the financial cost to affected countries, that would really strengthen your presentation.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：很对。疟疾仍然是世界上最严重的健康挑战之一。如果你也能找到受影响国家经济损失的数据，那会大大增强你的展示。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: Okay, I'll look into that. After that, I'll give a quick overview of the history of mosquito nets before introducing Olyset.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：好的，我会研究一下。在那之后，我会在介绍Olyset之前快速概述蚊帐的历史。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Keep it short and clear. Bullet points on the key features and a simple comparison with older designs would work well.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：保持简短和清晰。关键特征的项目符号和与旧设计的简单比较会效果很好。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: Right, understood. Then I'll explain how Olyset nets are made.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：好的，明白了。然后我会解释Olyset蚊帐是如何制造的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: That's fine.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：那没问题。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: The project's funding mainly comes from government grants and private donors. Do you think I ought to mention that?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：这个项目的资金主要来自政府拨款和私人捐赠。您觉得我应该提到这个吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Absolutely. Funding is a key part of product development---it often determines whether a product is sustainable in the long run. By the way, do you know where the nets are manufactured?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：当然。资金是产品开发的关键部分——它通常决定一个产品是否能长期可持续。顺便问一下，你知道这些蚊帐在哪里生产吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes. Over half are produced by a Tanzanian company called A to Z. They were able to buy specialised machinery with the help of an interest-free loan.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：是的。超过一半是由一家叫A to Z的坦桑尼亚公司生产的。他们在一笔无息贷款的帮助下购买了专门的机器。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good. Try to include a short profile of the company---how many staff they've got, who the main people are in the project, that sort of thing---if you can find it.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：好的。试着包含一个公司的简短介绍——他们有多少员工，项目中主要人物是谁——如果你能找到的话。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: Sure, I'll give that a go. One thing I'm uncertain about is the marketing strategy. I've gathered a lot of information, but I don't know if it fits.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：好的，我会试试。我不确定的一点是营销策略。我收集了很多信息，但不知道是否合适。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'd leave it out. You don't have time for everything, and you've already got plenty. But do make sure you include production figures. Did you check how many nets they make each year?
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：我会把它放一边。你没有时间涵盖所有内容，而且你已经有足够多了。但一定要包括生产数据。你查过他们每年生产多少蚊帐吗？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: Yes, I went through their website. It's over 30 million.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：查过了，我浏览了他们的网站。超过3，000万顶。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Dr Harper
transcriptSentences.englishText: Impressive.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 哈珀博士：惊人。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Jonathan
transcriptSentences.englishText: I'm still not sure how to wrap it all up. Do you think it'd be appropriate to end with the product's future potential?...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 乔纳森：我还是不知道该如何总结。您认为以产品的未来潜力作为结尾合适吗？……

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Good afternoon, everyone. Today I'll be talking about one of the world's most expensive spices---saffron. Often referred to as 'red gold', saffron is obtained from the minute stigmas of the crocus flower. It's prized not just for its vivid colour, distinctive aroma, and unique flavour, but also for its cultural importance, which stretches back over 3,000 years.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：大家下午好。今天我要谈谈世界上最昂贵的香料之一——藏红花。常被称为“红色黄金”的藏红花是从番红花微小的柱头中获取的。它珍贵的不仅仅在于其鲜艳的颜色、独特的香气和特别的味道，还在于其可以追溯到3，000多年前的文化重要性。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: At present, around 70 to 80 per cent of the world's saffron comes from Iran, especially the eastern province of Khorasan, the heartland of cultivation. The region's dry climate, together with big swings between day and night temperatures, provides ideal conditions for the crop. The flowering season is extremely short, and in most places the harvest takes place from mid to late October. The very first blooms of the season are usually the finest. And in terms of yield? The numbers are astonishing: it takes more than 14,000 flowers just to produce 50 grams of top-quality saffron. No wonder it's compared to panning for gold---it's back-breaking work for such a tiny return.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：目前，世界上大约70%到80%的藏红花来自伊朗，特别是东部的呼罗珊省——种植的中心地带。该地区干燥的气候，加上昼夜温差大，为这种作物提供了理想的条件。花期极短，在大多数地方收获期在10月中旬到下旬。季节的第一批花通常是最好的。产量方面呢？数字惊人：需要超过14，000朵花才能生产50克顶级藏红花。难怪它被比作淘金——对于如此微小的回报来说，这是非常辛苦的工作。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: What makes saffron especially valuable is that the stigmas have to be picked entirely by hand. This is slow, labour-intensive work. Once gathered, the best way to keep the quality is to dry them, usually under carefully controlled conditions at low heat. That step is crucial to preserve both flavour and aroma. But there's a catch: if the style isn't separated from the stigma at this stage, it can add up to 50 per cent extra weight, thereby lowering the overall quality. Properly processed saffron should have a gentle sweetness reminiscent of honey, and a rich but not overpowering floral scent.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：藏红花之所以特别珍贵，是因为柱头完全需要手工采摘。这是缓慢、劳动密集的工作。一旦收集，保持品质的最佳方法是干燥它们，通常在精心控制的低温条件下进行。这一步对保持味道和香气至关重要。但有一个问题：如果在这个阶段不将花柱与柱头分离，可能会增加高达50%的额外重量，从而降低整体品质。经过适当加工的藏红花应该有一种温和的甜味，让人想起蜂蜜，以及浓郁但不刺鼻的花香。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Commercially, saffron is available in two principal forms. One is powder, produced by dehydrating and milling the styles, which retains most of the active compounds. The other is whole stigmas---the delicate threads you often see in jars---which are generally pricier. Experts usually advise going for the threads, as they hold their flavour better and deliver a more intense taste. These days, saffron is widely used across the globe, especially in cooking. To give you an example, you can soak three to five saffron threads in warm water---about 80°C---for 10 to 15 minutes. The liquid that results can be poured over rice to enhance both colour and flavour. But you do have to be careful: too much will make food taste bitter. Another option is to stir a few drops of saffron water into warm milk---it makes a delicious, nourishing drink.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在商业上，藏红花有两种主要形式。一种是粉末，通过脱水和研磨花柱制成，保留了大部分活性化合物。另一种是整根柱头——你经常在罐子里看到的精致丝线——通常更贵。专家通常建议购买丝线状，因为它们能更好地保持风味并提供更浓郁的味道。如今，藏红花在全球广泛使用，尤其是在烹饪中。举个例子，你可以将三到五根藏红花丝浸泡在约80°C的温水中10到15分钟。所得的液体可以浇在米饭上以增强颜色和风味。但你必须小心：太多会使食物变苦。另一个选择是将几滴藏红花水搅拌到温牛奶中——它成为一种美味、有营养的饮品。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: Beyond the kitchen, saffron also plays a role in modern medicine. It's rich in natural carotenoids, which help protect the eyes, keeping both the lens and the retina healthy and supporting good vision. To test this, researchers ran controlled experiments on mice. The findings showed that saffron reduced vision damage when the animals were exposed to intense light.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：除了厨房，藏红花在现代医学中也扮演着角色。它富含天然类胡萝卜素，有助于保护眼睛，保持晶状体和视网膜健康，支持良好视力。为了测试这一点，研究人员对小鼠进行了对照实验。研究结果表明，当动物暴露在强光下时，藏红花减少了视力损伤。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: But saffron's story extends much further back. Let's take a quick look at how it was used historically. The earliest records come from the Minoan civilisation in ancient Greece, around 1500 BCE. Archaeologists have uncovered wall paintings at the Palace of Knossos depicting young women harvesting saffron. Interestingly, it wasn't first used as a spice or medicine, but as a dye for clothes. People there valued it so highly that they even considered it a gift from the gods.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：但藏红花的故事可以追溯得更远。让我们快速看看它在历史上是如何使用的。最早的记录来自古希腊的米诺斯文明，大约在公元前1500年。考古学家在克诺索斯宫殿发现了描绘年轻女性收割藏红花的壁画。有趣的是，它最初不是用作香料或药物，而是用作衣服的染料。那里的人们高度重视它，甚至认为它是神的礼物。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: In ancient Egypt, saffron found even wider applications. It was blended with oils to make cosmetics---things like face creams and lip balms---used by the wealthy to enhance their appearance. People also bathed in saffron-infused water, which acted like a natural perfume. Its fragrance helped disguise unpleasant odours while giving the experience a sense of luxury.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：在古埃及，藏红花有更广泛的应用。它与油混合制成化妆品——如面霜和润唇膏——被富人用来改善外貌。人们还用藏红花浸泡过的水沐浴，这起到了天然香水的作用。它的香味有助于掩盖难闻的气味，同时给体验一种奢华感。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: By the 10th century BCE, in Persia---which we now know as Iran---saffron had taken on fresh purposes. It was used as a natural dye to give carpets a deep red hue that endured for years. Because the dye was entirely natural, these textiles became treasured examples of Persian craftsmanship. And even today, during Nowruz, the Persian New Year, saffron is sprinkled over food to symbolise joy and prosperity---a tradition that links past and present.
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：到公元前10世纪，在波斯——也就是现在的伊朗——藏红花有了新的用途。它被用作天然染料，给地毯一种可以持续多年的深红色调。因为染料完全是天然的，这些纺织品成为波斯工艺的珍贵典范。即使在今天，在诺鲁孜节——波斯新年——期间，藏红花被撒在食物上象征着喜悦和繁荣——这是一种连接过去和现在的传统。

transcriptSentences.speaker: SPEAKER
transcriptSentences.englishText: So, to wrap up: saffron is far more than a spice. It's a golden thread woven through human history, tying together ancient rituals, traditional crafts, and even cutting-edge science...
transcriptSentences.chineseText: 发言人：所以，总结一下：藏红花远不止是一种香料。它是一条贯穿人类历史的金色丝线，将古代仪式、传统工艺，甚至尖端科学联系在一起……
